text:
Immortalis Book 1, Act 2, Scene 2

Scene II: The Pirate’s Rapid Fire

The 2nd Day of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
The Shipwreck Sombre

Allyra awoke in the early hours of the morning to find Nicolas gone. An envelope sat on the pillow next to her with ‘Immoless’ scrawled on it in yellow messy handwriting and a yellow and black plaid seal had been used to close the same envelope. Allyra rolled her eyes and tore it open. Inside she found a buried screwed up parchment that took a few minutes to unravel. 

Once she had stroked out the worst of the creases she read the letter,

‘My Beloved Bride, 

I have been called away on urgent matters that your low intellect could not understand. I appreciate your acceptance of my proposal, and you may select any colour wedding dress that you desire, providing that it is burgundy.

Your ever loving husband,

Nicolas DeSilva, Your Master, Superior and King

P.S. Bigglesworth has dodgy feet, don’t look at them.’

Allyra folded the letter, picked her kleptobag up off the floor, and popped the letter inside. She then dressed quickly and wandered to the deck to watch the two suns decide once again not to rise. She headed directly to the bulwark where she instantly forgot about the suns and took to staring at Sihr. 

Her mind drifted to her daydreams, and she shifted mentally from residing at the palace on Sihr to how she could decorate her ship instead. After careful thought, and Nicolas’s sneaky interference with her brain, Allyra decided that her ship would probably provide more solitude than barging into someone else’s home and demanding that they share it. The necromancer was rumoured not to be a people-person, so she resolved to live aboard her ship and stay away from Elyas. This resolve would not last.

Her reveries were quickly interrupted by the sudden intrusion of a deep voice,
‘You have a woman’s feet!’
Allyra jumped and turned. In the hammock behind her kegs lay Nicolas, or at least she presumed it was Nicolas. He certainly looked like Nicolas, only he was wearing a bizarre purple outfit, a cream-white frilly chemise, a feathered hat, and an eye-patch.

‘I thought you had gone,’ Allyra said at length.
‘Gone, Madam,’ the pirate replied, ‘I only just arrived, so I can’t very well be gone, since I am here. Can you not see me?’
‘I can see that you are here, but I thought you had gone.’ Allyra wondered if everyone in The Deep was insane.
‘Are you feeling quite alright woman?’ Nicolai-Bigglesworth asked.
‘I am quite myself.’
‘Which tells me nothing. Ibliss was once quite himself, and then the writing started and he became herself, whilst being himself for visitors. I think Ibliss is half the reason Nicolas is the way he is!’
Allyra climbed up onto the bulwark and sat down facing the pirate,
‘You’re Nicolas.’

Bigglesworth placed his hands behind his head and swung the hammock from side to side with his body,
‘I am Commodore Nicolas Bigglesworth, but I am not Nicolas.’
‘You just said you are Nicolas,’ Allyra snapped, taking a pre-rolled Ashurrel smoke from her bag and lighting it, ‘Commodore Nicolas Bigglesworth.’

Bigglesworth looked up at the stars,
‘Like I said, I am a Nicolas, not thee Nicolas.’ 
‘Whatever you say, chief,’ Allyra shrugged, ‘I am guessing either you want to engage in some weird role play or there is a carnival in town?’
‘No carnival, except the Dokeshi Carnival, but that was retired years ago. Only the clowns roam its former shadows. Of course you know that. You always sit in there on the big wheel when you’re depressed and want to be alone.’
Allyra exhaled into the sea air,
‘And how do you know that exactly?’ She asked.
Bigglesworth suddenly got quite fidgety and animated. He swung the hammock harder and waved his hands about,
‘We are all very excited, Immoless, so we watch you all the time. Even when you are asleep.’

Allyra caught her breath and glared at Bigglesworth,
‘What do you mean ‘we watch you.’ Who is we?’
‘Nicolas is we. Try to keep up. I should like to see you walk the plank, I often wonder if we could not improve your nautical skills,’ Bigglesworth mused as he sat up and jumped from the hammock.
‘When I said roleplay, that was not quite what I meant,’ Allyra sighed, taking another drag of her smoke. 
‘It’s what I meant.’
‘Is that why you are dressed like that, Nic?’

Bigglesworth marched to Allyra’s side, smiling. Not the sort of pleasant smile one has when meeting a friend, more the smile of a man, or monster, who forced the expression poorly. The smile was all teeth and slightly psychotic eyes.

‘Dressed like what?’ Bigglesworth asked.
‘Dressed like a toadstool-licker,’ Allyra replied. 
‘Toadstool-lickers are the domain of The Pied Piper; my function is nautical.’
‘Of course it is,’ Allyra muttered, then elected to change the subject rather than go around in circles of silliness, ‘Nic?’ She began.
Bigglesworth raised one eyebrow,
‘Commodore!’
‘Commodore, you know how I told you I don’t care for the Electi or the other Immolesses?’
‘No!’ Bigglesworth replied. 

Allyra sighed a sigh of deep annoyance and went to flick her smoke into the sea. Bigglesworth caught her arm,
‘The Necromancer does not like it when you pollute his ocean! We do not like it either.’
‘Fine!’ Allyra nodded, jumping down from the bulwark, dropping her smoke and smothering it with her boot. Bigglesworth growled a deep nasal groan of disapproval.

Allyra tried to free her arm from his grip, but he would not let go.
‘Continue, Immoless!’ The commodore commanded.
‘As I was saying,’ Allya said, shaking her arm to no avail, ‘as much as I have no care for them, I should like to know my sister Immolesses’ current situation.’
Bigglesworth started walking and dragged Allyra by the arm with him,
‘Why does it matter?’
‘It matters,’ Allyra replied desperately trying to resist his pull, and failing, ‘because I want to know when it will be my turn.’
‘Are you afraid of dying?’ Bigglesworth asked as he led her back to her cabin.
‘No. Not dying. I am afraid of not living. You didn’t listen to a word I said last night, did you?’ 
‘I was not here last night, but I can reflect on your words now and find out the situation with your sisters.’ 

Bigglesworth led Allyra, quite forcibly, into her cabin and shoved her onto the bed, releasing his grip. He then sat beside her and his eyes rolled back into his head. His entire body stilled and silenced. Allyra crawled next to him and waved her hand in front of his eyes. There was no response. She waited for five minutes, then tried again, still there was no response. 

For a moment Allyra thought she heard whispering. Bigglesworth’s mouth started moving but no sound came out. The whispering continued like shocks of wind blasting around the cabin.

Feeling a little fed up with The Nicolas Show, which was only just beginning, Allya dropped her kleptobag from her shoulder, pulled out Dr Otto Von Riesigerschwanz’s book, ‘Hit That Bitch!’ and opened it at the bookmarked chapter. She was soon engrossed.

After reading the bookmarked chapter entitled, ‘Women, Whips and Warts,’ Allyra noticed some movement from the pirate as Bigglesworth decided to reboot his brain. His eyes blinked several times, then returned to their normal position,
‘Your sisters…’
‘Yes?’ Allyra asked, closing the book and placing it back in her bag.
‘Stacia is to be collected by Robert, Theaten, in due course, and Lucia…,’ Bigglesworth laughed, ‘I can’t tell you. It’s a surprise. But you will be dispatched soon. You shall go to Corax…’
‘That’s not my plan!’ Allyra exclaimed.

‘You SHALL go to Corax and, hang on, I want to get this right,’ Bigglesworth said, then his eyes wandered back into his own brain again. He returned a lot faster than the first time, ‘They say you will give yourself to Nicolas as our bride, but Webster thinks you will create a massive scene first.’ 
‘Does he now? And who might Webster be?’ Allyra asked surreptitiously.
‘Nicolas.’
‘And what was the whole eye rolling thing about?’
‘We were communicating as you asked,’ Bigglesworth explained in an almost patronising tone.
‘Communicating with who?’
‘Nicolas.’
‘Who was?’ Allyra snapped impatiently.
Bigglesworth lay on the bed,
‘Who was what?’
‘Who was communicating with Nicolas?’
‘Nicolas,’ Bigglesworth replied, patting the sheet next to him, ‘lay here Immoless, under the sheets to keep yourself warm. You seem so cold.’

Allyra shook her head,
‘I’m not cold. So, let me get this straight, you, Nicolas spoke to Nicolas about what I said to Nicolas and were advised by Nicolas to reply but then cautioned by Nicolas that the reply may have inaccuracies and in between you had to check with Nicolas?’
‘Yes, you understand. Good. Lay here, you are cold and wet.’ 
‘I am neither wet, nor cold. Do you always confuse Immolesses on purpose?’ Allyra asked.
‘I waterboard them sometimes. Have you ever been waterboarded?’ 
‘No, and I don’t want to be.’
Bigglesworth rubbed his chin,
‘What if it improved your survival skills?’
‘I don’t think drowning me is going to help me survive, do you?’
Bigglesworth shrugged,
‘Depends on the context. Now come, warm yourself with me.’
‘I told you NO!’ Allyra barked. 

No sooner had Allyra spoken than Bigglesworth grabbed her and threw her over his shoulder. He stormed out of the cabin to the deck and stomped along the plank, with Allyra kicking and shouting, 
‘NO!’ all the way. 
Allyra’s use of THAT word just strengthened Bigglesworth’s resolve.

Allyra stopped shouting when the water came into view and stared down at the furiously frothing sea,
‘What are you doing Nic?’ 
Bigglesworth stopped at the very end of the plank,
‘Testing you, so recommendations maybe made for improvements.’
‘I don’t want to be improved,’ Allyra snapped glaring at the unwelcoming sea, ‘put me down this instant.’
‘As you wish!’ Bigglesworth replied, leaning forward. 
Allyra panicked,
‘No! No! No! No!’
Bigglesworth released his grip and threw her over the side of the ship. Allyra plummeted into the ocean, disappeared under the waves, then returned to the surface, coughing and spluttering as her feet trod water.

‘That is incorrect!’ Bigglesworth bellowed, ‘You will wear yourself out. Float.’
Allyra kicked about some more.
‘Float woman!’ Bigglesworth yelled. 
Allyra trod water harder, flapping her arms like Polly Parrot.
‘Will you relax and float. Relax or drown they’re your options.’ 
Allyra dipped under, then bobbed up again coughing some more. She attempted to swim to the rocks. Bigglesworth shook his head,
‘Don’t swim against the tide, idiot girl, do you think you are as strong and mighty as the ocean? Just float. Keep still. On your back. You usually like being on your back.’

Allyra collected herself, and tried to relax, whilst avoiding the rocks.
‘Feet first!’ Bigglesworth yelled.
Allyra paddled horizontally.
‘Feet, Madam. Feet! You shouldn’t have got in the water with those boots on anyway.’
Allyra swivelled with her hands. Her feet faced the rocks, and she did her best to trust the water to carry her. 

Bigglesworth was satisfied, so satisfied that he held the skull on his cane towards the sea. The water suddenly had a change of heart and swirled around and around engulfing Allyra’s body. 

The swirl deepened as did the suction.

‘EDDY!’ Allyra screamed, ‘GET ME OUT!’ 
Bigglesworth smirked then disappeared.
‘Nicolas! Nicolas!’ Allyra yelled, ‘You asshole.’
Bigglesworth returned, tied a rope to the pole jutting out from the bulwark by the plank and lowered himself down,
‘Swim perpendicular to the edge,’ Bigglesworth yelled.
Allyra flustered and flapped.
‘Woman, swim perpendicular to the edge. I won’t help you unless you help yourself. Punch forward with momentum.’ 
Allyra adjusted her gait and forced herself to follow the instructions. 

The baers had spent five years teaching Allyra advanced swimming skills in the lake at the Twin Lakes, the Kapparu lake and the Kapparu river. They had also taught her to row, sail, climb and hunt. She was used to following instructions, and the baers shouted just as much as Bigglesworth, especially in overzealous white water.

Once free from the eddy, Allyra floated as previously instructed. Bigglesworth dove into the sea, disappeared under the abating eddy and the returning waves, and resurfaced next to the poor woman. 
‘Did you enjoy that?’ He asked.
Allyra raised her middle finger. 

Bigglesworth ignored her insolent gesture, wrapped his arms about her neck and dragged her through the water to the rope.
‘Are you going to carry me up the rope?’ Allyra asked.
‘Certainly not!’ Bigglesworth replied, ‘Pull your own weight, and stop acting like a helpless bint.’
‘Rude,’ Allyra replied.
Bigglesworth released her into the sea,
‘Pirates first,’ he said, before quickly darting up the rope. 

Allyra, who had spent a little too much time in the Sapari bakery, hauled herself up at a somewhat slower rate than Bigglesworth, lurched onto the deck, and collapsed on the boards.

‘We have a few issues that need to be ironed out, don’t we?’ Bigglesworth asked, seating himself on a keg. 
‘Yes, like kicking my father’s butt for not telling me what an idiot you are!’ Allyra snapped, taking off her water-logged boots.
‘We shall start with following orders. When one accidentally puts their life in peril, one must follow the orders of the superior being who knows better.’
‘It was hardly an accident, was it?’ Allyra said, forcing herself to stand.
‘Further,’ Bigglesworth continued, undeterred, ‘we do not wear boots for swimming. I shall make recommendations to Nicolas that your footwear is addressed. Heels make you look like a tart anyway.’
‘Pardon me?’ Allyra frowned.
‘And then we have the issue of your feet. Like I said earlier, you have a woman’s feet.’ 
Allyra slopped over to Bigglesworth and collapsed on the keg next to him,
‘And what sort of feet should I have?’
‘Webbed feet!’ Bigglesworth replied.

Allyra scoffed,
‘Webbed feet. I am supposed to magically have webbed feet so that when a madman throws me into the water I can swim better?’
‘Exactly!’ Bigglesworth smiled, ‘Webbed feet. I shall make that recommendation to Archie.’
‘You don’t have webbed feet,’ Allyra sulked.
‘Au contraire, Madam,’ Bigglesworth replied, removing a boot, ‘I do indeed have webbed feet.’
Before Allyra could argue, Bigglesworth’s gigantic foot slammed on a spare keg. The toes were spread and giant layers of webbed skin rife with blood vessels and a strange layer of green-grey slimy film soaked the extremity’s revolting appearance.

‘Put it away!’ Allyra snapped, grimacing.
Bigglesworth smiled,
‘I shall put in a request for you, and Archie and Demus can do the surgery.’
‘What’s an Archie?’ Allyra asked, then paused before angrily saying, ‘Wait! What bloody surgery? I don’t want frog feet.’
‘You really do need to get out of those clothes,’ Bigglesworth continued, ‘I told you, you are wet and cold. You don’t listen; I shall talk to Nachtvinsky about your hearing. Now, come, follow me.’
Allyra sat perfectly still,
‘I’m not going anywhere with you, you’re barking mad.’
Bigglesworth grunted as he stood, leaned down and threw her back over his shoulder. He strode along the deck and to her cabin, then dolloped her on the floor,
‘Undress before you catch a disease.’
‘Diseases are caused by pathogens, not swimming,’ Allyra argued.

Bigglesworth’s eyes glowed red,
‘Don’t lecture me with your womansplaining, Madam, I know more about pathogens than you ever will. You have until the count of three then I shall undress you myself. ONE! TWO!’

‘Fine,’ Allyra sighed as she removed her catsuit. Bigglesworth cast his eyes over her body, taking in her lingerie which was even tighter than her suit.
‘And the rest!’ Bigglesworth ordered.
‘Turn around then!’ Allyra grouched.
‘Madam, you spend the better part of your time riding your way through The Deep, I am sure a quick glance from my loving eyes will not harm you.’ 
Allyra shook her head and dropped her underwear.
‘You are very wet,’ Bigglesworth observed, ‘I would say you rather liked being thrown into the sea.’ 
He took one of the sheets from the bed and used it to towel dry her body. 

Once Bigglesworth was satisfied, he rubbed the same sheet through her hair,
‘Now get under the dry sheet and keep yourself warm.’
‘What, so I can sleep for five minutes, and you can wake me up again with more nonsense?’
Bigglesworth gripped Allyra under the arm, frogmarched her to her bed, peeled back the remaining blanket and pushed her in. He then removed his own clothes at haste.

‘What in Irkalla do you think you are doing?’ Allyra asked.
‘You don’t want me to catch my death of cold, do you?’
‘I already said pathogens cause… Oh forget it,’ Allyra moaned, cuddling up to the warmth of the sheet.

Once Bigglesworth was fully naked, Allyra copped a sneaky eyeful. 

He climbed into bed next to her.
‘I presume you are aware of the wedding plans by now?’ He asked.
‘I am aware that you think we are getting married, you told me that earlier, you senile old git.’
Bigglesworth shifted up to Allyra,
‘Body heat to keep you warm,’ he whispered. ‘And don’t be insolent to your betters,’ he growled, then his mood shifted again. This time to an eerily cheerful disposition, or, as Allyra considered it, creepy.
‘Since we are all marrying you,’ Bigglesworth grinned, ‘I think a little pre-wedding taste would not be considered too forward.’ 

Allyra did not answer, as she was not really sure how to handle, well, any of it. 

Bigglesworth ran his hand through her hair,
‘Nicolas made the right choice,’ he said, stroking her gently.
‘Did he now?’ Allyra asked, ‘Nic, is this some sort of game before I am dispatched to lower my guard? Or do you just drive all Immolesses nuts?’
‘Don’t insult us,’ Bigglesworth commented as his hand moved to her cheek, ‘I like you, Allyra. I really do.’ 
‘Are you going to kill and eat me like the others?’ Allyra asked.
Bigglesworth bit his tongue until it bled,
‘Our marriage is eternal,’ he replied at length. 
‘That is not what I asked.’

Bigglesworth ignored Allyra’s comment, pulled back the sheets and took in her body. His stomach lurched, and a warmth spread throughout his belly. The warmth then travelled up his throat, into his mouth, and he vomited a thick pool of dark red blood on the Nicolai bride. 

Allyra’s mouth opened as if she was just about to say something, when a second waterfall of blood cascaded onto her tongue. She froze,
‘What the fuck?’ 
Bigglesworth took the opportunity to further his romantic gestures by shoving his boner into her belly button. 
‘You are most beloved,’ he sang as Allyra wiped the vomit from her tongue.

Bigglesworth rubbed his horn up and down her body some more and whispered,
‘I should like to make gentle love to you until mid-morning, then you may rest.’
‘I can rest?’ Allyra asked as she wiped more blood-vomit onto the sheet. 
‘Yes.’
‘Is that a promise?’
Bigglesworth looked from side to side,
‘And I shall send you flowers of the deepest black to your home in Togaduine.’
‘I live in Thanata,’ Allyra replied.

Bigglesworth rubbed himself harder against her opting to ignore her obvious confusion over her place of residence. 

Like all women, Allyra found nothing more arousing than to have a dick poked into her flesh.
‘Fine, make love to me,’ she said with the enthusiasm of a confused and chronically depressed lemming.

Bigglesworth kissed her gently on the lips.

He stroked her breasts.

He parted her legs.

text:
Fancy this.

Despite US blacklist, procurement records show that Northwestern Polytechnical University (NPU) managed to purchase Nvidia H200 chips last month, Reuters reports.

https://t.co/XJAQBtH3Ki

Northwestern Polytechnical University (西北工业大学) is located in the Shaanxi province of China.

Based in the northwestern city of Xian, NPU conducts research related to military aircraft, missiles and satellites.

The NPU is positioned as a member of the "Seven Sons of National Defense" group of Chinese universities under US sanctions and ⁠with a history of conducting defence-related research for Beijing.

Reuters described it as a university with ​deep ties to the People's Liberation Army.

Reports show the NPU bought two H200 chips ​last month (October 2026) for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), according to an October 21 procurement record on its website.

The chips were purchased for its management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia, the record shows.

However, Reuters says it could not determine contact details for Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology.

Reuters has traced NPU's access this year to H200 chips and other powerful Nvidia AI processors through five contracts for rented computing capacity from Chinese companies, ​based on procurement records.

The H200 is among Nvidia's most capable chips for training and running advanced AI systems ​and is subject to US export licence approvals, which are normally denied for blacklisted institutions such as Northwestern Polytechnical.

Procurement records also show that other universities have bought Nvidia chips barred from export to China.

The university list includes Shenzhen University, Wuhan University of Technology, Beihang University (another of the Seven Sons of National Defense universities), and the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences.

The awards of supply contracts went to several little-known Chinese technology suppliers. But the records offered scant information about where the processors originated or where the rented servers ​operated.

What's starkly is that the chips were bought from Chinese suppliers rather than directly from Nvidia.

USA now jolted...

Such purchases highlight the limits of Washington's controls on advanced AI chips.

The findings come as Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang now face mounting scrutiny in Washington over his lobbying for looser restrictions on sales of AI chips to China, following reports alleging he was targeted by a Chinese spying operation.

Whilst, Huang has been a vocal advocate for looser US export controls on AI chip exports to China.

SOMETHING HUANG DID NOT TELL...

A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to Nvidia-powered computing services that use such chips through domestic suppliers. 

Several had close ‌links to China's ⁠defence industry or military research, Reuters says.

Let me say it again... US is now jolted.

According to POLITICO, the blast radius from Nvidia’s espionage scandal is now spreading to the Commerce Department, potentially setting up Secretary Howard Lutnick or other agency leaders to be the Trump administration’s scapegoats.

https://t.co/XELZ3h749y

On Nov 12, Trump authorised a crack down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China for the third time this year — and one man stood up naked: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

So says Axios.

https://t.co/9fc7iFKwoN

In fact, CNN quoted sources as saying Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had challenged Howard Lutnick over his department’s reluctance to label Nvidia customer Megaspeed a possible national security threat in a Situation Room confrontation last week.

https://t.co/cacVU69wPx

That aptly illustrates the tension inside the Trump administration over Chinese access to Nvidia’s advanced chips.

By the look of it, I think we haven't heard the last of it as yet... until the search in Megaspeed and Speedmatrix is resolved.

For the sake of AI advancement, may Malaysia offer help? 

These China-funded AI-trading companies were active in Johor!

text:
So-called business journalists in Malaysia are hopelessly ignorant or simply lazy.

NST-Business Times probably has a worthy angle when it touched on the tighter scrutiny expected on Malaysia as Nvidia scandal spills over.

But their interview candidates are bankers honing the 'economist' label - BIMB Securities, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd... the 'usual suspects' dispensing viewpoints as if they are true-blood AI industry practitioners.

https://t.co/z03OWjE8iz

The Nvidia controversy is this: 

The intimate relationship between Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a China's spy trying to get advanced AI technology from the US.

https://t.co/ll8ffeYAua

Alice was alleged to have founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd, which had been investigated by authorities in the US and Singapore over suspected breaches of US export controls over advanced AI chips to China.

https://t.co/NlqVQOhMle

The FBI is currently intensifying probe on Nvidia after failed attempts by the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice since 2023.

https://t.co/a6G0zCKhdG

The issue has since drawn attention back to Malaysia following reports linking Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, to the supply chain. 

If NST-Business Times journalists had bothered to do their homework well, they should have researched their Reuters archive for a story the global agency ran as early as as on December 8, 2023.

2023 was about the same time New York Times, Financial Times and WSJ mentioned as the starting point of the honey-trap that both Huang's fell into.

Why December 8? Read the Reuters headlines:

'Nvidia to partner Malaysia's YTL Power in $4.3 bln AI development project'

Byline: Journalists Rozanna Latiff (Reuters' Malaysia and Brunei bureau chief) and Fanny Potkin. 

The story's opener is traced to what YTL Power International said in a statement on the same day. 

https://t.co/RFbMA4VDoZ

The announcement confirmed the Nvidia-YTL project would be hosted at YTL's data centre park in Kulai, Johor.

PM Anwar Ibrahim was so elated that he posted on X (this same social media platform formerly known as Twitter), that the collaboration between Nvidia and YTL will involve an investment worth RM20 billion (US$4.29 billion).

That's after Anwar having a meeting with Jensen Huang and YTL Power managing director Yeoh Seok Hong in Putrajaya.

If the Nvidia scandal were to affect the import of AI-related chips, GPU and accelerators into Malaysia, the one most directly affected will be YTL Power.

YTL Power's AI project is skewed towards Nvidia, and its systemic updates and upgrades would require hardware way more advanced than the H100 and H200 versions... and with that comes more monetary investments in US$. 

YTL can't afford to fail or change course midway. Their views are important and relevant to Malaysia's AI infrastructural growth.

What's the point of gearing up a 2025 start-up like SNS Network Technology Bhd that NST-Business Times chose to talk to... and quote lavishly?

Showlah some respect to Malaysia's Nvidia taiko-partner. 

Get YTL Power for valuable perspectives though they may be less successful in 5G outing via Yes!
 
LASTLY... while tracing the Alice Huang's whereabout, don't forget to dig up on her operative vehicles in Malaysia - Megaspeed and Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd - both are in Johor.

Don't ever let the foreign press get the scoop again on all things so nasi lemak!

And here's the latest from Reuters, again:

'Nvidia faces deepening scrutiny over China chip ties, CEO affair'

https://t.co/W1Zw6geuvD

Jordan Gatley was a 24-year-old British Army veteran who volunteered to defend Ukraine following Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. Originally from Glossop, England, Gatley attended Sandbach School in Cheshire before serving six years in the British Army, reaching the rank of Lance Corporal with the Rifles. In March 2022, he left the Army and travelled to Ukraine, where he joined the International Legion. He was killed in June 2022 during the brutal fighting for Sievierodonetsk, reportedly while providing covering fire for his comrades as Russian forces advanced on their position. Footage from his final engagement, along with testimony from a Canadian soldier who survived it, offers a particularly sobering account of his final hours.

I had originally intended to publish this tribute on Remembrance Day, but unfortunately, we did not have the editorial capacity to get it finished in time. Nevertheless, I want to extend my heartfelt condolences to Jordan Gatley's family, who raised such a diligent, courageous, and remarkable young man. At just 24 years old, he made the ultimate sacrifice in the defense of Ukraine and, by extension, European freedom. His service and sacrifice deserve to be remembered, particularly by those of us who understand what it means to volunteer for a war far from home.

text:
🌍 WORLD MILITARY FILES
🇺🇸 PATRIOT — AMERICA'S AIR & MISSILE DEFENSE SYSTEM

🚀 Can a missile really destroy another missile in midair?

The answer is yes.

Meet the MIM-104 Patriot, one of the world's most widely recognized air and missile defense systems.

But how does it work, and can it stop every incoming threat?

Let's explore.

🔹 1. WHAT IS PATRIOT?

Patriot is not just a missile.

It's an integrated defense system consisting of:

📡 Radar — Detects and tracks aerial threats
💻 Command & Control — Coordinates engagements
🚀 Launchers — Carry and fire interceptors
⚡ Interceptors — Attempt to destroy incoming threats

These components work together to defend military forces and critical infrastructure.

🔹 2. WHAT CAN IT INTERCEPT?

Patriot is designed to defend against several types of threats:

✈️ Military aircraft
🚀 Cruise missiles
🎯 Tactical ballistic missiles
🛡️ Other supported aerial threats

However, interception performance depends on the missile variant, radar, target characteristics and engagement conditions.

No air defense system guarantees a successful interception every time.

🔹 3. PAC-2 VS. PAC-3: WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE?

Patriot uses different interceptor families.

🔸 PAC-2 GEM-T

Primarily uses a blast-fragmentation warhead to destroy targets.

🔸 PAC-3 MSE

Uses hit-to-kill technology, designed to destroy a target through a high-energy direct impact.

The PAC-3 MSE also offers improved performance over earlier PAC-3 variants.

A compatible launcher can carry:

• Up to 4 PAC-2 GEM-T missiles
• Up to 12 PAC-3 MSE interceptors

These are published launcher configurations, not the loadout of every deployed unit.

🔹 4. WHY IS HIT-TO-KILL IMPORTANT?

Imagine trying to intercept a fast-moving missile with another missile.

Instead of relying primarily on an explosive fragmentation effect, PAC-3 MSE is designed to collide directly with the incoming threat.

The enormous kinetic energy of that collision helps destroy the target.

It's an extraordinary engineering challenge involving precision guidance, sensors and rapid control adjustments.

🔹 5. THE NEXT GENERATION: 360° DEFENSE

The U.S. Army is developing the Lower Tier Air and Missile Defense Sensor (LTAMDS).

Unlike the traditional Patriot radar's sector-oriented coverage, LTAMDS is designed to provide 360-degree surveillance.

Combined with the Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS), it aims to connect sensors and interceptors more flexibly.

Successful flight tests have demonstrated important capabilities, but tests should not be confused with universal operational performance.

🔹 6. THE BIGGEST CHALLENGE: COST & PRODUCTION

Missile defense has a serious economic problem.

Advanced interceptors are expensive and take time to manufacture.

Sustained attacks can consume valuable missile inventories, creating pressure on industrial production and supply chains.

In July 2026, the U.S. Army announced a multiyear PAC-3 MSE contracting framework with a ceiling of approximately $58.62 billion.

Importantly, this was a contract ceiling, NOT money already spent.

Lockheed Martin has announced plans to expand annual PAC-3 MSE production capacity from approximately 600 to 2,000 by the end of 2030.

That is a future capacity target, not today's production rate.

⚖️ FINAL ASSESSMENT

Patriot demonstrates how modern defense depends on combining radar, computing, precision-guided missiles and coordinated military networks.

But even highly sophisticated defenses face limitations:

• Finite interceptor inventories
• High procurement and sustainment costs
• Complex, simultaneous threats
• The need for layered protection

Technology matters. So does the ability to manufacture and sustain it.

text:
The Second Section, 
  which is the Second Treatise 
  On the Month of Ramadan 
   [There having been a brief discussion of 'the marks of Islam' at the end of the First Section, the most brilliant and splendid of the marks, Ramadan the Noble, is discussed in this Second Section. This Section consists of Nine Points, which explain nine of the numerous instances of wisdom in the month of Ramadan.]
  In the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. 
   It was the month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was bestowed from on high as a guidance unto man and a self-evident proof of that guidance, and as the standard to discern true from false. {[*]: Qur'an, 2: 185.}
   FIRST POINT 
   The fast of Ramadan is one of the five pillars of Islam, and it is one of the greatest of the marks and observances of Islam.
   There are many purposes and instances of wisdom in the fast of Ramadan which look to both God Almighty's dominicality, and to man's social life, his personal life and the training of his instinctual soul, and to his gratitude for Divine bounties. One of the many instances of wisdom in fasting from the point of view of God Almighty's dominicality is as follows:
   God Almighty created the face of the earth in the form of a table laden with bounties, and arranged on the table every sort of bounty in a form of From whence he does not expect, {[*]: Qur'an, 65:3.} in this way stating the perfection of His dominicality and His mercifulness and compassionateness. Human beings are unable to discern clearly the reality of this situation while in the sphere of causes, under the veil of heedlessness, and they sometimes forget it. However, during the month of Ramadan, the people of belief suddenly become like a well drawn-up army. As sunset approaches, they display a worshipful attitude as though, having been invited to the Pre-Eternal Monarch's banquet, they are awaiting the command of "Fall to and help yourselves!" They are responding to that compassionate, illustrious, and universal mercy with comprehensive, exalted, and orderly worship. Do you think those who do not participate in such elevated worship and noble bounties are worthy to be called human beings?
   SECOND POINT 
   One of the many instances of wisdom in the fast of the blessed month of Ramadan with respect to thankfulness for God Almighty's bounties is as follows:
   As is stated in the First Word, a price is required for the foods a tray-bearer brings from a royal kitchen. But, to give a tip to the tray-bearer, and to suppose those priceless bounties to be valueless and not to recognize the one who bestowed them would be the greatest foolishness.
   God Almighty has spread innumerable sorts of bounties over the face of the earth for mankind, in return for which He wishes thanks, as the price of those bounties. The apparent causes and possessors of the bounties are like tray-bearers. We pay a certain price to them and are indebted to them, and even though they do not merit it, are over-respectful and grateful to them. Whereas the True Bestower of Bounties is infinitely more deserving of thanks than those causes which are merely the means for the bounty. To thank Him, then, is to recognize that the bounties come directly from Him; it is to appreciate their worth and to perceive one's own need for them.
   Fasting in Ramadan, then, is the key to a true, sincere, extensive, and universal thankfulness. For at other times of the year, most of those who are not in difficult circumstances do not realize the value of many bounties since they do not experience real hunger. Those whose stomachs are full and especially if they are rich, do not understand the degree of bounty there is in a piece of dry bread. But when it is time to break the fast, the sense of taste testifies that the dry bread is a most valuable Divine bounty in the eyes of a believer. During Ramadan, everyone from the monarch to the destitute, manifests a sort of gratitude through understanding the value of those bounties.
   Furthermore, since eating is prohibited during the day, they will say: "Those bounties do not belong to me. I am not free to eat them, for they are another's property and gift. I await his command." They will recognize the bounty to be bounty and so will be giving thanks. Thus, fasting in this way is in many respects like a key to gratitude; gratitude being man's fundamental duty.    THIRD POINT 
   One of the many instances of wisdom in fasting from the point of view of man's social life is as follows:
   Human beings have been created differently with regard to their livelihoods. As a consequence of the difference, God Almighty invites the rich to assist the poor, so that through the hunger experienced in fasting, the rich can truly understand the pains and hunger which the poor suffer. If there was no fasting, there would be many self-indulgent rich unable to perceive just how grievous is hunger and poverty and how needy of compassion are those who suffer them.
   Compassion for one's fellow men is an essential of true thankfulness. Whoever a person is, there will always be someone poorer than himself in some respect. He is enjoined to be compassionate towards that person. If he was not himself compelled to suffer hunger, he would be unable give the person-by means of compassion-the help and assistance which he is obliged to offer. And even if he was able, it would be deficient, for he would not have truly experienced the state of hunger himself.
   FOURTH POINT 
   One instance of wisdom in fasting in Ramadan with respect to training the instinctual soul is as follows:
   The instinctual soul wants to be free and independent, and considers itself to be thus. According to the dictates of its nature, it even desires an imaginary dominicality and to act as it pleases. It does not want to admit that it is being sustained and trained through innumerable bounties. Especially if it possesses wealth and power in this world, and if heedlessness also encourages it, it will devour God's bounties like a usurping, thieving animal.
   Thus, in the month of Ramadan, the instinctual soul of everyone, from the richest to the poorest, may understand that it does not own itself, but is totally owned; that it is not free, but is a slave. It understands that if it receives no command, it is unable to do the simplest and easiest thing, it cannot even stretch out its hand towards water. Its imaginary dominicality is therefore shattered; it performs its worship and begins to offer thanks, its true duty.
   FIFTH POINT 
   One of the many instances of wisdom in fasting in Ramadan from the point of view of improving the conduct of the instinctual soul and giving up its rebellious habits is as follows:
   The human soul forgets itself through heedlessness. It cannot see the utter powerlessness, want, and deficiency within itself and it does not wish to see them. And it does not think of just how weak it is, and how subject to transience and to disasters, nor of the fact that it consists merely of flesh and bones, which quickly decline and are dispersed.
   Simply, it assaults the world as though it possessed a body made of steel and imagined itself to be undying and eternal. It hurls itself onto the world with intense greed and voracity and passionate attachment and love. It is captivated by anything that gives its pleasure or that benefits it. Moreover, it forgets its Creator Who sustains it with perfect compassion, and it does not think of the results of its life and its life in the hereafter. Indeed, it wallows in dissipation and misconduct.
   However, fasting in the month of Ramadan awakens even the most heedless and obstinate to their weakness, impotence, and want. By means of hunger, they think of their stomachs; they understand the need therein. They realize how unsound are their weak bodies, and perceive how needy they are for kindness and compassion. So they abandon the soul's pharaoh-like despotism, and through recognizing their utter impotence and want, perceive a desire to take refuge at the Divine Court. And they prepare themselves to knock at the door of mercy with the hands of thankfulness. So long as heedlessness has not destroyed their hearts, that is.
   SIXTH POINT 
   One of the many instances of wisdom in fasting in Ramadan from the point of view of the revelation of the All-Wise Qur'an, and with respect to the fact that the month of Ramadan was the most important time in its revelation, is as follows:
   Since the All-Wise Qur'an was revealed in the month of Ramadan, to shun the lower demands of the soul and trivialities and to resemble the angelic state by abstaining from food and drink in order to greet that heavenly address in the best manner, is to attain to a holy state. And to read and listen to the Qur'an as though it was just revealed, to listen to the Divine address in it as if it was being revealed that very instant, to listen to that address as though hearing it from God's Noble Messenger (Upon whom be blessings and peace), indeed, from the Angel Gabriel, or from the Pre-Eternal Speaker Himself, is to attain to that same holy state. To act in this way is to act as an interpreter and to cause others to listen to it and in some degree to demonstrate the wisdom in the Qur'an's revelation.
   Indeed, it is as if the world of Islam becomes a mosque during the month of Ramadan. In every corner of that mighty mosque millions of those who know the whole Qur'an by heart cause the dwellers on the earth to hear the heavenly address. Each Ramadan displays the verse It was the month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was bestowed from on high in luminous shining manner. It proves that Ramadan is the month of the Qur'an. Some of the members of the vast congregation listen to the reciters with reverence, while others read it themselves.
   Following the appetites of the base instinctual soul while in a sacred mosque that is such, and quitting that luminous condition through eating and drinking, is truly loathsome and makes such a person the target of the aversion and disgust of the congregation in the mosque. In the same way, people who oppose those who fast during Ramadan are to the same extent the target of the aversion and disgust of the whole world of Islam.
   SEVENTH POINT 
   One of the many instances of wisdom in the fast of Ramadan with respect to mankind's gain and profit, who comes to this world in order to cultivate and trade for the hereafter, is as follows:
   The reward for actions in the month of Ramadan is a thousandfold. According to Hadith, each word of the All-Wise Qur'an has ten merits; each is counted as ten merits and will yield ten fruits in Paradise. While during Ramadan, each word bears not ten fruits but a thousand, and verses like Ayat al-Kursi {[*]: Qur'an, 2:255.} thousands for each word, and on Fridays in Ramadan it is even more. And on the Night of Power, each word is counted as thirty thousand merits.
   Indeed, the All-Wise Qur'an, each of whose words yield thirty thousand eternal fruits, is like a luminous Tree of Tuba that gains for believers in Ramadan millions of those eternal fruits. So, come and look at this sacred, eternal profitable trade, then consider it and understand the infinite loss of those who do not appreciate the value of those words.
   To put it simply, the month of Ramadan is an extremely profitable display and market for the trade of the hereafter. It is an extremely fertile piece of land for the crops of the hereafter. For the growth and flourishing of actions it is like April showers in the spring. It is like a brilliant holy festival for the parade of mankind's worship in the face of the sovereignty of Divine dominicality. Since it is thus, mankind has been charged with fasting in order not to heedlessly indulge the animal needs of the instinctual soul like eating and drinking, nor to indulge the appetites lustfully and in trivialities. For, by temporarily rising above animality and quitting the calls of this world, man approaches the angelic state and enters upon the trade of the hereafter. And by fasting, he approaches the state of the hereafter and that of a spirit appearing in bodily form. It is as if man then becomes a sort of mirror reflecting the Eternally Besought One. Indeed, the month of Ramadan comprises and gains a permanent and eternal life in this fleeting world and brief transient life.
   Certainly, a single Ramadan can produce fruits equal to that of a lifetime of eighty years. The fact that, according to the Qur'an, the Night of Power is more auspicious than a thousand months is a decisive proof of this.
   For example, a monarch may declare certain days to be festivals during his reign, or perhaps once a year. Either on his accession to the throne or on some other days which reflect a glittering manifestation of his sovereignty. On those days, he favours his subjects, not within the general sphere of the law, but with his special bounties and favours, with his presence without veil and his wondrous activities. And he favours with his especial regard and attention those of his nation who are completely loyal and worthy.
   In the same way, the All-Glorious Monarch of eighteen thousand worlds, Who is the Sovereign of Pre-Eternity and Post-Eternity, revealed in Ramadan the illustrious decree of the All-Wise Qur'an, which looks to the eighteen thousand worlds. It is a requirement of wisdom, then, that Ramadan should be like special Divine festival, a dominical display, and a spiritual gathering. Since Ramadan is such festival, God has commanded man to fast, in order to disengage him to a degree from base and animal activities.
   The most excellent fasting is to make the human senses and organs, like the eyes, ears, heart, and thoughts, fast together with the stomach. That is, to withdraw them from all unlawful things and from trivia, and to urge each of them to their particular worship.
   For example, to ban the tongue from lying, back-biting, and obscene language and to make it fast. And to busy it with activities like reciting the Qur'an, praying, glorifying God's Names, asking for God's blessings on the Prophet Muhammad (Upon whom be blessings and peace), and seeking forgiveness for sins. And for example, to prevent the eyes looking at members of the opposite sex outside the stipulated degrees of kinship, and the ears from hearing harmful things, and to use the eyes to take lessons and the ears to listen to the truth and to the Qur'an, is to make other organs fast too. As a matter of fact, since the stomach is the largest factory, if it has an enforced holiday from work through fasting, the other small workshops will be made to follow it easily.    EIGHTH POINT 
   One of the many instances of wisdom in Ramadan from the point of view of man's personal life is as follows:
   It is a healing physical and spiritual diet of the most important kind. When man's instinctual soul eats and drinks just as it pleases, it is both harmful for man's physical life from the medical point of view, and when it hurls itself on everything it encounters without considering whether it is licit or illicit, it quite simply poisons his spiritual life. Further, it is difficult for such a soul to obey the heart and the spirit. It wilfully takes the reins into its own hands, and then man cannot ride it, it rather rides man. But by means of fasting in Ramadan, it becomes accustomed to a sort of diet. It tries to discipline itself and learns to listen to commands.
   Furthermore, it will not be attracting illness to that miserable, weak stomach by cramming it with food before the previous consignment has been digested. And by abandoning even licit actions as it is commanded, it will acquire the ability to listen to the commands of the Shari'a and the reason, and so to avoid illicit actions. It will try not to destroy his spiritual life.
   Moreover, the great majority of mankind frequently suffer from hunger. Man, therefore, needs hunger and discipline, which are training for patience and endurance. Fasting in Ramadan is patient endurance of a period of hunger that continues for fifteen hours, or for twenty-four if the pre-dawn meal is not eaten, and it is a discipline and a training. That is to say, fasting is also a cure for impatience and lack of endurance, which double man's afflictions.
   Futhermore, the factory of the stomach has many workers. And many of the human organs are connected to it. If the instinctual soul does not have a rest from activity during the day for a month, it makes the factory's workers and those organs forget their particular duties. It makes them busy with itself so that they remain under its tyranny. Also, it confuses the rest of the organs in the human body with the clangour and steam of the factory's machinery. It continuously attracts their attention to itself, making them temporarily forget their exalted duties. It is because of this that for centuries those closest to God have accustomed themselves to discipline and to eating and drinking little in order to be perfected.
   However, through fasting in Ramadan the factory's workers understand that they were not created for the factory only. While the rest of the organs, instead of delighting in the lowly amusements of the factory, take pleasure in angelic and spiritual amusements, and fix their gazes on them. It is for this reason that in Ramadan the believers experience enlightenment, fruitfulness, and spiritual joys which differ according to their degrees. Their subtle faculties, such as the heart, spirit, and intellect, make great progress and advancement in that blessed month by means of fasting. They laugh with innocent joy inspite of the stomach's weeping.
   NINTH POINT 
   One of the instances of wisdom in fasting in Ramadan with regard to shattering the instinctual soul's imaginary dominicality and making known its worship through pointing out its impotence is as follows:
   The instinctual soul does not want to recognize its Sustainer; it wants its own lordship, like Pharaoh. However much torment it suffers, that character remains in it. It is however destroyed through hunger. And so, fasting in Ramadan strikes direct blows at the soul's pharaoh-like front, shattering it. It demonstrates its impotence, weakness, and want. It makes it realize that it is a slave.
   Among the narrations of Hadith is the following: "God Almighty said to the instinctual soul: 'What am I and what are you?' The soul replied: 'I am myself and You are Yourself.' So He punished it and cast it into Hell, then asked it again. Again it replied: 'I am myself and You are Yourself.' However He punished it, it did not give up its egoism. Finally He punished it with hunger. That is, He left it hungry. Then again He asked it: 'Who am I and who are you?' And the soul replied: 'You are my Compassionate Sustainer and I am your impotent slave.'"
   O God! Grant blessings and peace to our master Muhammad, that will be pleasing to You and fulfilment of his truth to the number of the merits of the words of the Qur'an in the month of Ramadan, and to his Family and Companions, and grant them peace. 
   Limitless in His glory is your Sustainer, the Lord of Almightiness, [exalted] above anything that men may devise by way of definition! * And peace be upon all His message-bearers. * And all praise is due to God alone, the Sustainer of All the Worlds! 4

text:
Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy on Sunday and kept his job running a $4 trillion company.

By Wednesday night his own board was reportedly getting ready to fire him, over something way more ordinary than espionage.

The New York Times dropped a second story. Five people who worked at Nvidia told the paper Jensen had been in a relationship with one of his own executives, a VP who reports directly to him. Two of them say someone at a San Jose hotel caught the two of them on video during Nvidia's big developer conference in March. Nvidia, Jensen and the executive haven't confirmed any of it, and the Times says it hasn't seen the video.

Here's why that's worse than a spy, at least if you're sitting on his board.

Go back and read what the board said on Sunday. Directors called Jensen "the target of a foreign intelligence effort" and said they had confidence in him. A target is basically a victim, and a board can stand behind a victim even when he made it easy.

You can't spin a relationship with your own direct report that way. Nvidia's code of conduct tells employees to avoid conflicts that come from personal relationships, and if the reporting is right, the guy at the very top broke a rule that applies to every person who works for him.

And it gets worse. Per the Times, after someone filmed them, Jensen's security team pulled that person aside and offered them an NDA. Once a security detail and a nondisclosure agreement are in the picture, directors have to start asking what else got handled quietly.

Boards already know how this movie ends, because McDonald's lived it. Back in 2019 McDonald's fired CEO Steve Easterbrook over a relationship with an employee, but they did it "without cause," so he walked away with tens of millions in pay and stock. The next year the company accused him of lying to cover up relationships with other employees, sued him, and got back more than $105 million.

Then in 2023 a Delaware judge let shareholders drag McDonald's former HR chief to trial, the first time that court said executives have the same duty to watch for this stuff that directors do.

That's what three days did to Nvidia's board. If they keep Jensen now, shareholder lawyers basically have their complaint written for them, and anybody who sat on a public board in 2019 watched McDonald's go through exactly that.

He doesn't have the safety net a lot of founders have, either. Zuck can survive almost anything because he controls the majority of Meta's votes, and Nvidia has one class of stock, so Jensen has nothing like that. More than 528 million of his shares sit in a family trust that his wife Lori, the person he apologized to on Sunday, co-manages.

The part that gets me is who's making the call. Tench Coxe and Harvey Jones have been on Nvidia's board since 1993, the year Jensen and his two co-founders started the company after meeting at a Denny's. Both of them got rich betting on him for 33 years.

If those two are ready to let him go, the lawyers already won.

text:
"Highly beneficial to Tesla." That was a Delaware judge's verdict on the SolarCity acquisition in April 2022, after an 11-day trial.

Six years earlier, legacy media had a different story. In June 2016 the Los Angeles Times wrote that analysts saw Tesla's offer as "more like a rescue effort for struggling SolarCity." Glass Lewis called it a "thinly veiled bailout plan," and the LA Times and Bloomberg both printed the line. In 2019 Bloomberg Businessweek was still calling the purchase "the top threat to Tesla's future."

Elon Musk had laid out the plan back in the first Tesla Master Plan, in August 2006: move the world "towards a solar electric economy." He named SolarCity in that same post. In 2016 he wrote that Tesla and SolarCity couldn't do it well as separate companies.

Tesla's unaffiliated shareholders agreed. With the votes of Elon Musk and other affiliated holders excluded, 85.1 percent voted yes in November 2016.

Then the shareholders who sued got their day in court. Vice Chancellor Joseph Slights applied entire fairness, the toughest standard in Delaware law, and found that "SolarCity was, at a minimum, worth what Tesla paid for it." The Delaware Supreme Court affirmed in June 2023.

This is now the SECOND OR THIRD time you've come after my opinions. I was kind and respectful enough to tell you we could agree to disagree. Yet here you are again.

I've followed the Karen Read case for over TWO YEARS. I've watched testimony, followed the evidence, and listened to both sides. I can have an intelligent discussion, present facts, and respect a difference of opinion. Can you?

And since you brought up Netflix being a for-profit business, let's talk FACTS. Netflix makes BILLIONS and is increasingly competing with YouTube for viewers, creators, and advertising revenue. So yes, I have every reason to question whether profits and sensationalism are taking priority over responsible storytelling.

Look at the people highlighted in the trailer. Even DISGUSTING Michael Proctor, the disgraced former Massachusetts State Police trooper! Where is Karen Read's perspective? Where is her defense team?

As @takenaps would say, this is looking like a one-sided SLOPumentary!

And NO, I haven't watched the documentary. It hasn't even premiered yet! But I've watched the trailer, and after spending two years following this case, I certainly don't need your permission to question its apparent direction.

A documentary doesn't have to be objective, but it absolutely should be truthful. And viewers have every right to question what is being presented—and what may be left out. That's why it's called a documentary; it's usually based on real events. 

Here's what you seem to be missing: Disagreeing with someone doesn't give you a license to repeatedly belittle them.

I've already offered to agree to disagree. You might consider showing the same maturity.

And one final thing: A degree after your name doesn't make your opinion a fact, and it certainly doesn't invalidate mine. 

Now, can we agree to disagree, or is that too much to ask? 👠 XOXO SASSY ✨💕💁‍♀️

text:
She robbed a video store for $162, shot porn to pay rent, and overdosed on Valium at 14 - but none of that killed Dana Plato’s career. Getting pregnant did. Fired from Diff’rent Strokes at 20, she watched her accountant steal everything while America forgot her name. On her last day alive, she told Howard Stern she’d been sober for ten years. They called her a liar. She was dead before sunrise.

Dana Plato was born in 1964 in Maywood, California, given up by her teenage mother and adopted as an infant. By seven she was doing commercials, by thirteen she was Kimberly Drummond on Diff’rent Strokes, one of the biggest sitcoms in America.

Then she got pregnant at 19. NBC wrote her out. No negotiations, no maternity leave - just gone.

Her accountant embezzled most of her savings and disappeared. Broke and desperate, she posed for Playboy in 1989 trying to rebrand herself. It didn’t work. She took roles in adult films for cash and forged Valium prescriptions.

In February 1991, she walked into a Las Vegas video store with a pellet gun and demanded the money. She got $162. A customer wrote down her plate. She was arrested within minutes.

“If I hadn’t gotten caught, it could have been the worst thing that happened to me because I could have died of a drug overdose,” she said after the arrest.

She spent the next years drifting between rehab and failed comebacks, living out of a Winnebago with her fiance Robert Menchaca. By 1999 she was booking appearances at conventions alongside fading rock bands, promoting B-movies nobody watched.

On May 7, 1999, she went on The Howard Stern Show. She told Stern she was engaged, happy, and sober for over a decade. “I have been sober for over ten years now. No joke,” she said. Then the phone lines opened. Caller after caller tore into her, calling her a liar and a junkie. She fought back tears and offered to take a drug test on air. A strand of her hair was cut for testing.

The next day, she stopped at her fiance’s mother’s house in Moore, Oklahoma for a Mother’s Day visit. Dana went to lie down in their RV. She never woke up.

The coroner found lethal levels of Lortab and Valium. Her death was ruled a suicide. She was 34. Betty Bridges, the mother of her former co-star Todd Bridges, blamed Howard Stern directly. “He pushed her over the edge,” she told reporters.

In the video below, you can see Dana Plato’s final interview on The Howard Stern Show, recorded less than 24 hours before her death. She insists she’s clean while strangers call in to tell her she’s worthless. She offers her own hair to prove she’s telling the truth. By the next morning, she would be dead in an RV in Oklahoma.

Her son Tyler Lambert was 14 when his mother died. On May 6, 2010, almost exactly eleven years later, he took his own life in Tulsa. He was 25. Gary Coleman, another Diff’rent Strokes child star, died that same year. People stopped calling it bad luck and started calling it a curse.

Some will say Howard Stern gave Dana Plato a platform and she destroyed herself. Others will say strangers calling a woman a liar on her last day alive is something no one comes back from.

But the real question is: what kind of industry takes a child, makes her a millionaire, fires her for being human, and then watches her rob a video store for $162 without ever picking up the phone?

text:
THE PAY PARADOX: A HEDGE FUND MANAGER'S MORNING IS WORTH FORTY-SIX YEARS OF A NURSE

NUMBERS THAT NEED NO COMMENT

In 2025, Steve Cohen, founder of the Point72 fund, earned approximately $3.4 billion. Bloomberg's ranking places him at the top of the list of the year's highest-paid hedge fund managers, ahead of Ken Griffin of Citadel. Dividing that figure by 365 days yields approximately $9.3 million per day. If we consider "before lunch" as a half-workday, Cohen earns approximately $4.6 million in a morning.

A registered nurse in the United States earns an average of $98,430 per year, with a median of $93,600, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data cited by Diversity Nursing. https://t.co/Dp63kC4jXO lists the average at $100,329. In California, the state with the highest wages, the average rises to $140,330.

The calculation is simple: Cohen's morning is equivalent to about 46 years of the average American nurse's salary. A full day is equivalent to 93 years.

THE ISSUE IS NOT THE GAP, BUT WHAT JUSTIFIES IT

The gap itself is nothing new. What's new, if you can call it that, is the way it's being described. Nurses are celebrated as "heroes" and "essential workers," but these labels don't translate into pay. Cancer Nursing Today magazine wrote unambiguously in 2024: "The label 'essential,' like 'hero,' sounds like praise, but during the pandemic, neither word has been accompanied by any real social capital." The same magazine added an observation that clarifies the mechanism: "If hospitals truly respected nurses, Nurses Week wouldn't exist. Fair and adequate pay is a reward in itself; it doesn't need to be supplemented with free pizza and coffee."

There's no such thing as a "Hedge Fund Manager Week." There's no such thing as a "Silicon Valley Billionaire Week." These professions don't receive symbolic labels because they receive money. Nurses receive symbolic labels because the money isn't forthcoming. The issue isn't that someone explicitly told nurses "you shouldn't do it for the money." The issue is that they're offered symbolic recognition as a substitute for material compensation, while fund managers are offered material compensation without the need for any symbolic recognition.

POLITICAL CRITICISM AND ITS LIMITS

Robert Reich, former U.S. Secretary of Labor, formulated this criticism bluntly: "Pay is inversely proportional to actual social benefit. Social work, teaching, nursing, eldercare, and childcare are among the lowest-paid professions, but they have enormous social benefit. Investment banking, management consulting, corporate law, and hedge fund management are among the highest-paid professions... their social benefit is negligible."

This is a political critique, not an empirical description of a speech addressed to nurses. The difference is important: Reich's critique concerns the way society values ​​productive work, not a single act of moralization aimed at a professional category. And yet the substance of the critique holds: the pay system treats symbolic recognition as an acceptable substitute for money for some professions, and money as the sole recognition for others.

CONCLUSION

That a hedge fund manager earns more in a morning than a nurse earns in a lifetime is a matter of arithmetic, not opinion. That nurses receive "heroism" instead of pay is a documented fact, not an interpretation. The point isn't that someone told them "don't do it for money." The point is that the system decided that money wasn't the appropriate reward for them and provided a symbolic alternative. For fund managers, the symbolic alternative was never necessary.

#HedgeFunds #Nurses #PayInequality #FactCheck #TheWorldCorrespondent

text:
🥾 On Pikk Street in Tallinn's Old Town, a medieval merchant's house asks a modern question: what really happens in the garage?

🏛️ The house is home to the People's Museum of Tallinn (Tallinna Rahvaste Muuseum), a branch of the Tallinn City Museum that tells the story of the many peoples who shaped the city's culture. Its current exhibition, "Garaaž. Гараж. Garage," curated by Denis Jatsenko and Aleksandra Ianchenko, treats the garage as a space both private and communal and shows how it became three things at once.

🛡️ First, it was protection for cars. Tallinn's early 20th-century garage buildings and Soviet-era garage areas sheltered the vehicles of a changing city, and the exhibition recalls Estonia's first female drivers among them.

🎨 Then it became a creative den. Workshops, hobby spaces and artists' studios moved in, and artists still make their work in garages today.

💻 Finally, it became an innovation center for entrepreneurs. Businesses still run out of garages, and the exhibition points to the most famous of all: the Palo Alto, California, garage where Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard formed their partnership in 1939, now State Historical Landmark No. 976, the "Birthplace of Silicon Valley."

📜 One of the exhibits presents the "11 Rules of the Garage" that HP formulated, inspired by that garage, on a panel styled like an early computer screen. The list opens with "Believe you can change the world" and closes with a single word: "Invent." Along the way: "Radical ideas are not bad ideas" and "The customer defines a job well done."

🪢 The rules land differently after the Tallinn Digital Summit, which opened with the Estonian folk tale of the kratt, a tireless servant that works as long as it has orders. The advice from the stage: always keep one end of the rope in your own hand. Today's kratt is the AI agent, and the summit spent two days on how to hold that rope. The garage offers the other half of the conversation, why people build at all, and Rule 9 connects the two: "Make a contribution every day. If it doesn't contribute, it doesn't leave the garage."

🚀 The next destination on ComplexDiscovery's Estonia and Finland conference journey is Slush in Helsinki next week, where thousands of founders will carry the same garage spirit onto a much larger floor.

💡 The business lesson: innovation and control are not opposites, and Rule 9 shows how they work together. Inside the garage, ideas can be radical and unfinished. Before anything leaves, whether a product, a feature or an AI agent, it must answer one question: does it contribute? Rule 6 defines who decides, because the customer, not the builder, defines a job well done.

🧭 From the summit stage to a garage door on Pikk Street, the message holds: build boldly, test honestly and keep one end of the rope in hand.

🔎 Read about the "Garage" exhibit at https://t.co/z7jJ8xkLr5.

ChironAI OM: When 14 Occupational Medicine Workflows Become One Intelligent Operating System

Occupational medicine is entering a period of significant technological transformation, particularly within California's complex workers' compensation system, where clinical decisions, medical documentation, regulatory requirements, and administrative processes are closely interconnected.

For physicians and healthcare organizations, the challenge extends beyond delivering quality medical care. Managing medical records, preparing Qualified Medical Evaluator (QME) reports, assessing causation, documenting impairment, monitoring regulatory deadlines, and coordinating billing requires considerable time and specialized expertise.

The real opportunity for artificial intelligence is not simply automating individual tasks, but connecting fragmented clinical and administrative workflows within one intelligent operating environment.

ChironAI™ Occupational Medicine introduces that approach through an agentic AI operating system designed around 14 interconnected workflows supporting California occupational medicine and workers' compensation.

Rather than requiring clinicians to navigate multiple disconnected applications, the platform aims to coordinate information, support clinical reasoning, streamline documentation, and improve operational efficiency.

What distinguishes this approach is its emphasis on maintaining professional decision making.

The AI reasons. The clinician decides.

That principle is particularly important in occupational medicine, where causation determinations, impairment ratings, treatment recommendations, and medical reporting can have significant consequences for patients, employers, insurers, and legal proceedings.

AI can help organize evidence, identify relevant information, and support consistency, but clinical conclusions must remain subject to qualified medical judgment, independent verification, and applicable regulatory standards.

My perspective is that the next generation of healthcare AI will be defined by integrated intelligence rather than isolated automation.

The greatest value will emerge when technology reduces administrative burdens while strengthening the clinician's ability to make informed, timely, and defensible decisions.

The future of occupational medicine is not about replacing physicians with artificial intelligence. It is about giving physicians an intelligent operating system that supports their expertise across the entire workflow.

ChironAI OM offers a compelling vision of that transformation.

Watch the 72-second demonstration to explore how agentic AI could reshape occupational medicine.

text:
Welcome back to The State of AI, a new collaboration between the Financial Times and MIT Technology Review. Every Monday, writers from both publications debate one aspect of the generative AI revolution reshaping global power.

In this week’s conversation MIT Technology Review’s senior reporter for features and investigations, Eileen Guo, and FT tech correspondent Melissa Heikkilä discuss the privacy implications of our new reliance on chatbots.

Eileen Guo writes:

Even if you don’t have an AI friend yourself, you probably know someone who does. A recent study found that one of the top uses of generative AI is companionship: On platforms like https://t.co/JGIsV0b4hq, Replika, or Meta AI, people can create personalized chatbots to pose as the ideal friend, romantic partner, parent, therapist, or any other persona they can dream up. 

It’s wild how easily people say these relationships can develop. And multiple studies have found that the more conversational and human-like an AI chatbot is, the more likely it is that we’ll trust it and be influenced by it. This can be dangerous, and the chatbots have been accused of pushing some people toward harmful behaviors—including, in a few extreme examples, suicide. 

Some state governments are taking notice and starting to regulate companion AI. New York requires AI companion companies to create safeguards and report expressions of suicidal ideation, and last month California passed a more detailed bill requiring AI companion companies to protect children and other vulnerable groups. 

But tellingly, one area the laws fail to address is user privacy.

This is despite the fact that AI companions, even more so than other types of generative AI, depend on people to share deeply personal information—from their day-to-day-routines, innermost thoughts, and questions they might not feel comfortable asking real people.

After all, the more users tell their AI companions, the better the bots become at keeping them engaged. This is what MIT researchers Robert Mahari and Pat Pataranutaporn called “addictive intelligence” in an op-ed we published last year, warning that the developers of AI companions make “deliberate design choices … to maximize user engagement.” 

Ultimately, this provides AI companies with something incredibly powerful, not to mention lucrative: a treasure trove of conversational data that can be used to further improve their LLMs. Consider how the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz explained it in 2023: 

“Apps such as https://t.co/JGIsV0b4hq, which both control their models and own the end customer relationship, have a tremendous opportunity to  generate market value in the emerging AI value stack. In a world where data is limited, companies that can create a magical data feedback loop by connecting user engagement back into their underlying model to continuously improve their product will be among the biggest winners that emerge from this ecosystem.”

This personal information is also incredibly valuable to marketers and data brokers. Meta recently announced that it will deliver ads through its AI chatbots. And research conducted this year by the security company Surf Shark found that four out of the five AI companion apps it looked at in the Apple App Store were collecting data such as user or device IDs, which can be combined with third-party data to create profiles for targeted ads. (The only one that said it did not collect data for tracking services was Nomi, which told me earlier this year that it would not “censor” chatbots from giving explicit suicide instructions.) 

All of this means that the privacy risks posed by these AI companions are, in a sense, required: They are a feature, not a bug. And we haven’t even talked about the additional security risks presented by the way AI chatbots collect and store so much personal information in one place. 

So, is it possible to have prosocial and privacy-protecting AI companions? That’s an open question. 

What do you think, Melissa, and what is top of mind for you when it comes to privacy risks from AI companions? And do things look any different in Europe? 

Location

A location I care about is

Generating your personalized response…

Melissa Heikkilä replies:

Thanks, Eileen. I agree with you. If social media was a privacy nightmare, then AI chatbots put the problem on steroids. 

In many ways, an AI chatbot creates what feels like a much more intimate interaction than a Facebook page. The conversations we have are only with our computers, so there is little risk of your uncle or your crush ever seeing what you write. The AI companies building the models, on the other hand, see everything. 

Companies are optimizing their AI models for engagement by designing them to be as human-like as possible. But AI developers have several other ways to keep us hooked. The first is sycophancy, or the tendency for chatbots to be overly agreeable. 

This feature stems from the way the language model behind the chatbots is trained using reinforcement learning. Human data labelers rate the answers generated by the model as either acceptable or not. This teaches the model how to behave. 

Because people generally like answers that are agreeable, such responses are weighted more heavily in training. 

AI companies say they use this technique because it helps models become more helpful. But it creates a perverse incentive. 

After encouraging us to pour our hearts out to chatbots, companies from Meta to OpenAI are now looking to monetize these conversations. OpenAI recently told us it was looking at a number of ways to meet $1 trillion spending pledges, which included advertising and shopping features. 

AI models are already incredibly persuasive. Researchers at the UK’s AI Security Institute have shown that they are far more skilled than humans at persuading people to change their minds on politics, conspiracy theories, and vaccine skepticism. They do this by generating large amounts of relevant evidence and communicating it in an effective and understandable way. 

This feature, paired with their sycophancy and a wealth of personal data, could be a powerful tool for advertisers—one that is more manipulative than anything we have seen before. 

By default, chatbot users are opted in to data collection. Opt-out policies place the onus on users to understand the implications of sharing their information. It’s also unlikely that data already used in training will be removed. 

We are all part of this phenomenon whether we want to be or not. Social media platforms from Instagram to LinkedIn now use our personal data to train generative AI models. 

Companies are sitting on treasure troves that consist of our most intimate thoughts and preferences, and language models are very good at picking up on subtle hints in language that could help advertisers profile us better by inferring our age, location, gender, and income level.

We are being sold the idea of an omniscient AI digital assistant, a superintelligent confidante. In return, however, there is a very real risk that our information is about to be sent to the highest bidder once again.

Eileen responds:

I think the comparison between AI companions and social media is both apt and concerning. 

As Melissa highlighted, the privacy risks presented by AI chatbots aren’t new—they just “put the [privacy] problem on steroids.” AI companions are more intimate and even better optimized for engagement than social media, making it more likely that people will offer up more personal information.

Here in the US, we are far from solving the privacy issues already presented by social networks and the internet’s ad economy, even without the added risks of AI.

And without regulation, the companies themselves are not following privacy best practices either. One recent study found that the major AI models train their LLMs on user chat data by default unless users opt out, while several don’t offer opt-out mechanisms at all.

In an ideal world, the greater risks of companion AI would give more impetus to the privacy fight—but I don’t see any evidence this is happening. 

Further reading 

FT reporters peer under the hood of OpenAI’s five-year business plan as it tries to meet its vast $1 trillion spending pledges. 

Is it really such a problem if AI chatbots tell people what they want to hear? This FT feature asks what’s wrong with sycophancy 

In a recent print issue of MIT Technology Review, Rhiannon Williams spoke to a number of people about the types of relationships they are having with AI chatbots.
