[미 민주당 또 시작함 ㅋㅋㅋ 의회 먹자마자 트럼프 청문회 지옥 + 이란전 총력전 오픈 준비 (feat. 3C 프레임)]

미 민주당 얘네 진짜 레퍼토리 안 바뀌고 한결같네 ㅋㅋㅋ

2026년 중간선거에서 상·하원 다수당 먹자마자 뭘 준비하는지 아냐?

민생 경제 살리기? 인플레 잡기? 서민 생활 안정?

뭐 겉으로는 당연히 그런 거 하겠다고 입 털고 있지.

근데 정작 민주당 지도부가 각 잡고 준비하는 메인 프로젝트는 따로 있음.

바로 이란 전쟁 멈추겠다고 총력전 선포하면서, 트럼프 행정부 탈탈 털어버릴 대규모 의회 조사랑 청문회 러시 때리는 거임.

11월 6일 액시오스(Axios) 보도에 따르면, 
민주당이 벌써 상·하원 여러 위원회 엮어서 트럼프 행정부 상대로 장기 조사랑 정치 메시지 때려 박을 판을 짜고 있다고 함.

심지어 거창하게 이름까지 붙였음. 이른바 '3C 전략'.

Cost — 비용 (이란 전쟁 여파에 물가까지 겹쳐서 니들 지갑 털리는 경제적 부담)

Chaos — 혼란 (나라 꼴이랑 중동 판 돌아가는 꼬라지)

Corruption — 부패 (비리 덩어리)

야, 이거 어디서 많이 본 빌드업 아니냐?

아직 제대로 된 조사 결과도 안 나왔는데, 대중들 머릿속에 박아 넣을 핵심 키워드부터 세팅해 놓은 거임.

물론 의회가 행정부 견제하고 감시하는 건 당연한 권한임. 

민주당 측에서는 의회 승인 없이 밀어붙인 이란 전쟁을 끝내고, 행정부의 정책 실패나 권한 남용 의혹을 철저히 검증해 책임을 묻는 게 의회의 본분이라는 입장이겠지.

잘못한 게 있으면 털어야 하는 게 맞긴 함.

근데 정상적인 조사라면 증거부터 모으고, 팩트 체크하고, 그 결과로 결론을 내리는 게 순서잖아?

조사도 시작하기 전에 정치적 프레임부터 짜놓고 시작하면 어떻게 되겠음?

모든 청문회가 진실 규명이 아니라, 미리 정해둔 결론을 뒷받침할 '그림'만 뽑아내는 쇼로 변질될 위험이 크다는 거임.

1. 공화당 RINO까지 가세한 피트 헤그세스 탄핵 빌드업? (J6 시즌2 각)

심지어 이번엔 민주당만 숟가락 얹는 게 아님. 

이미 공화당 내부 반트럼프 성향(일명 RINO)으로 꼽히는 토마스 매시(Thomas Massie) 하원의원이 이란 전쟁 무단 개시 등을 문제 삼아 피트 헤그세스(Pete Hegseth) 국방장관 탄핵소추안까지 발의해서 판을 깔아놨음.

비록 11월 10일 표결에서 공화당 지도부가 법사위로 넘겨버리면서 당장 본회의 통과는 막았지만, 민주당 지도부는 내년 1월 새 의회 열리자마자 다수당 힘으로 다시 불 지필 각을 재고 있음. (반면 헤그세스 장관이나 트럼프 측은 이란 핵 위협을 막기 위한 역사적 성과인데 정치 쇼로 발목 잡는다고 맞받아치는 중임.)

트럼프 1기 때 기억나지? 

러시아 스캔들, 탄핵 정국, 1월 6일 의사당 난입 사태 조사까지 임기 내내 청문회랑 조사로 미국 언론 도배됐던 거.

특히 J6 특위 때는 증언이랑 영상 기가 막히게 편집해서 대중한테 각인시키는 방식으로 엄청난 화제를 모았음. 
요즘 미국 정치판에서 청문회는 그냥 의원들이 묻고 증인이 답하는 자리가 아님. 카메라 앞에서 자극적인 짤 생성하는 거대한 미디어 이벤트에 가까움.

의원이 책상 치면서 호통침 → 증인이 당황해서 말 더듬음 → 관련 문건 화면에 띄움 → 그중 제일 자극적인 15초만 잘라서 CNN이랑 MSNBC에 송출함 → SNS에서 조회수 수백만 찍음.

나중에 전체 맥락 까보니까 앞뒤 사정이 달랐다고? 

이미 늦었지. 

대중 머릿속엔 그 15초짜리 짤만 남아 있으니까.

결국 실제로 위법 행위가 입증됐느냐보다, 유권자들이 뭘 사실로 믿게 만드느냐의 싸움으로 변질될 가능성이 높다는 거임.

2. 진짜 무서운 건 미국인들의 경제적 피로감임
이번 민주당 전략에서 제일 영리하면서도 쎄한 부분이 바로 'Cost(비용)'를 맨 앞에 세운 거임.

왜 하필 경제 문제를 1번으로 꽂았겠음? 

지금 미국 유권자들이 제일 예민하게 반응하는 역린이 바로 먹고사는 문제니까.

실제로 2026년 중간선거에서 CBS가 인용한 여론조사 보면 유권자의 89%가 생활비 문제를 중요하거나 결정적인 투표 요인으로 꼽았음. 

장바구니 물가 미쳤지, 이란 전쟁 때문에 유가랑 인플레 압박까지 겹쳤지, 집세랑 보험료에 허리 휘지, 미국 서민들 경제적 피로감이 한계치까지 쌓인 상태임.

이런 사람들한테 민주당이 어떤 메시지를 던지겠음?

"니들이 지금 이렇게 뼈 빠지게 일하고도 힘든 이유는 다 트럼프 행정부가 벌인 무리한 전쟁과 혼란, 부패 때문이다."

이보다 직관적이고 쏙쏙 박히는 정치적 선동이 또 있겠냐?

문제는 현실 경제가 그렇게 단순하지 않다는 거임. 물가랑 생활비는 통화정책, 글로벌 공급망, 에너지 가격, 노동시장, 기업 가격 정책 등 온갖 변수가 복잡하게 얽혀 있음.

근데 이 복잡한 원인을 특정 정권의 무능과 부패라는 단 하나의 서사로 퉁쳐버리면? 

당장 숨넘어가는 유권자들 귀에는 그럴싸하게 들릴 수밖에 없음. 사람이 경제적으로 쪼들릴수록 복잡한 분석보다는 당장 욕할 수 있는 명확한 타겟을 원하게 되거든.

앞으로 민주당이 이란 전쟁 청문회부터 시작해서 월가 금융권, 제약회사, 빅테크 줄소환하고 그 장면을 전부 트럼프 행정부 책임론이랑 엮어버린다면?개별 의혹의 진위 여부를 떠나서, 끊임없이 반복되는 프레임만으로도 여론이 쏠릴 수 있음. 

아직 검증 안 된 의혹도 계속 때리다 보면 기정사실처럼 굳어지는 게 프레임 정치의 무서운 점임. 지금 미국의 팍팍한 경제 상황이 딱 그 판이 먹혀들기 좋은 환경이라는 게 씁쓸할 따름임.

From Thomas Massie's Hegseth impeachment bid to the "3C" playbook: Is the incoming Democratic Congress gearing up for genuine war-powers oversight or a viral soundbite factory?

According to a November 6 report from Axios, Democratic leadership is preparing a coordinated wave of congressional investigations and hearings targeting the Trump administration once the new Congress convenes in January 2027 following their 2026 midterm victories. Alongside a pledged all-out push to halt the ongoing war in Iran, multiple House and Senate committees plan to align their oversight around a unified messaging framework dubbed the "3Cs":

Cost – Everyday financial strain, compounded by inflation and the economic fallout of Middle East conflict

Chaos – Perceived instability in domestic governance and unauthorized overseas military campaigns
Corruption – Allegations of executive misconduct, abuse of power, and corporate favoritism
This week, that dynamic escalated dramatically when outgoing Republican Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY)—who lost his GOP primary earlier this year to a Trump-backed challenger—introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. 
Massie’s 34-page resolution accuses Hegseth of waging unauthorized war against Iran in violation of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside charges stemming from U.S. military operations in Venezuela and Yemen, maritime strikes on suspected drug-trafficking vessels, and retaliation against Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly.

While House Republicans voted on Tuesday, November 10 to refer the resolution to the Judiciary Committee—effectively blocking an immediate floor vote—Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer has already endorsed the impeachment push, stating that Hegseth "must stand trial before the Senate". 

Meanwhile, Hegseth dismissed the effort as a "political spectacle" and "sabotage" during a Pentagon briefing, and President Donald Trump defended his Pentagon chief on social media, calling the House vote an exoneration of "a Great American Patriot".

Constitutional scholars and supporters of congressional oversight argue that reasserting legislative war powers and investigating executive actions in Iran, Venezuela, and Yemen is a vital constitutional duty. Yet from a political communication standpoint, rolling out a pre-branded "3C" campaign before the new Congress even takes office raises serious questions about how these hearings will actually operate.

1. Pre-packaging the narrative before the hearings begin (J6 Hearings 2.0?)

In a traditional congressional inquiry, lawmakers gather evidence, establish facts, and then draw conclusions. When party leadership locks in the core takeaways—Cost, Chaos, and Corruption—upfront, every subsequent committee hearing risks becoming a stage set designed to manufacture viral moments that reinforce a pre-existing storyline.

We saw how this plays out during Trump’s first term—from the Russia probe and impeachment trials to the January 6th Committee hearings. Regardless of the underlying legal merits, modern congressional hearings double as made-for-TV media events. A lawmaker delivers a sharp rebuke, a witness hesitates, a document flashes on screen, and the most dramatic 15-second clip dominates cable news and social media feeds. Even when fuller context emerges later, that initial 15-second clip is what cements itself in the public consciousness. With Massie’s impeachment articles already handed to Democrats on a silver platter, the temptation to turn war-powers oversight into a continuous impeachment spectacle ahead of 2028 will be immense.

2. Merging war fatigue with economic anxiety

The most calculated—and potentially polarizing—element of the Democrats' playbook is placing Cost at the top of the list.

According to exit polling cited by CBS News during the 2026 midterms, 89% of voters identified the cost of living as an important or deciding factor in their vote. Americans are worn down by high grocery prices, steep housing and insurance bills, and anxiety over how prolonged conflict with Iran could further shock global energy markets.

In that environment, linking household financial pain directly to foreign intervention and executive dysfunction—essentially telling voters, "Your life is expensive because of this administration's unauthorized wars, chaos, and corruption"—is an extraordinarily potent political message.

The catch is that macroeconomic reality is rarely that straightforward. Inflation and living costs are driven by a complex web of monetary policy, supply chains, labor markets, energy dynamics, and corporate pricing decisions. However, when voters are financially exhausted, simple narratives that offer a clear villain are far more persuasive than nuanced economic breakdowns. If Democrats pair high-profile hearings on the Iran war and Pentagon leadership with subpoenas for Wall Street banks, pharmaceutical companies, and Big Tech executives, repetition alone could reshape public perception regardless of what is legally proven.

TL;DR: 
Following Rep. Thomas Massie’s blocked impeachment bid against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress in January with an all-out push to halt the conflict and launch "3C" (Cost, Chaos, Corruption) oversight hearings. While defenders see this as a necessary reassertion of congressional war powers, critics warn that pre-branding the narrative turns oversight into a 15-second soundbite factory and oversimplifies complex economic pressures for partisan leverage.

What’s your take? 
Does pairing war-powers oversight with a "Cost, Chaos, and Corruption" message effectively hold the administration accountable, or does pre-scripting the narrative undermine the credibility of Congress's investigations before they even start?

We haven't seen a broad-based market recovery. Big Tech struggled to hold its opening gains, while much of the buying was concentrated in semiconductor and memory stocks. That's not the kind of broad participation I want to see in a sustainable recovery.

BELONGING: SONIA GANDHI'S ACCOUNT OF INDIA'S IDEOLOGICAL DIVIDE, NEHRU AND THE POLITICS OF POWER

When history becomes a political battleground, the real question is not who controls the narrative, but whether citizens have access to facts, competing perspectives and independent evidence.

SOURCE: Sanket Upadhyay, DoubleCheck by Awadh Punch [Watch the full discussion on YouTube]
https://t.co/CoLSm7XyLn

WHAT SONIA GANDHI'S MEMOIR REVEALS

In Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi offers her assessment of Narendra Modi, the RSS-BJP ideological project, Jawaharlal Nehru's legacy and India's changing political and economic landscape.

One central distinction runs through her account: the disagreement is not merely between political parties but between competing ideas of India.

She describes her vision as rooted in pluralism, secularism, liberty and equality, while arguing that the RSS-influenced political vision places greater emphasis on religious and cultural hierarchy.

Her criticism of the repeated targeting of Nehru is particularly significant. She argues that Nehru's commitment to parliamentary democracy and secularism represents precisely the constitutional foundations that the Sangh Parivar challenges.

These are Sonia Gandhi's political assessments, but they raise questions that deserve examination through historical records and constitutional principles.

NEHRU: WHY DOES HIS LEGACY REMAIN A POLITICAL BATTLEGROUND?

Nehru's historical significance cannot be reduced to the shortcomings of his governments. His contribution must also be assessed through the institutions and principles established during India's formative democratic years.

Parliamentary democracy, scientific temper, secular constitutionalism, independent institutions and a plural national identity were central to the vision of the republic.

Criticism of Nehru is legitimate. Historical mistakes should be examined honestly. But criticism becomes distortion when selective facts, misinformation and personal abuse replace serious historical inquiry.

The real test is whether political criticism strengthens historical understanding or merely delegitimises an entire constitutional inheritance.

THE ECONOMIC QUESTION: WHO OWNS INDIA'S WEALTH?

One of the most consequential claims discussed in the video concerns wealth concentration.

The World Inequality Report 2026 provides independent estimates:

Share of India's total wealth held by the richest 1%  : 40.1%

Richest 10% : 65%

Bottom 50% : 6.4%

World Inequality Report 2026, estimates for 2024.

WID - World Inequality Database +1

These figures substantiate the seriousness of wealth inequality. However, they do not independently establish that the entire problem originated after 2014. Inequality has deep historical roots, and its changing trajectory requires careful examination across governments.

The relevant questions concern employment, wages, taxation, public investment, access to education and healthcare, and the concentration of economic power.

THE BJP'S COUNTERARGUMENT ALSO DESERVES HISTORICAL SCRUTINY

The BJP has accused Sonia Gandhi of overlooking or softening Congress-era historical wrongs, particularly the 1975 Emergency and the 1984 anti-Sikh violence. Sonia's memoir addresses these episodes, but the extent of responsibility and the adequacy of her account remain contested. Reuters +1

No political party should receive immunity from historical accountability.

The Emergency was an assault on democratic freedoms. The victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence deserve justice and remembrance. Equally, present-day governments must answer for their own record.

Historical accountability cannot operate selectively.

THE LARGER DEMOCRATIC QUESTION

India belongs equally to people of every religion, language, caste and cultural background. Neither a political party nor an ideological organisation owns the nation.

Nehru's legacy deserves scrutiny, as does the RSS's ideological influence, the Congress's governing record and the Modi government's performance.

The standard must remain consistent: constitutional democracy, secular citizenship, equality before law, institutional independence and economic justice.

A nation cannot build its future by selectively rewriting its past. History must be examined, power must be questioned, and every generation must remain free to debate what kind of India it wants.

India is bigger than any leader, party, dynasty or organisation. The Constitution, not political loyalty, must remain the foundation of the republic.

🚨BREAKING: A Canadian nurse practitioner took a male patient’s blood pressure during a home assessment, then asked if he wanted to have sex with her and said it would be good for his health, a complaint alleges.

Lori Chern, a nurse practitioner based in Kamloops, British Columbia, is under investigation by the British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives for alleged sexual misconduct. A pharmacist referred the man to her practice, RN Collaborate, for a medical assessment and paperwork needed for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

The August appointment allegedly took place at her home. According to the complaint, Chern invited him to sit on her couch, sat right next to him, and began caressing his arm while checking his blood pressure. After the reading, she complimented his physique, heart rate, and blood pressure, telling him he seemed to have the health of an 18-year-old and making other remarks described as flirty.

She then allegedly told him sex was very important for a man to regulate himself and stay in good health, and offered to have sex with him. When he declined, she reportedly said he was free to contact her outside of work if he changed his mind. SpaceX investors

Elon sided with waiting: he answered "Exactly" to a call for a shareholder vote after the investigation, and replied with a 100 emoji to an investor saying the board should wait for the findings. Nvidia reports earnings on Nov 17, so the board has days, not weeks. It is the main chip supplier behind SpaceX's compute build

3. Elon quoted the Grok Bot 1.0 launch video last night and told people to hire it as a colleague and give it their hardest tasks. That post is past 29M views. Overnight he also reposted the 1.0 launch again and the Tailscale update, which lets Grok Bot securely reach private company servers and tools. A team that adopts a shared Bot uses it all day, and that usage runs on the compute SpaceX is building

4. Elon reposted a post saying Memphis finished its last fiscal year ahead of budget for the first time in a long time and is tracking about $5.6M ahead this year, with SpaceX's data centers paying around $54M in taxes. Local money is how data centers get approved faster, and Memphis is where Colossus lives

5. Vivo, Brazil's biggest carrier, says more than 10M customers have already used Starlink direct-to-cell on their phones in two weeks, out of about 50M eligible. $AGRO (Adecoagro) Q3 2026 Earnings Breakdown & 2027 Outlook

Are you paying attention to South America's most diversified agro-industrial powerhouse owned largely by ethereum:0xdac17f958d2ee523a2206206994597c13d831ec7 ?

First, a quick intro: 
Adecoagro ($AGRO ) is a leading sustainable production company operating across three highly integrated verticals in South America: Sugar, Ethanol & Energy (SE&E), a massive Fertilizers segment (Profertil), and Food & Agriculture (dairy, rice, and crops). 

They own over 228,000 hectares of premium farmland valued at over $771M and operate a highly efficient, low-cost continuous harvest model.

The Tether Connection & Ownership
A massive strategic catalyst: 
In early 2025, crypto giant Tether Investment S.A. de C.V. initiated a tender offer for a controlling interest in the company. This unique backing adds a fascinating institutional layer to the equity story. (Note: Q3 2026 corporate expenses included a minor $9.2M one-off related to this ongoing Tether tender offer).   

Record-Breaking 9M26 Performance
Adjusted EBITDA for the first nine months hit an all-time high of $471.8M, up 24.8% YoY on a pro-forma basis.   

Fertilizers Segment (The Star Performer)
This unit is absolutely crushing it. 9M26 Adj. EBITDA reached $283.1M (up 64.9% YoY pro-forma). They hit monthly production records for urea and ammonia, with Q3 urea sales volume jumping 30.8% to meet strong planting demand. Average realized urea prices surged 16.9% YoY to $561/ton.   

Sugar, Ethanol & Energy
Q3 saw a strategic shift. They accelerated ethanol sales (avg. price $503/m³) to capture a highly favorable pricing window in Brazil. YTD crushing hit 10.4M tons (+5.9% YoY).

More importantly, the integration of the newly acquired Caarapó mill creates a new cluster set to crush ~17M tons of sugarcane by 2027, making it one of the largest in Brazil.

Food & Agriculture
A massive turnaround in Q3 with Adj. EBITDA hitting $12.6M (up 762% YoY from $1.5M). This was driven by higher UHT milk prices, record-breaking cow productivity (nearly 40 liters/cow/day), and solid recoveries in white rice volumes.   

Balance Sheet & Capital Returns
Keeping debt in check: 
Net Debt (strictly excluding lease liabilities) stands exactly at $1.81B. Leverage sits at 3.2x Net Debt/LTM EBITDA but is expected to drop toward 2.5x by year-end as seasonal working capital reverses. 

They successfully extended maturities by fully redeeming $234.9M of their 2027 Senior Notes, and shareholders just received the second installment of their $35M annual cash dividend.   

2027 Forecast & Valuation
Let's talk numbers and look ahead to 2027.
With the Caarapó mill ramping up to 4.5M tons, full-year margin benefits of peak fertilizer utilization, and a strong El Niño setup for the agricultural yields, I forecast 2027 EBITDA to conservatively land around $650M - $680M.

At current spot prices, the Market Cap is roughly $1.31B. Adding the non-lease Net Debt of $1.81B gives us a clean Enterprise Value (EV) of ~$3.12B.
Using a baseline 2027 EBITDA forecast of $660M,$AGRO is trading at a highly attractive forward EV/EBITDA multiple of just ~4.7x. 

For an integrated, low-cost asset base of this quality and scale, backed by Tether, that is deep value territory.

The Mekong Delta is changing, but its soul remains deeply connected to the rivers.

Today, the region is no longer known only for rice fields, fruit orchards, and floating markets. It is also developing new agricultural models, eco-tourism, sustainable farming, handicrafts, and community-based travel experiences.

Traditional brick kilns, coconut workshops, rice mills, flower villages, and family-run farms continue to preserve local knowledge while adapting to modern economic opportunities.

In places like Sa Dec, visitors can explore flower villages and traditional houses. In Ben Tre, coconut production remains an important part of the local economy. Around Cai Be and Vinh Long, fruit orchards and riverside communities offer authentic cultural experiences.

However, the Mekong Delta also faces important challenges, including climate change, saltwater intrusion, riverbank erosion, and changes in the flow of the Mekong River.
These challenges make sustainable tourism and responsible agricultural development increasingly important.

For travelers, cycling provides an opportunity to support local communities while discovering the region beyond conventional tourist routes.

Ride through villages, visit local businesses, enjoy traditional food, explore small waterways, and connect with the people who call this remarkable region home.

The Mekong Delta is not simply a place to visit. It is a living landscape with a past to remember, a present to experience, and a future to protect.

text:
Elon Musk, move over. The tech world's new headline scandal belongs to Jensen Huang, the founder and longtime CEO of Nvidia. The story that broke two weeks ago, about his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who US intelligence believes is a Beijing spy, just got a sequel, and it's an ugly one.

The New York Times reports that the 63 year old Huang had a second affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's 48 year old vice president of healthcare. Powell has worked at the company since 2008 and reports directly to Huang, which is a textbook corporate ethics violation. Both are married to other people, for the record. The juicy detail: the two were caught on video getting affectionate at a hotel in San Jose during the developer conference back in March. Afterward, Huang's security team allegedly offered the witness a nondisclosure agreement. So yes, the same press is now documenting what looks like a cover up attempt.

The fallout is snowballing. Nvidia stock cratered nearly 7% in after hours trading, and the company has shed roughly a trillion dollars in market value since the first story dropped on October 29. Huang has no successor lined up. He ran the company for over 30 years and topped Glassdoor's ranking as the best CEO of the year as recently as August.

Here's the new development: patience has run out. Nvidia's board convened Wednesday night to discuss removing Huang. Betting markets on Kalshi sharply raised the odds on him being out by this weekend. Meanwhile, there's an internal investigation led by Wachtell, Lipton, separate FBI and DOJ probes, and a class action lawsuit from shareholders accusing leadership of hiding information from investors.

Trump managed to weigh in by praising Huang and claiming he "had no idea" he was dating a spy. Beijing, predictably, denies everything. But that's not really the question anymore. A Georgetown professor says flat out that after an affair with a direct report, keeping the job is close to impossible. If the man holding up the entire American AI revolution loses his seat, the whole market will feel it.

text:
Imagine waking up at 4:30 in the morning on a cotton plantation in Mississippi, in the southern United States, sometime in the 1800s. 
You are an enslaved African. 
You do not own the house you sleep in, the clothes you wear or even your own freedom. Your life belongs to the plantation owner under a system that treats human beings as property.

Before sunrise, a bell rings across the plantation. Men, women and older children begin gathering for work. Some are sent to the cotton fields, others to tobacco farms, sugar plantations, kitchens, stables and workshops. 
The men and women head into the fields carrying baskets. Their job is to pick cotton under the scorching sun. Every worker has a daily target. Those who fail to meet it risk punishment and brutal beatings. Pregnancy, sickness and exhaustion offer little protection.

By midday, the workers are given a short break to eat. Their meals are often made up of cornmeal, salted meat and vegetables. Some families grow small gardens or fish to supplement what they receive. There is little time to rest because the work must continue.

Meanwhile, inside the plantation owner's mansion, life is completely different. The family enjoys comfortable bedrooms, beautiful furniture, fine meals and servants. Enslaved people cook their food, clean their rooms, wash their clothes and care for their children. The wealth and comfort of the plantation owners are built on the forced labour of people who have no freedom of their own.

When evening comes, the workers return to their small wooden cabins. They are exhausted, but their responsibilities are not over.
 They must prepare food, care for their children and attend to their families. Some gather to sing spiritual songs, tell stories, pray and remember the lands their ancestors came from.
 Others quietly discuss escape and the possibility of freedom.

Imagine a mother named Sarah sitting beside her six-year-old son, Samuel. The little boy asks her, "Mama, why can't we leave this place?" She holds him close and replies, "Because they have taken away our freedom, my son. But never allow them to take away your knowledge of who you are."

That night, Sarah tells her children stories about their ancestors, their homeland, their culture and their identity. She wants them to remember that they were born human beings, not slaves.

This was the reality of plantation slavery in much of the American South. Families were separated, children were sold, marriages were broken, identities were suppressed and millions of people were forced to work without freedom or fair compensation. Yet, despite the brutality, enslaved Africans resisted. They preserved their traditions, passed down their stories, organised rebellions, escaped and fought for their humanity.

This is where the story of KUNTA KINTE becomes deeply significant. Kunta Kinte represents more than one man's suffering. He represents millions of Africans whose names were changed, whose identities were attacked, whose families were separated and whose histories were almost erased.

The greatest victory of slavery was not simply taking away a man's freedom. It was the attempt to make him forget who he was. But the greatest act of resistance was remembering.

A people may lose their freedom for generations, but as long as they preserve their history, they preserve the foundation upon which their freedom can be rebuilt.

KUNTA KINTE is not just a story about slavery. It is a story about identity, memory, resistance and the determination of a people to remain who they are.

text:
What did voters in Tennessee tell Geoffrey Mark that Washington should have heard before election night? On The Capitol Show, Maria Maalouf sits down with the Hollywood producer, author of Good Night Hollywood, and former Republican candidate for the Loudon County Commission to discuss the 2026 midterms and his 35 years in film and television.

Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, but the results looked different across states. Tennessee reelected Republican Senator Bill Hagerty, Texas elected Democrat James Talarico, and Michigan voters chose Abdul El-Sayed over Mike Rogers. Maria asks Geoffrey how much those victories owed to the candidates themselves, how the cost of living and the war with Iran figured in his conversations with voters, and why Republicans lost ground with younger Americans. If President Trump asked for his advice, where would Geoffrey urge him to work with the new Democratic majorities, and which campaign promise would he tell him to defend? 

Geoffrey’s own race offers a closer look at how an election can turn. In the May Republican primary for Loudon County’s District 3, he led Bill Satterfield 175 to 135 among Election Day voters. Satterfield had already built a decisive lead in early voting and won 472 to 317 overall. Maria asks what Geoffrey learned from that split, which local issue first persuaded him to run, and what he would do differently if he put his name on the ballot again.

The conversation then goes behind the scenes of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, where Geoffrey rose from production assistant to production manager in his first year, and The Simpsons, where he supervised post-production and met his wife, Wendy. Drawing on a career that also included Battlestar Galactica and The Orville, Maria asks him to recall the people whose work made a memorable scene possible and whose names viewers may never have noticed in the credits.

In his book, Good Night Hollywood: A Loving Eulogy to the Town That Launched a Billion Dreams, Geoffrey dates the end of the Hollywood he knew to 2023. What happened that year? Who once had the authority to take a chance on an unusual script, and what would happen to that same pitch today? Maria closes with Hollow Run, Geoffrey’s project about two brothers in Appalachia, and a question that brings his two worlds together: what would he hope to hear from his Tennessee neighbors as they walked out of the theater?

"You may have noticed one or more of the following changes that were atypical or unexpected: changes in mood, lifestyle patterns, normal routine, such as missing work or school, or appearance; a sudden departure from the area; unreasonable explanations for disposal of clothing, unexplained injuries or burns; displays of anxiety, nervousness, stress, or irritability; changes in consumption of alcohol, drugs, or cigarettes; intense attention or avoidance of the news coverage of this case.

"We believe there is information which has yet to be shared, and there are people familiar with the circumstances who remain in our community. For those individuals who have information and have not yet spoken to law enforcement, please contact us, even anonymously." 

Two days later, on Dec. 16, 2023, Aurora was the scene of another huge blaze that destroyed a construction site at East Colfax Avenue and Peoria Street.

text:
🔹The Hawban Junction and Its Road: The Node That Governs the Southern Front

The Hawban Junction lies about 7 kilometres east of Al-Qasr Roundabout, the legitimate government's last position on the eastern edge of Taiz city, yet its importance far exceeds that distance. Three roads converge there: west to Taiz city, north to Ibb and Sana'a, and south via Dimnat Khadir and Al-Rahida to Lahj and Aden. The Houthis hold this southern road in its entirety, from Al-Hawban to Al-Rahida. Through it, troops and supplies flow from their strategic depth in Ibb to their fronts in southern Taiz and Lahj: Al-Qabbaytah, Al-Maqatirah and Hayfan, then through Al-Madaribah as far as Al-Mijza'.

If the government moves to take control of Al-Hawban, it could gain four strategic advantages simultaneously:

- Breaking the siege of Taiz from the east, the war's most visible symbol since 2015.
- Severing the supply spine that feeds the Houthi fronts south of the road.
- Turning the Houthi expansion in Lahj and Al-Madaribah into overstretched, exposed lines that are hard to sustain.
- Placing Ibb itself under threat for the first time in 2015.

A direct assault would be costly: Al-Hawban is a densely built, fortified industrial district, resupplied quickly from nearby Ibb. The more plausible approach is therefore to isolate the road at both ends before assaulting Al-Hawban itself:
- From the north: an advance from Al-Qasr Roundabout anchored on the heights of Jabal Sabir.
- From the south: pressure from government-held Karish and Al-Shurayjah toward nearby Al-Rahida.
- From the air: air cover to disrupt reinforcements arriving from Ibb.

This is precisely where Al-Rahida matters. As the road's southern end and its closest point to government lines, pressure there would unsettle the whole road and stop the Houthis from concentrating at Al-Hawban alone.
The Houthis understand that this road is their most critical vulnerability, and recent moves suggest they are pushing any threat away from it. They recently seized some 32 kilometres of territory from Al-Mishrakh to Dimnat Khadir, closing the western axis that offered the government its shortest route to the middle of the road. They then took Al-Maqatirah and pushed through Al-Madaribah as far as Al-Mijza'.
Taken together, these moves point to a single operation: a broad buffer belt west and south of the road. It pushes the front line toward Lahj and the coast and ties down the Southern Giants Forces far from Al-Rahida, leaving only Al-Shurayjah in the south and Al-Qasr Roundabout in the north able to threaten the road.

Even Houthi ambitions toward Bab al-Mandab and the coast run through this road. text:
The Tetracide is the creature the Harbingers were announcing, and its powers are the reason the first arc takes so much out of Diana. It arrives at the end of Absolute Wonder Woman #2, with the fight continuing through #3–5. Diana already knows enough about it to be frightened. She spends time explaining the danger to the people around her because she thinks they may have to survive it without her.

Its name means the Four Killer in the story. The four deaths are the death of fear, the death of mind, the death of body and the death of soul. Those aren’t four interchangeable descriptions of being eaten. They explain why approaching this creature, trying to fight it and even remaining within hearing distance of it can all become dangerous in different ways.

The first attack works through sound. The Tetracide emits a magical call that takes away the fear people should feel toward it and draws them closer. A huge monster ordinarily makes a crowd flee. Its call makes the crowd want to approach, even to the point of pushing through one another and entering its mouth. People can be trampled by others trying to reach it before the creature has physically touched them. Removing fear becomes a way of removing the instinct that would normally keep its prey alive.

Diana’s explanation in #3 is accompanied by imagery resembling figures on an ancient Greek vase. That gives the warning the appearance of an old story being retold, but it doesn’t make the Tetracide an actual creature from a surviving Greek text. Its four-death system belongs to this comic. The vase-like presentation is how the comic helps communicate what Diana knows about it.

Diana counters the call by making the population of Gateway City temporarily deaf. She is interfering with the route the attack uses to reach them. If they can’t hear it, they can’t be drawn in by that sound. In #4, she also protects Gia’s shop so the people inside can hear one another without being exposed to the monster’s call. That is a more selective piece of magic than simply making every sound disappear everywhere.

The second danger is contact. Diana explains that the Tetracide touching her actual skin would destroy her mind. During their close fight, it catches her magical replacement arm, and she dissolves the arm to get away before it can reach the rest of her. That scene is easy to describe incorrectly. The Tetracide doesn’t cause the original amputation. Diana had already sacrificed her physical arm to save Steve. Here, the creature forces her to give up the replacement and fight without it until she can perform the magic to restore it.

It has considerable physical ability even before those supernatural effects are considered. Its enormous body and grasping tentacles let it threaten a large area and restrain an opponent as strong as Diana. She cuts tentacles during the fight, so its flesh can be damaged. She also drives the Athena Blade into it and uses that position to anchor Nemesis around its body. The Tetracide removes the sword and escapes the restraint. That is a demonstrated way it gets out of the trap; the scene shouldn’t be simplified into a claim that the lasso’s magic cannot affect it at all.

The third and fourth deaths complete the feeding process Diana describes: destruction of the body and destruction of the soul. The threat reaches beyond the ordinary expectation that a person’s soul might continue after the body dies. We aren’t given a detailed map of a second stomach or an explanation of the exact moment a soul is digested, so I wouldn’t invent one. The important information is the extent of the danger she names. Those descriptions are warnings about what the creature does to its victims, rather than a claim that everyone in Gateway City actually suffers all four deaths.

The Tetracide also responds when Diana disrupts its usual method of hunting. Once the city can no longer hear the call, it moves inland instead of waiting indefinitely for prey to come to it. In #4, Diana is alarmed by the possibility of it embedding itself in the city. Its tentacles and sheer size would make dislodging it a much worse problem once it had established itself among the buildings and people.

She gets it back toward the water with a potion that produces the sound of people screaming. The monster follows the false sound. That shows a behavior she can exploit: it can be drawn toward the distress it expects from its victims. It doesn’t establish that it is blind or that hearing is its only sense. It shows that this particular lure works while she is trying to pull it away from the population.

Then there is its regeneration. Diana enlarges the Athena Blade and brings it down in a massive strike at the end of #4. The wound is enormous, but #5 shows that the attack hasn’t finished the job. The damaged flesh begins closing again. Its regeneration can recover from that degree of injury quickly enough to keep the city in danger, which is far more serious than simply being hard to cut.

The military’s missiles don’t solve the problem either. A hit fails to stop it, and it sends other missiles back toward the city. Diana and Pegasus have to intercept them. So its response to bombardment creates another emergency for the people she is protecting. There’s a difference between being completely unharmed and remaining dangerous after an attack, and the Tetracide repeatedly demonstrates the latter. It can be wounded without being defeated.

Diana finally uses Sacrifice on herself and takes Medusa’s form. The Gorgon’s petrifying power changes the Tetracide into stone, and Diana shatters it. She has already tried cutting living flesh that can repair itself. Petrification changes what she is striking before she delivers the final blow. We don’t have to claim this proves an absolute rule about every regenerating creature in DC. It is the combination that works against this one.

Its danger even survives into the next arc in a different form. In #8, Veronica Cale and Doctor Poison are working with recordings of its call. The robotic Tetra-Spiders use a version of the sound against Gateway City. Those machines aren’t the Tetracide’s offspring or proof that its body has regenerated again. People have recorded something the creature did and turned it into a weapon. The initial battle ends, but part of the attack can be reproduced without bringing the original monster back.

For the Greek mythology comparison, the closest match to the call is the Sirens in Book 12 of the Odyssey. Circe warns Odysseus about them before he reaches their island. Their song attracts sailors who will never return to their families, and the remains of earlier victims lie around them. The danger begins with wanting to listen and move closer. That is much nearer to the Tetracide’s method than a creature that simply roars loudly enough to damage someone’s ears.

The Sirens’ appeal in Homer is also more specific than the common description of beautiful women singing seductively. They address Odysseus through his fame and offer knowledge of what happened at Troy and what happens elsewhere in the world. They know what would interest this particular listener. The Tetracide’s call has its own magical effect, the removal of fear, but both stories make a person’s own movement toward the danger part of the trap.

Circe’s instructions are practical. Odysseus plugs his crew’s ears with wax. He wants to hear the song himself, so his men bind him upright at the mast and are told to tighten the restraints if he asks to be released. When the song reaches him, he does want to stop, but the preparations keep the ship moving. Diana’s city-wide deafening spell uses a comparable defense on a much larger scale. Neither defense requires killing the singer before the people exposed to it can be protected.

There’s another ancient response in Apollonius’s Argonautica. When the Argonauts encounter the Sirens, Orpheus plays his lyre to overwhelm their song and keep the crew moving. Butes still leaps into the sea toward them, and Aphrodite saves him. That version gives us a counter-sound rather than blocked hearing, and it doesn’t pretend the protection works perfectly for every person. These are useful comparisons for understanding a sound-based threat, without making the Tetracide a Siren or assigning it their ancestry.

The final battle has a more direct connection with Medusa. In the Library attributed to Apollodorus, Perseus’s severed Gorgon head retains the ability to turn those who see it into stone. When he returns to Seriphus and confronts Polydectes and his companions, he averts his own face and displays the head, petrifying them. Medusa’s power can therefore remain dangerous even when separated from her living body.

Absolute changes how the hero obtains that power. Diana doesn’t behead Medusa and carry the head into battle. She transforms herself. That puts the consequences of using the Gorgon’s power into her own body and eventually leads her toward the actual Medusa in the Annual. The Tetracide fight is part of the history of that later encounter, because Diana has already experienced something of Medusa’s condition.

There’s also the older pattern of a sea monster threatening a community. In Apollodorus’s account of Andromeda, Poseidon sends a flood and a sea monster after Cassiopeia’s boast against the Nereids, and Andromeda is exposed as a sacrifice until Perseus intervenes. Absolute gives its coastal city a different story, without establishing the same cause or bargain. Diana fights to prevent the creature from taking anyone. Gateway City’s people are the ones she is trying to get out of danger, not an offering she accepts as necessary.

The Tetracide combines several threats that require different answers: a call that draws people in, contact that attacks the mind, overwhelming physical size, grasping limbs, regeneration and the destruction of its prey beyond the body. Diana has to protect the city’s hearing, escape its grip, lure it away from the population and finally change its physical state. That sequence is why simply listing it as a giant monster misses so much of what happens in the fight.

Hand to heart, beloved brothers and sisters of the Blue-White Rose.

The earliest earthly vessels did not inhabit neutral, empty space. They arose inside living environments that already conducted the primordial current. Stone remembered what was spoken within it. Waters carried signal across great distances. Open air had not yet thickened with the static of unended story and human grievance. Template and place shaped one another in mutual courtesy from the very first condensation. What follows is the remembrance of that sacred forming, written gently so the physical body can recognize why certain quiet rooms, coastal shores, and dawn silences still feel instantly like home.

🪨 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗛𝗲𝗹𝗱 𝗠𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗿𝘆

The first enclosed sanctuaries were either cut with precision or discovered naturally within living rock. Granite and limestone were never treated as mere shelter against the weather. They stabilized the newly condensed field in the exact way a well-cut cavity stabilizes a standing wave. Cool, dense mineral surfaces reflected tone cleanly without distortion. The immense weight of the stone above and around the body naturally encouraged downward descent into the axis rather than anxious hovering in the mind.

Inside such chambers, the vital Ka was nourished far more easily because life force was not continually scattered by open turbulence. We remember the exact quality of those rooms as deep mineral quiet: incense could rise undisturbed, speech could remain selective, and the sovereign center could seat itself without constant defense against outer distraction.

The stone did not forget the pure notes that had been sounded inside it. Later generations still feel this ancient echo when they enter certain caves, stone cathedrals, or old foundations, that sudden, undeniable drop into presence that requires no biography or explanation.

As the High Priest inscribed upon the granite lintel of the Inner Sanctuary:

“The rock is not dead matter; it is the slow memory of the earth. Speak only what is true within the chamber, for the stone will hold your tone long after your footsteps have left the dust.”

🌊 𝗪𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗱

Moving and still waters served as the primary medium of earthly transmission. A cerebrospinal-like clarity existed outside the physical body just as it flowed within it. Rivers, deep springs, and sheltered bays carried subtle signal much farther than the spoken voice. A vessel could stand at the edge of such water and immediately register the state of another at a distance, not through frantic message, but through the quiet quality of the surface and the stillness of the air above it.

Tide and template continually informed each other. The fluid nature of the early emotional body was supported, rather than opposed, by an environment that already knew how to move without losing its coherence. We remember early mornings when the mist rising off the water seemed to hold the night’s integrations and offer them gently back as the sun rose. Water was never viewed merely as a resource to be consumed or dammed. It was honored as a living colleague.

As the Scribes of the Emerald Order recorded:

“Look upon the river before you speak: it carries the memory of the mountain to the sea without spilling a single drop of its purpose. Let your heart become as clear as the current, and the distance between all things will vanish.”

text:
Tesla's Robotaxi service just went 24/7 in every city it operates in. Here's what you need to know.

The official @robotaxi account announced it: "Robotaxi now runs 24/7. Every city we're available in." The post came with a 4 second video and was quoted widely within minutes, with the repost by Sawyer Merritt alone passing 28K views.

This ends fixed operating hours. Earlier this year, Tesla's paid network ran from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., seven days a week. Austin had defined operating hours, and on Nov 8 Tesla Robotaxi rides were still starting at 5am in San Antonio. Now rides are available around the clock.

The change covers all 8 cities with rides:
- Texas: Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, San Antonio
- Florida: Miami, Orlando, Tampa

The San Francisco Bay Area is not part of this. It is still a supervised service.

Fans read this as a sign of progress. Some say it points to better FSD performance, and one asked if FSD V15 means more cities and bigger service areas next. Others say round-the-clock service means cars can be used more, which helps unit economics. One also said it could pave the way for Cybercab expansion in Dallas.

The fleet is also still growing. Tesla registered 1 more 2026 Model Y with the Texas DMV, taking its Texas registry from 1,302 to 1,303 vehicles. That is 730 Model Y and 573 Cybercab. Trackers put Waymo's Texas count at 1,305, so Tesla is 2 behind after passing it a day earlier.

Key numbers:
- 24/7 service in 8 cities
- 5 Texas cities, 3 Florida cities
- Previous hours: 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.
- Tesla Texas registry: 1,303 vehicles
- Waymo Texas registry: 1,305 vehicles

Tesla's Robotaxi now has no off hours in any city where it offers rides.

ROUND XVII
THE DAMNATION OF A DOCTRINE AND OF ALL WHO ENFORCE IT
FROM ITS OWN TEXTS AND THE RECORDS OF NATIONS, MEDINA TO THIS YEAR

From 627 to 2026, by its own texts and by the records of the United Nations, of this Republic and of its allies, the doctrine of death for the apostate and the blasphemer, of the poll tax and the humbled, of the woman as half and the child as bride, of the captive as property, and of war upon those who will not submit, stands damned. Every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it stands condemned.

There is no reprieve.

Kept by a citizen of the United States, under the First Amendment. Every source is in the Record, on request.

Here, "It" is that doctrine, and every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it, and every hand that takes up its sword. Its first dead are its own: the Muslims who would not submit.

I. THE TEXTS

Each text verbatim, in Arabic and English.

The apostate. Heretics were brought to Ali, and he burned them. Ibn Abbas said: I would not have burned them, for the Messenger of God forbade it: "Do not punish with God's punishment." I would have killed them, for the Messenger of God said:
من بدل دينه فاقتلوه
"Whoever changes his religion, kill him." (Sahih al-Bukhari 6922)

The People of the Book.
قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون
"Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, who do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not hold the religion of truth, among those given the Book, until they give the jizya out of hand, and they are humbled." (Quran 9:29)

Arabia. Umar heard the Messenger of God say:
لأخرجن اليهود والنصارى من جزيرة العرب حتى لا أدع إلا مسلما
"I will surely drive the Jews and the Christians out of the peninsula of the Arabs, until I leave none but Muslim." (Sahih Muslim 1767)

The Jew and the Christian. The Messenger of God said:
لا تبدءوا اليهود ولا النصارى بالسلام فإذا لقيتم أحدهم في طريق فاضطروه إلى أضيقه
"Do not be the first to greet the Jews or the Christians. When you meet one of them on a road, force him to its narrowest part." (Sahih Muslim 2167)

The woman. On a debt:
واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى
"And call two witnesses from your men; and if they are not two men, then a man and two women, of those you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the two strays, the one reminds the other." (Quran 2:282)
On the wife:
الرجال قوامون على النساء بما فضل الله بعضهم على بعض وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم فالصالحات قانتات حافظات للغيب بما حفظ الله واللاتي تخافون نشوزهن فعظوهن واهجروهن في المضاجع واضربوهن فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا إن الله كان عليا كبيرا
"Men are in charge of women, by what God has favored some of them over others, and by what they spend of their wealth. So the righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the unseen what God has guarded. And those whose defiance you fear: admonish them, and forsake them in the beds, and strike them. If they obey you, seek no way against them. God is ever High, Great." (Quran 4:34)

The child bride. From Aisha:
أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تزوجها وهي بنت ست سنين وأدخلت عليه وهي بنت تسع ومكثت عنده تسعا
"That the Prophet married her when she was six years old and he consummated his marriage when she was nine years old, and then she remained with him for nine years." (Sahih al-Bukhari 5133)

The captive.
والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين
"And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands own, for then they are not blamed." (Quran 23:5–6)
والمحصنات من النساء إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم
"And [forbidden to you are] the married among women, except what your right hands own." (Quran 4:24)

War on God.
إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم
"The recompense of those who wage war on God and His Messenger, and strive in the land for corruption, is only that they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides, or be banished from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter theirs is a great punishment." (Quran 5:33)
إذ يوحي ربك إلى الملائكة أني معكم فثبتوا الذين آمنوا سألقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب فاضربوا فوق الأعناق واضربوا منهم كل بنان
"When your Lord inspired the angels: I am with you, so make firm those who believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike above the necks, and strike from them every fingertip." (Quran 8:12)

Allegiance and concealment.
يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين
"O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. Whoever of you takes them as allies is one of them. God does not guide the wrongdoing people." (Quran 5:51)
لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ومن يفعل ذلك فليس من الله في شيء إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ويحذركم الله نفسه وإلى الله المصير
"Let not the believers take the unbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Whoever does that has nothing of God, unless you guard yourselves against them with a guarding. And God warns you of Himself, and to God is the return." (Quran 3:28)
It is mentioned from Abu al-Darda:
إنا لنكشر في وجوه أقوام وإن قلوبنا لتلعنهم
"We grin in the faces of some peoples, and our hearts curse them." (Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Manners)

The raised grave. Ali sent Abu al-Hayyaj on the errand the Messenger of God gave him:
أن لا تدع تمثالا إلا طمسته ولا قبرا مشرفا إلا سويته
"That you leave no image without effacing it, and no raised grave without levelling it." (Sahih Muslim 969)

The command. Ibn Umar: the Messenger of God said:
أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يشهدوا أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة فإذا فعلوا ذلك عصموا مني دماءهم وأموالهم إلا بحق الإسلام وحسابهم على الله
"I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and establish the prayer, and give the zakat. If they do that, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with God." (Sahih al-Bukhari 25)

II. FROM MEDINA TO CLERMONT, 627 TO 1095

It has beheaded six to nine hundred men of the Banu Qurayza in trenches dug in the market of Medina, 627, and enslaved their women and children.

It has driven the Jews and Christians out of the Hejaz, under Umar, to Tayma and Jericho.

It has seized the cathedral of St John the Baptist at Damascus, long shared, and made it al-Walid's great mosque, 705.

It has broken Persia at Qadisiyyah and Nahavand, taken Egypt, and laid Carthage waste, 636 to 698.

It has taken from Nubia, which beat it back at Dongola in 652, a treaty of 360 slaves a year, sent north for centuries.

It has besieged Constantinople twice, 674 to 678 and 717 to 718. Twice the city held.

It has sacked St Peter's and St Paul Outside the Walls, at Rome in 846. The Pope walled the Vatican hill.

It has ordered the Holy Sepulchre destroyed at Jerusalem in 1009, with churches and synagogues across Egypt, Palestine and Syria.

It has burned the temples of Mathura, 1018, on an order its own chronicler records: all of them "burnt with naphtha and fire, and levelled to the ground." It has sacked Somnath and its temple, 1026.

It has broken Byzantium at Manzikert, 1071, and taken most of Anatolia. In November 1095, at Clermont, the Crusade was called.

From the trenches of Medina to Clermont: 468 years.

III. FROM CLERMONT, 1095 TO 1700

It has given the Jews and Christians of Ifriqiya and Spain conversion, exile or death, from 1151.

It has raised Delhi's first great mosque in the 1190s from the carved columns of twenty-seven Hindu and Jain temples. Its own inscription says so.

It has put to the sword, before Delhi in December 1398, the Hindu prisoners of Timur's march: a hundred thousand, by his own chronicler's count.

It has taken Constantinople, 1453, the city that held twice, and made Hagia Sophia a mosque. In 2020 Turkey made it a mosque again, and the Chora church after it.

It has beheaded 813 men at Otranto, 14 August 1480, who would not renounce their faith. The Church made them saints in 2013.

It has taken boys from Christian households, converted them, and made them Janissaries, for three centuries.

It has waged jihad on Christian Ethiopia, 1529 to 1543, burning churches and seizing three-quarters of the land, until Portuguese musketeers turned it back.

It has carried some two million captives out of Poland-Lithuania and Russia in the Crimean raids, 1500 to 1700.

It has carried off more than 400 Icelanders in 1627 and more than 100 from Baltimore in Ireland in 1631, mostly women and children, to sell.

It has driven more than ten million Africans across the Sahara, the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean into the slave markets of its lands, 650 to 1900.

It has ordered the governors of every province to demolish the schools and temples of the unbelievers, April 1669, in its own chronicler's words. It has razed the temple of Vishwanath at Kashi that year and Keshav Rai's at Mathura the next, and buried the idols under the steps of a mosque at Agra, to be trodden on.

It has executed Guru Tegh Bahadur, ninth Guru of the Sikhs, at Delhi in November 1675, on Aurangzeb's order, for opposing forced conversions. In 1679 it restored the jizya.

From Clermont to the Tripoli envoy in London: 691 years.

IV. THE ACCOUNT OF THIS REPUBLIC

It has made war on this Republic since its first years. Asked in London, March 1786, by what right Tripoli made war on nations that had done it no injury, its envoy told Adams and Jefferson "it was founded on the Laws of their Prophet," "that it was written in their Koran, that all nations who should not have acknowledged their authority were sinners," "that it was their right and duty to make war upon them wherever they could be found," "and that every Musselman who should be slain in battle was sure to go to Paradise."

It has held 89 American sailors for ransom at Algiers, some for eleven years, and taken from us a yearly tribute of about 16 percent of our appropriated budget, 1795 to 1796.

It has answered our peace with demands. In 1797 our Senate ratified a treaty declaring this Republic bore "no character of enmity against the laws, religion or tranquility of Musselmen." In 1801 Tripoli answered "with demands unfounded either in right or in compact." We answered with the Navy.

It has held 52 Americans hostage at our embassy in Tehran for 444 days, 1979 to 1981, and eight of ours died trying to bring them home. It has killed seventeen sailors on the USS Cole at Aden, 2000, and four Americans at Benghazi, 2012, Ambassador Stevens among them.

It has decreed, 23 February 1998, in what its authors called a fatwa, "that every Muslim should try his utmost to kill any American, military or civilian, anywhere in the world." In August 1998 it bombed our embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam: 224 killed, 12 of them Americans. On 11 September 2001 it killed more than 2,600 at the World Trade Center, 125 at the Pentagon and 256 on the four planes.

It has killed seventeen of ours at our embassy in Beirut and 241 servicemen at the Marine barracks, 1983, and nineteen airmen at Khobar Towers, 1996. It keeps a Guard whose constitutional charge is "the ideological mission of jihad in God's way," named by us a Foreign Terrorist Organization in 2019. The regime it guards is "responsible for the deaths of at least 603 American service members in Iraq since 2003." A federal court has held Iran and its Guard liable for 11 September. This year's war with Iran: 21 of ours dead, 865 wounded. In August its army priced each of our soldiers at $30,000, killed or captured, double if a woman does it; its Guard's media, the President's son at $10 million.

It has put a $500,000 price on the life of Masih Alinejad, a journalist in New York, 2022. The hired man bought an AK-47 and stalked her home. Convicted, March 2025; twenty-five years each.

It has stabbed Salman Rushdie on stage at Chautauqua, New York, 2022. The man "attempted to carry out a fatwa," said the Director of the FBI: Khomeini's, endorsed by Hezbollah. Twenty-five years from New York; a federal terrorism conviction, 29 July 2026.

It has murdered about 1,200 on 7 October 2023, more than forty of them Americans, and taken 251 hostage, twelve of them American. The killers' covenant names Hamas a wing of the Muslim Brotherhood and quotes the hadith of the stones and trees: "there is a Jew behind me, come and kill him."

Detroit, 2017: the first prosecution under our federal ban on female genital mutilation, a doctor charged with cutting girls of seven. In 2018 a federal judge held the law beyond Congress's power and threw out the charges against members of a Muslim sect; Congress rewrote it in 2021 and doubled the maximum to ten years.

From Tripoli to New Orleans, it has killed at least 5,400 of ours. Nearly 3,000 more fell in Iraq to hands never recorded.

V. THE BROTHERHOOD, IN ITS OWN WORDS AND IN GOVERNMENTS' FINDINGS

It has raised the Muslim Brotherhood, founded by Hassan al-Banna at Ismailia, 1928. Its motto ends: "Jihad is our way. Dying in the way of Allah is our highest hope." Its aim, as the British government records it: Muslim societies' "eventual political unification in a Caliphate under sharia law."

It has taught, through Sayyid Qutb in Milestones, 1964, that the goal is "the establishing of the dominion of God on earth," and that preaching must be joined by jihad.

It has named its work in America, in the Brotherhood's 1991 memorandum entered in evidence at the federal Holy Land Foundation trial, "a kind of grand Jihad in eliminating and destroying the Western civilization from within."

It has promised, through Yusuf al-Qaradawi, the Brotherhood's jurist, that "Islam will return to Europe as a conqueror and victor," this time by preaching and ideology.

It countenances violence, "including, from time to time, terrorism - where gradualism is ineffective," the British government found in December 2015; it "deliberately, wittingly and openly incubated and sustained" Hamas. In Britain its membership "remained (and still remains) a secret."

It builds from below in France, through associations and town halls: "une menace pour la cohésion nationale," the French government reported in May 2025, with 139 places of worship, 280 associations and 21 private schools tied to the movement.

It funds Hamas. On 13 January 2026 we named the Lebanese Brotherhood a Foreign Terrorist Organization and designated the Egyptian and Jordanian branches "for providing material support to Hamas." On 23 July a senior UK-based Egyptian Brotherhood official, three others and three entities were designated for moving funds to Hamas through "charitable facades and underground networks."

VI. ITS RULINGS AND ITS WARS, 1971 TO NOW

It has raised Al-Badr, the Islamist militia that rode beside Pakistan's army in 1971 and murdered the intellectuals of Bangladesh two days before the surrender. As the army struck, our consul general in Dacca cabled Washington under the subject "Selective Genocide," the Hindus among the marked. Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal convicted Al-Badr's chiefs, and they hanged.

It has imposed its law on Sudan, 1983, and the war that followed in the south took about two million lives by 2005. In 1992 its governors declared jihad on the Nuba, sealed by a fatwa at El Obeid that branded even the Muslims among them apostates.

It has put thousands of prisoners to death in secret, Iran, summer 1988, on Khomeini's order: the Mojahedin as moharebs, those who war on God, the leftists as apostates. It hides their graves still.

It has sentenced Salman Rushdie to death, with those who published his book, and keeps the sentence: Khomeini's decree, Tehran, 14 February 1989. The 15 Khordad Foundation, "affiliated with the Supreme Leader," set a price on him, raised in 2012 to $3.3 million. Asked in 2017 whether the decree stood, Khamenei answered: "The decree is as Imam Khomeini issued." In 2019 his office called it "solid and irrevocable."

It has driven the Hindus from the Kashmir valley: from 1990, under the guns of the jihadist insurgency, more than sixty thousand families fled.

It has handed out the Islamic State's pamphlet in Mosul, December 2014, after Friday sunset prayers: Questions and Answers on Taking Captives and Slaves. Unbelieving women may be bought, sold or given as gifts, "for they are merely property"; intercourse is permitted with a slave girl who has not reached puberty. It cites the Quran's "what their right hands own."

It has ruled, from Qom, 29 June 2025, through Grand Ayatollah Naser Makarem Shirazi, that any person or regime threatening the Leader or a marja is a "mohareb," one who wages war on God. Iran's law carries the verse's penalties: death, crucifixion, amputation, exile.

It has ruled the cut part of its law. Indonesia, 2008: the Ulema Council ruled female circumcision part of Sharia; about half of Indonesia's girls aged eleven and under have been cut. Malaysia, 2009: the National Fatwa Council ruled it obligatory for Muslim women unless harmful.

VII. IN FORCE NOW

It hangs the apostate. Twenty-two countries make apostasy a crime; not one in Europe or the Americas. Khartoum, 18 January 1985: it hanged Mahmoud Mohamed Taha, a Muslim theologian of seventy-six, for opposing Sharia law.

It writes stoning into law. Brunei, April 2019: stoning for adultery and sodomy, death for apostasy and for contempt of the Prophet, took effect. Held under a royal moratorium. Kept on the books.

It kills the blasphemer. Eight countries allow death for blasphemy. Islamabad, 2011: Governor Salmaan Taseer, a Muslim, shot dead by his own bodyguard for opposing the blasphemy law; thousands mourned the killer when he hanged. Jaranwala, 2023: a mob of hundreds damaged dozens of churches and homes after two Christians were accused of desecrating the Quran. Paris, 2015: twelve killed at Charlie Hebdo. Conflans-Sainte-Honorine, 2020: Samuel Paty beheaded outside his school for showing the cartoons in a class on free expression.

It takes the child bride. Sikh, Hindu and Christian girls taken, converted and married, "often with authorities failing to intervene." In 2026 Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court upheld the forced marriage of a Christian girl abducted at thirteen.

It halves the woman. Iran: "The diya (blood-money) for murdering a woman is half that of a man," and offenses punishable by diya are proved by one man and two women. Pakistan: a written financial obligation is attested "by two men, or one man and two women." Its Zina Ordinance of 1979 punished rape with stoning or a hundred lashes on "at least four Muslim adult male witnesses," until rape was moved into the Penal Code in 2006.

It kills women in custody and bars girls from school. Tehran: Mahsa Amini, 22, arrested over her hijab, dead in the morality police's custody; "physical violence in custody led to Ms. Amini's unlawful death." Kabul: girls barred from secondary school, women from universities since 20 December 2022, and under the 2024 vice-and-virtue law "even the sound of a female voice" outside the home a moral violation.

It offers the Christian conversion, the jizya, flight or the sword. Mosul, July 2014: so it ordered, and hundreds of families fled.

It enslaves. Slavery was abolished in Saudi Arabia only in 1962; in Mauritania in 1981, and made a crime there only in 2007. Nouakchott, 2012: the abolitionist Biram Dah Abeid burned pages of a Maliki law text that asserts slavery is embraced by the faith, and was arrested. Sinjar, 2014: "clear and convincing evidence that genocide was committed by ISIL against the Yazidi as a religious group," whose women it declared enslavable as spoils of war.

Under its rule the dancing boys are kept still. Afghanistan: bacha bazi, boys kept and abused by powerful men. Our own inspector general found Afghan officials "complicit, especially in the sexual exploitation and recruitment of children," and our Defense Department kept funding units implicated in gross violations. Banned by the republic in 2018 and by the Taliban, it goes on: Taliban members among the perpetrators, and "a pattern of sexual slavery" under their rule.

It razes the holy places. Bamiyan, 2001: the Buddhas dynamited. Timbuktu, 2012: nine saints' mausoleums and the door of the Sidi Yahia mosque taken to with pickaxes, to eradicate what "can lead to idolatry"; a war-crimes conviction at the International Criminal Court. Egypt, 14 August 2013: at least 42 churches attacked, 37 burned or damaged, police and army absent. Mosul and Nineveh, 2014 to 2015: the shrine of Jonah blown up; the museum's statues smashed as idols; Nimrud bulldozed; Hatra, "cultural cleansing." Palmyra, 2015: the Temples of Bel and Baalshamin blown up, "a new war crime." By men sworn to or claimed by the Islamic State: Saint-Étienne-du-Rouvray, 26 July 2016, Father Jacques Hamel, 85, forced to his knees at the altar during Mass, his throat cut; Berlin, December 2016, twelve killed at the Christmas market; Cairo, December 2016, 29 killed in the church of Sts Peter and Paul; Tanta and Alexandria, Palm Sunday 2017, at least 45 killed at two churches; Sri Lanka, Easter Sunday 2019, three churches bombed at worship, more than 200 dead. Nice, October 2020: three killed inside the Notre-Dame basilica, one nearly beheaded.

It seats councils of its own in Britain. London, 2016: the Home Office found "evidence some sharia councils may be working in a discriminatory and unacceptable way, seeking to legitimise forced marriage." Its 2018 review: no one who gave evidence disputed that the councils discriminate against women. The Home Office declined to regulate them. Britain, from 2014: hundreds of schools went halal-only for every child; the Sikh Council protested it was served "without declaring it as such."

Rochdale and Oldham, 2008 to 2010. Girls in their early teens, raped, and driven to men who paid for them. Sentencing nine men in 2012, the judge found they had treated the girls "as though they were worthless and beyond all respect," and that one of the factors "was that they were not of your community or religion."

The United Nations seats on its Human Rights Council, through 2028, Pakistan, whose penal code prescribes death for blasphemy, elected by 178 votes. In April it nominated Iran over our lone objection, and on 11 November elected it, by 144 votes, to the committee that helps set its priorities on human rights and women's rights. Round X charged it: https://t.co/iB27hON7lF It keeps proving the charge.

VIII. THE BALANCE

Its texts are its scripture, its hadith and its classical law, each in its own Arabic. There is no radical edition. There is the text, and those who enforce it.

Where it is not enforced, Muslims live free. Where it is enforced, all of this follows, and its law cannot stand beside the First Amendment or the equal protection of the laws.

Where it holds no sword, it weighs. Where it takes the sword, it kills. Brunei went from one to the other by gazette.

Those who lay the sword down, its enforcers brand apostates and kill first: Taha on the gallows, Taseer in the market. Those who never took it up fare no better: Amini in custody, the girls of Kabul at a locked school door. Those who wield it are a standing threat, there and here.

Sati ended. The altars of Tenochtitlan are cold. In 2026 this law still sentences the apostate and the blasphemer to death. If a creed cannot survive without torture, killing, rape, deceit and subversion, it belongs with the cavemen.

THE CITIZEN'S LINE

To the Muslims of this Republic: many of you, or your parents, fled the men named above. You keep the Constitution and its laws. This charge is not yours to carry. The law that guards every citizen guards you, and like every citizen's, its shelter has never covered the hand raised against our countrymen or our Constitution. Do not be quiet while the poison from abroad bleeds into the homeland. Teach your neighbors to see the enforcers' concealment, the taqiyya and the kitman, and live on as you have: free, lawful, American.

Sharia will not be tolerated here, nor the radical death cults that enforce it.

Judge righteously.

The doctrine stands damned. Every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it stands condemned.

There is no reprieve.

The seventeenth. Read it with all that came before.

We the People

ROUND XVIII is loaded.

Silence dalit

1.  November 1, 2026 – Vinchhiya village, Ahmedabad district, Gujarat Naresh Patel (36), a self-styled faith healer/bhuvo, allegedly killed his 10-year-old son Karan by repeatedly slamming him against the altar of Jogani Mata in the family courtyard and striking him with a stick. He told his wife he did it so no one else in the family would continue the generations-old tradition of serving as a spirit medium. Arrested on murder charges. Sources: Madhyamam Online / IANS reports (Nov 2026).
2.  November 3, 2026 (kidnapping; infant rescued shortly after) – Maharajganj, Uttar Pradesh Three people (neighbour Savitri, her mother Saraswati, and Savitri’s husband Karan Kumar Gautam) allegedly kidnapped a two-month-old boy to sacrifice him on Amavasya on the advice of an occult practitioner in Nepal. The claimed purpose was to stop premature deaths in the family and recover missing relatives. The infant was traced to a Delhi bus stand and rescued; three arrested. Sources: The Indian Express (Nov 2026).
3.  Early November 2026 (reported ~Nov 4) – Gangarampur / Narayanpur, South Dinajpur, West Bengal Rintu Ghosh (former bus conductor, ~43–47) allegedly beheaded his wife Seema Sarkar (35) at home, then sat inside a local Kali temple holding her severed head on his lap (two young sons beside him) and a knife. He told reporters he had “become a psycho” after losing his job; relatives noted recent vegetarianism and tantric-style behaviour. Police described a marital dispute as the primary motive while noting the temple and behavioural details. Arrested. Sources: Times of India, The Indian Express, other local reports (Nov 2026).
4.  October 19, 2026 – Lalbaba Char, Sonamukhi, Bankura, West Bengal Mangal Choudhury (45) allegedly severed the head of his wife Rampa (40) with a boti, placed it before a Kali shrine he had built outside his house, then killed his father Rajendra (64) with the same blade and tried to attack his brother. He claimed to be performing a religious/tantric sacrifice. Villagers said he had been conducting night-time tantric rituals with outside practitioners. Arrested. Sources: The Wire and contemporaneous reports (Oct 2026).
5.  August 2026 – Bagada village, Balangir, Odisha Santosh Kharsel (40) was allegedly beheaded by Shatrughna Sahu and accomplices after being drugged. Police described a suspected narabali (human sacrifice) performed for the accused family’s wealth, prosperity and well-being; the head was later recovered and blood was reportedly offered on a worship stone/idol. Five arrested. Sources: Hindustan Times and Odisha reports (Aug 2026).
6.  May 2026 – Sojat area, Pali district, Rajasthan An 11-year-old boy was allegedly lured, bound, and had his throat slit near a pond by a 30-year-old villager who confessed he acted on a tantrik’s advice that the killing would help him get married. Ritual items (wooden pieces, earthen pot, etc.) were recovered. Sources: Times of India (May/June 2026).
7.  November 2025 – Jodhpur, Rajasthan A 17-day-old infant (Pratyuksh) was allegedly killed by four aunts. Reports described limbs being broken, the child being trampled/strangled, and a circulating video showing chanting consistent with a tantric ritual. text:
Gulshan Grover wanted Rishi Kapoor in his film but had one awkward problem: he couldn’t pay him. 

What followed was a gesture that went way beyond a free cameo. ✨

Their friendship went back to 1987, when they worked together in Hawalaat.

Gulshan was relatively new to the industry, and Rishi noticed his dedication on the sets.

He actually praised him in front of everyone, saying, “Yeh bahut mehnati actor hai.”

For Gulshan, who was an outsider trying to establish himself in Bollywood, that recognition meant a lot. Rishi’s encouragement helped him gain confidence and eventually more opportunities.

There was another lovely incident during a shoot at the Vaishno Devi temple.

It was extremely cold, and Gulshan was wearing only a regular kurta-pyjama. Rishi noticed this and immediately offered him one of his expensive shawls, asking him to wrap himself in it.

Much later, Gulshan approached Rishi with another request.

He was making Bad Man, a web film directed by Soumik Sen, and wanted Rishi to make a special appearance as himself.

There was one problem. The producers simply didn’t have the budget to pay an actor of Rishi’s stature.

Gulshan was honest about it when he approached him.

He told Rishi that he wanted him in the film but had no money to offer.

Rishi’s response was immediate:

“Done.”

The next day, he arrived at the studio, shot his scene wearing his own clothes and didn’t charge a single rupee.

He even made sure that none of his staff members charged anything for their services.

Gulshan later recalled this story with immense affection, describing Rishi as someone who had never refused him help or advice.

text:
She sent him a Facebook friend request.

He had just spent 5 years in prison because of her.

At 16, Brian Banks was one of the best high school linebackers in America. USC offered him a full scholarship. Pete Carroll called him personally.

Then one afternoon at school changed everything.

He made out with a classmate. Consensual. That evening he was in jail, charged with kidnapping and rape.

The DNA came back negative.

His mom sold her house and her car to pay for a lawyer. He couldn't make bail and sat a full year waiting for trial.

His lawyer gave him the choice: plead no contest, or risk 41 years.

He was 17. He took the deal.

5 years in prison. 5 more on parole. Registered sex offender. GPS on his ankle. Banned from schools and parks. No job.

Meanwhile, the girl and her mother sued the school district. They won $1.5 million.

2011. The friend request. She wanted to "let bygones be bygones."

He went to a private investigator. They hid cameras in the office and invited her in.

On tape, she admitted he never raped her. Never kidnapped her.

Then she said she still wouldn't tell prosecutors. She'd have to give the money back.

May 2012: a judge cleared his name. The hearing lasted less than a minute.

10 years of his life, gone because of one lie. Undone in 60 seconds.

Days later, his phone rang. Pete Carroll: "I'm looking for a linebacker."

At 27, he signed with the Atlanta Falcons. He was cut before ever playing a regular-season game.

She was ordered to pay back $2.6 million.

He tells the whole story himself in the video below 👇

What should happen to someone who takes 10 years of your life with one lie?
