ethereum:0xbb0e17ef65f82ab018d8edd776e8dd940327b28b  — THE FORGOTTEN GIANT OF WEB3 GAMING
⠀
A $140 MILLION cryptocurrency.
⠀
More than $1.4 BILLION in historical protocol fees.
⠀
A gaming ecosystem that once helped define an entire crypto cycle.
⠀
And a token trading 99.5% below its all-time high.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Axie Infinity demonstrated that blockchain gaming could attract global attention and generate substantial economic activity.
⠀
Yet its current monthly protocol revenue is only around $101,000.
⠀
And approximately 35% of its maximum token supply remains outside reported circulation.
⠀
Is ethereum:0xbb0e17ef65f82ab018d8edd776e8dd940327b28b one of the most overlooked gaming recovery opportunities?
⠀
Or is the market correctly discounting a business model that has struggled to regain its former scale?
⠀
Let's examine the fundamentals.
⠀
01 | WHAT IS AXIE INFINITY?
⠀
Axie Infinity is a blockchain gaming ecosystem built around collectible digital creatures called Axies.
⠀
Players can own, trade, breed, and use these NFT-based characters in games.
⠀
Its ecosystem includes:
⠀
• Axie Infinity: Origins
• Axie Infinity: Classic
• NFT marketplace infrastructure
• Axie breeding
• AXS staking
• Community governance
• Ronin ecosystem integrations
⠀
The project became one of the most recognizable examples of Play-to-Earn gaming.
⠀
But historical popularity is not evidence of sustainable future growth.
⠀
02 | THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER
⠀
November 12, 2026 snapshot:
⠀
AXS Price: ~$0.797
Market Cap: ~$140M
FDV: ~$215M
Circulating Supply: ~175.60M AXS
Total Supply: 270M AXS
Maximum Supply: 270M AXS
Circulating Ratio: ~65%
24H Trading Volume: ~$11.6M
All-Time High: $164.90
Decline From ATH: ~99.5%
⠀
AXIE INFINITY PROTOCOL:
⠀
30D Fees: ~$104,512
30D Revenue: ~$101,012
24H Fees: ~$3,260
24H Revenue: ~$3,031
Cumulative Fees: ~$1.414B
Cumulative Revenue: ~$1.413B
30D Tracked Tokenholder Revenue: $0
⠀
These figures reveal a project with an extraordinary historical revenue record but a much smaller current economic footprint.
⠀
03 | THE PLAY-TO-EARN LEGACY
⠀
Axie Infinity helped popularize the concept of earning digital assets through gameplay.
⠀
At its peak, players participated in a game economy involving:
⠀
NFT ownership.
⠀
Breeding.
⠀
Marketplace trading.
⠀
Token rewards.
⠀
And competitive gameplay.
⠀
But Play-to-Earn exposed a structural weakness.
⠀
If players participate primarily to earn tokens, the economy may depend on continuous new demand.
⠀
When new demand weakens, rewards and asset prices can decline.
⠀
A sustainable game must offer entertainment value beyond financial incentives.
⠀
04 | THE REVENUE COLLAPSE
⠀
DefiLlama reports more than $1.4 billion in cumulative Axie Infinity protocol revenue.
⠀
That is a substantial historical achievement.
⠀
But the last 30 days generated only about $101,000.
⠀
Annualizing that monthly figure produces approximately $1.21 million.
⠀
This is only an illustrative run rate, not a forecast.
⠀
The gap between cumulative revenue and current revenue is critical.
⠀
Historical revenue cannot be treated as recurring earnings.
⠀
And a business that generated enormous fees in a previous cycle may not regain those economics.
⠀
05 | THE NFT ECONOMY
⠀
Axie Infinity uses NFTs to represent game characters and other digital assets.
⠀
NFT ownership allows players to trade assets independently of traditional game accounts.
⠀
Potential economic activity includes:
⠀
Marketplace transactions.
⠀
Breeding-related payments.
⠀
Game-related purchases.
⠀
And other ecosystem interactions.
⠀
But NFT trading volume is highly cyclical.
⠀
An increase in speculative asset trading is not necessarily evidence of growing player retention.
⠀
Investors should separate genuine gameplay demand from financial speculation.
⠀
06 | THE RONIN CONNECTION
⠀
Axie Infinity has a close relationship with Ronin, a blockchain ecosystem originally developed to support gaming applications.
⠀
This provides infrastructure designed around gaming transactions and digital assets.
⠀
But investors must distinguish between AXS and RON.
⠀
AXS represents utility and governance within Axie Infinity.
⠀
RON is the native asset associated with the Ronin network.
⠀
Growth in Ronin applications does not automatically create proportional demand for AXS.
⠀
The two tokens have different economic exposures.
⠀
07 | THE AXS TOKEN MODEL
⠀
AXS is an ERC-20 governance and utility token.
⠀
Its documented functions include:
⠀
Staking.
⠀
Governance participation.
⠀
Marketplace payments.
⠀
Ecosystem rewards.
⠀
And participation in selected game-related activities.
⠀
AXS holders can participate in staking programs and governance mechanisms.
⠀
But owning AXS does not automatically grant a direct legal claim on all Axie Infinity revenue.
⠀
That distinction matters when evaluating the token.
⠀
08 | THE STAKING ECONOMICS
⠀
The official Axie Treasury dashboard reports approximately 44 million AXS staked in its latest displayed historical period.
⠀
That represents roughly 25% of reported circulating supply.
⠀
Staking can encourage long-term participation.
⠀
But rewards may be funded through token issuance.
⠀
Newly issued staking rewards are not equivalent to profits generated from customers.
⠀
Investors should examine:
⠀
Net token issuance.
⠀
Real yield after dilution.
⠀
Staking participation.
⠀
And the sustainability of rewards.
⠀
A high nominal staking yield does not guarantee a positive investment return.
⠀
09 | THE TOKEN SUPPLY QUESTION
⠀
AXS has a maximum supply of 270 million tokens.
⠀
Approximately 175.6 million are currently reported in circulation.
⠀
That represents about 65% of maximum supply.
⠀
The difference is approximately 94.4 million AXS.
⠀
At the current price, that difference represents roughly $75 million in theoretical token value.
⠀
However, this is not a confirmed amount of upcoming unlocks.
⠀
Noncirculating supply can include different categories of treasury holdings, allocations, and undistributed tokens.
⠀
A precise unlock calendar is required to estimate future selling pressure.
⠀
The key question is how much additional liquid supply enters the market and when.
⠀
10 | THE COMMUNITY TREASURY
⠀
Axie Infinity's Community Treasury receives economic activity associated with parts of the ecosystem.
⠀
Its design includes governance participation by AXS stakeholders.
⠀
This creates a potential relationship between the community and ecosystem resources.
⠀
But a treasury balance is not automatically a dividend.
⠀
It is not necessarily redeemable by individual tokenholders.
⠀
And governance rights are not equivalent to equity ownership.
⠀
Investors should distinguish treasury assets from directly distributable tokenholder cash flows.
⠀
11 | THE TOKEN VALUE-CAPTURE PROBLEM
⠀
This is the central investment question.
⠀
Axie Infinity can generate marketplace fees.
⠀
It can operate successful games.
⠀
And it can attract new players.
⠀
But those developments do not automatically produce equivalent AXS buying pressure.
⠀
The relevant questions are:
⠀
How much AXS is required for actual economic activity?
⠀
How much is purchased by users?
⠀
How much is distributed as rewards?
⠀
How much enters circulating supply?
⠀
And what economic rights do tokenholders actually possess?
⠀
Game success and token success are related, but they are not identical.
⠀
12 | THE COMPETITIVE CHALLENGE
⠀
Axie Infinity competes with:
⠀
• Traditional mobile games
• Other blockchain games
• Immutable gaming ecosystems
• Ronin-based applications
• Emerging Web3 gaming platforms
⠀
Its advantages include brand recognition, historical experience, and an established digital asset economy.
⠀
But gaming is intensely competitive.
⠀
Players can leave quickly when gameplay becomes repetitive or incentives weaken.
⠀
A successful comeback requires compelling games, not merely another token reward campaign.
⠀
13 | THE VALUATION QUESTION
⠀
Using the maximum supply of 270 million AXS:
⠀
$1 AXS implies $270M FDV.
⠀
$2 implies $540M.
⠀
$3 implies $810M.
⠀
$5 implies $1.35B.
⠀
$10 implies $2.70B.
⠀
These are illustrative valuations, not price targets.
⠀
At $5, Axie Infinity would need to justify a fully diluted valuation near $1.35 billion.
⠀
That would require a substantial improvement in expectations for adoption, revenue, and token demand.
⠀
The previous $164.90 all-time high is not a reliable valuation benchmark.
⠀
The market structure and token supply are different from the previous cycle.
⠀
14 | THE BULL CASE
⠀
Axie Infinity launches or improves games that attract recurring players.
⠀
Player retention increases.
⠀
Marketplace activity recovers.
⠀
Breeding and game-related transactions expand.
⠀
Protocol revenue grows sustainably.
⠀
AXS utility becomes more economically meaningful.
⠀
And organic demand absorbs additional token supply.
⠀
Under this scenario, AXS could benefit from renewed interest in blockchain gaming.
⠀
But the recovery must be demonstrated through measurable activity.
⠀
15 | THE BEAR CASE
⠀
Play-to-Earn demand remains structurally weak.
⠀
Players prioritize traditional games.
⠀
Marketplace revenue stagnates.
⠀
New game launches fail to retain users.
⠀
Token distributions create persistent selling pressure.
⠀
And AXS continues trading primarily on its historical reputation.
⠀
A 99.5% decline from an all-time high does not guarantee that a token has reached fair value.
⠀
A large historical drawdown can coexist with weak fundamentals.
⠀
16 | THE FINAL VERDICT
⠀
Axie Infinity has several important strengths.
⠀
One of the most recognizable brands in blockchain gaming.
⠀
A functioning NFT economy.
⠀
A long operating history.
⠀
More than $1.4 billion in cumulative protocol revenue.
⠀
And an established governance and staking token.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
A $140 million circulating market capitalization.
⠀
Approximately $215 million in FDV.
⠀
Only $101,000 in monthly protocol revenue.
⠀
No tracked direct tokenholder revenue.
⠀
And roughly 35% of maximum supply outside reported circulation.
⠀
The next major catalyst isn't simply another GameFi narrative.
⠀
It's evidence that Axie Infinity can rebuild a sustainable player economy without depending primarily on token incentives.
⠀
Historical revenue demonstrates what the ecosystem once achieved.
⠀
Active players demonstrate current adoption.
⠀
Recurring fees demonstrate monetization.
⠀
But token value capture and future supply determine long-term investment returns.

Active addresses were approximately 3,135.
⠀
These are relatively modest levels of activity.
⠀
However, transaction counts alone cannot establish the success or failure of a gaming ecosystem.
⠀
Investors should also examine:
⠀
Recurring players.
⠀
Application revenue.
⠀
Digital asset transactions.
⠀
Developer retention.
⠀
And user acquisition independent of token incentives.
⠀
The strongest signal is sustained economic participation.
⠀
08 | THE ECOSYSTEM INVESTMENT MODEL
⠀
Beam's history through Merit Circle includes ecosystem investment and support for blockchain gaming projects.
⠀
This creates a different investment thesis from a blockchain whose value depends entirely on transaction fees.
⠀
Potential advantages include:
⠀
Strategic investments.
⠀
Developer relationships.
⠀
Infrastructure partnerships.
⠀
And ecosystem development.
⠀
But investors must distinguish between assets held by an organization and assets legally or economically attributable to tokenholders.
⠀
A treasury is not automatically redeemable equity.
⠀
And an investment portfolio is not automatically reflected in the native token's value.
⠀
09 | THE TOKEN VALUE-CAPTURE QUESTION
⠀
This is the central issue for BEAMX.
⠀
BEAM has network utility through gas, staking, delegation, and governance.
⠀
But that does not establish a direct claim on all ecosystem business revenue.
⠀
The investment thesis requires evidence of mechanisms such as:
⠀
Sustainable gas demand.
⠀
Staking requirements.
⠀
Executed token burns.
⠀
Recurring application demand.
⠀
And economically meaningful governance.
⠀
A successful gaming project within the broader ecosystem does not necessarily create proportional buying pressure for BEAM.
⠀
10 | THE SUPPLY STRUCTURE
⠀
Market data providers report approximately 50.3 billion BEAM in circulation.
⠀
Binance uses a reference maximum supply near 58.5 billion.
⠀
That places circulating supply around 86% of the reported maximum.
⠀
This is a relatively high circulating ratio compared with many newer crypto projects.
⠀
However, supply providers differ in their definitions.
⠀
Current total supply, maximum supply, historical burns, and circulating supply should be reconciled before calculating exact dilution.
⠀
A high circulating ratio reduces one form of supply uncertainty.
⠀
It does not eliminate selling pressure.
⠀
11 | THE BURN QUESTION
⠀
Beam has used token-burning mechanisms as part of its token economy.
⠀
Burns can reduce outstanding supply.
⠀
But investors should verify:
⠀
How many tokens were permanently destroyed?
⠀
Were burns funded by real revenue or treasury decisions?
⠀
Are they recurring?
⠀
And how do they compare with new issuance or token distributions?
⠀
Historical burns do not guarantee future burns.
⠀
The relevant metric is net supply change over time.
⠀
12 | THE COMPETITIVE CHALLENGE
⠀
Beam competes with:
⠀
• Immutable
• Ronin
• Avalanche gaming infrastructure
• Other EVM gaming ecosystems
• Traditional gaming platforms
⠀
Its potential advantages include existing ecosystem relationships and specialized infrastructure.

But competitors may offer greater liquidity, larger user bases, or stronger developer distribution.
⠀
Gaming infrastructure is a competitive market.
⠀
A functioning blockchain is not sufficient.
⠀
Beam must attract applications that people repeatedly use.
⠀
13 | THE VALUATION QUESTION
⠀
Using approximately 58.5 billion BEAM as a reference supply:
⠀
$0.005 implies ~$293M valuation.

$0.010 implies ~$585M.

⠀
The previous all-time high does not establish fair value.

Other November 11th Holidays:

Air Day - Air Day commemorates the launch of commercial inter-island air service in Hawaii in 1929. The observance highlights aviation’s role in improving transportation and connectivity across the islands. #AirDay 

Angola Independence Day - Angola Independence Day commemorates the country’s independence from Portugal in 1975. The day is observed with official ceremonies, cultural performances, and national celebrations. #AngolaIndependenceDay 

Bhai Dooj - Bhai Dooj is a Hindu festival celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters offer prayers and apply a ceremonial tilak to their brothers, symbolizing protection, prosperity, and long life. #BhaiDooj 
 
Bonza Bottler Day - Bonza Bottler Day is a lighthearted observance celebrated when the month and day numbers match. It encourages people to enjoy simple pleasures and find reasons to celebrate everyday moments. #BonzaBottlerDay 
 
Cartagena Independence Day - Cartagena Independence Day celebrates the Colombian city’s declaration of independence from Spain in 1811. Festivities feature parades, music, cultural performances, and community events. #CartagenaIndependenceDay 
 
International Energy Saving Day - International Energy Saving Day promotes energy conservation and the responsible use of resources. The observance encourages individuals and organizations to adopt practices that improve efficiency and reduce environmental impact. #InternationalEnergySavingDay 
 
International Pathology Day - International Pathology Day raises awareness of the important role pathologists and laboratory professionals play in diagnosing disease and advancing healthcare through scientific analysis and research. #InternationalPathologyDay 
 
National Education Day (India) - National Education Day commemorates the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, India’s first Minister of Education. The day promotes awareness of education's importance in personal and national development. #NationalEducationDay 
 
Poland Independence Day - Poland Independence Day marks the restoration of Polish sovereignty on November 11, 1918, after more than a century of foreign partition. The occasion is celebrated with patriotic ceremonies, parades, and cultural events. #PolandIndependenceDay 
 
Remembrance Day - Observed throughout the Commonwealth, Remembrance Day commemorates military personnel who lost their lives in service. Ceremonies often include the wearing of red poppies and a two-minute silence at 11 a.m. #RemembranceDay 
 
Saint Martin’s Day (Martinmas) - Saint Martin’s Day honors Saint Martin of Tours, known for his generosity toward the poor. Celebrations in many European countries include lantern processions, community gatherings, and traditional seasonal foods. #StMartinsDay

Veterans Day - Veterans Day is a U.S. federal holiday honoring all military veterans who have served in the armed forces. text:
A Veterans’ Day Message
From The Arizona Libertarian Party Chairman

We honor our Veterans (and all enlisted) by respecting their lives and not carelessly sacrificing them for special interest and exploitative gain. 

The most recent data* out of the VA (The U.S. Dept. of Veteran Affairs) notes that, after accounting for age differences, the ARIZONA Veteran suicide rate WAS SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER than the national Veteran suicide rate and WAS SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER than the national general population suicide rate. Someone I love struggles with this issue every minute of every day. They joined the Marine Corps because of their grandfather, my father, who served in WWII. They enlisted willing to sacrifice their life for honor and patriotism and came home feeling lied to. This story is far too common, and decades of hindsight regarding the negative repercussions of war have not informed present-day representatives sufficiently to avoid making the same mistakes with the lives of our younger generations. 

Once the most decorated Marine General, Smedley D. Butler wrote: "War is a racket. It always has been. It is possibly the oldest, easily the most profitable, surely the most vicious. It is the only one international in scope. It is the only one in which the profits are reckoned in dollars and the losses in lives." With General Butler, I say, "There are only two things we should fight for. One is our homes and the other is the Bill of Rights."

As I express my respect and appreciation for our Veterans (and enlisted who will one day be Veterans) I echo U. S. Army Air Force pilot, George McGovern's words, "I'm fed up to the ears with old men dreaming up wars for young men to die in."

DEFEND THE GUARD ACT

The Arizona Libertarian Party calls for an end to The War Party – “The United States should both avoid entangling alliances and abandon its attempts to act as policeman for the world.” (Libertarian Party Platform). Congress must reclaim its collective power to restrain the Executive Branch as was intended by The U.S. Constitution and its Founders. 

“The Constitution vests the power of declaring war in Congress; therefore, no offensive expedition of importance can be undertaken until after they shall have deliberated upon the subject and authorized such a measure.” -George Washington

“The Constitution supposes, what the History of all Governments demonstrates, that the Executive is the branch of power most interested in war, and most prone to it. It has accordingly with studied care vested the question of war to the Legislature.” -James Madison, The Father of the Constitution

“We have already given in example one effectual check to the dog of war by transferring the power of letting him loose from the Executive to the Legislative body. . .” and “Considering that Congress alone is constitutionally invested with the power of changing our condition from peace to war, I have thought it my duty to await their authority for using force in any degree which could be avoided.” -Thomas Jefferson, The author of the Declaration of Independence

The Arizona Libertarian Party continues to support the Defend The Guard Act, and will continually strive for the just treatment and care of those individuals who offered to or actually made the ultimate sacrifice in service of their fellow countrymen and women. 

The American Legion daily toast to Veterans every day at 7pm:
To Those That Went!
To Those That Are There Still!
To Those That Have Not Returned!
To Those That Never Will!
We salute you.

In Liberty,
Dru Heaton, AZLP Chairman

*2026 report is based on 2024 data. 
#DefendTheGuard 
#WarIsARacket

Fictional Obituary: Martha Kent (Absolute Superman comic spoilers)

Martha Kent of Smallville has died in her sleep. She had been living in a nursing home and was preceded in death by her husband, Jonathan.

Together, Martha and Jonathan offered shelter to Kal-El after his arrival on Earth. He came to them carrying a history and losses they had not shared, and they gave him care at a time when he had little reason to expect safety. Their time together was interrupted, but Martha continued to regard him as her son.

Illness affected her later years. Even as dementia made familiar things harder to hold on to, she spoke of him during her lucid moments. She also began making a suit for him, entrusting it to a nurse so that he would receive it when he returned.

The sewing remained unfinished when she died. Kal-El arrived afterward and was given what she had made, a final expression of the welcome she and Jonathan had offered him years earlier.

Martha leaves her memory with the young man she loved as a son. The home she helped give him lasted in his life long after he could safely remain in it.

text:
Renly had zero claim. And he knew it. That is what makes his story so tragic.

By every law in Westeros, Stannis was the rightful heir after Robert died. Robert had no trueborn sons—Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen were Jaime Lannister’s bastards. The throne belonged strictly to the next oldest Baratheon brother: Stannis.
Renly was the younger brother. He was fourth in line at best. He had no legal right to sit on the Iron Throne.
So why did he think he could take it?
Because Renly understood the cold truth Stannis refused to see: In Westeros, law doesn’t make you king. Armies do.
Renly built an unstoppable coalition:
100,000 swords behind his banner.
 House Tyrell, bringing the endless food and wealth of Highgarden.
The Stormlands, uniting the martial strength of the east.
The love of the people, fueled by his charisma, charm, and youth.
Stannis, by contrast, had 5,000 men, a red priestess, and a personality that alienated every potential ally. Stannis had the law, but nobody liked him. Renly had no right, but everybody wanted him.
As Renly bluntly put it: "Do you think your brother's claim or your own gives you the right to rule? Might makes right in this world."
He believed power was a popularity contest—and if enough lords named him king, the crown was his. He was almost right. Had he moved faster, he likely would have seized King’s Landing before Stannis even set sail.
His fatal mistake was rejecting Stannis's ultimatum.
Stannis offered a generous compromise:
1. Bend the knee.
2. Be named heir to the Iron Throne (since Stannis had no sons).
3. Keep Storm's End and sit on the Small Council.
Renly mocked him. Overconfident in his 100,000 men, he assumed Stannis was powerless. He forgot that Stannis possessed a weapon no army could block: Melisandre and her shadow magic. One tent, one shadow, and the King with the largest army in Westeros was dead before the sun rose.
The Tragic Bottom Line:
Renly and Stannis together would have crushed the Lannisters in a week. Renly had the army; Stannis had the claim. United, they were unstoppable. But Renly’s ambition and Stannis’s unbending pride destroyed them both.

text:
“THE MYTH OF RUSSIAN INVINCIBILITY IS NONSENSE!”

Former U.S. presidential envoy General Keith Kellogg has delivered a sharp assessment of Russia's military capabilities, the negotiations in Abu Dhabi, and the approach taken by Donald Trump's negotiating team.

Kellogg warned that the talks were unlikely to produce a breakthrough. After two days of meetings, the fundamental disagreements remain unresolved. Moscow continues demanding Ukrainian territory it has failed to capture on the battlefield, while Kyiv has shown no willingness to surrender its land simply to satisfy the Kremlin.

There is, however, one potentially significant development. Ukraine and Russia have reportedly discussed preparations for a large-scale prisoner exchange, involving 1,000 or possibly 1,500 people from each side. The final numbers are expected to be discussed on November 12. For Ukrainian families waiting for their loved ones, this could be the most meaningful outcome of the negotiations.

Kellogg also challenged the exclusion of European allies from the main negotiating process. He believes France, Britain, and Germany must have a direct role in shaping any peace agreement. More importantly, credible security guarantees for Ukraine should include an actual European military presence on Ukrainian territory.

The general went even further, saying he trusts European countries more than the United States on this particular issue. Europe, after all, will have to live with the consequences of whatever agreement emerges.

His criticism extended to Trump's negotiating team. Kellogg explained that he initially handled both the Ukrainian and Russian portfolios before Trump transferred responsibility for negotiations with Moscow to Steve Witkoff. In Kellogg's assessment, commercial interests subsequently received increasing attention, even though the central issue is the survival of the Ukrainian people.

And then came his assessment of Russia's supposedly unstoppable military machine.

According to Kellogg, Russian forces are suffering at least 30,000 casualties every month, killed and wounded combined. Despite these enormous losses, Russia has managed to capture only about 1% of additional Ukrainian territory since the initial phase of its full-scale invasion.

That is hardly the record of an invincible army.

Diplomatic efforts are continuing. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are reportedly scheduled to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow on November 12, followed by talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin.

For now, there is no peace agreement. Russia's territorial demands remain unchanged, Ukraine's security guarantees remain unresolved, and European allies are still fighting for a meaningful place at the negotiating table.

But the possibility of a major prisoner exchange offers something tangible: the chance for hundreds of Ukrainian families to finally embrace the people they have spent months or years waiting for.

That would be worth far more than another round of diplomatic speeches.

Jawar Mohammed, on 9 October you said you had long opposed Abiy Ahmed’s hostile rhetoric over sea access and would oppose any Eritrean incursion into Ethiopia.

 Days later, you outlined an advance on Assab and warned it could provoke resistance and outside intervention.

 By 28 October, you told AFP it was time to use military force to secure sea access. Now, in The Day After Isaias, you say port access “must not be imposed through military force.” Which of your October positions are you asking readers to forget?

Reuters described you as a former ally who helped bring Abiy to power. You became a prominent opponent, were detained in 2020 and were still publicly criticising his government in late 2024. Now you ask Eritreans to trust his army to cross their border, help oversee a transition and leave their sovereignty intact. Eritreans are entitled to scrutinise the power you would have Abiy exercise in their country.

Your reading of the Horn is amateurish. You list risks in Tigray, Sudan and the Red Sea, then write as though Addis Ababa could manage them once its troops cross the border. You already conceded that Eritreans who oppose Isaias could resist a prolonged Ethiopian military presence.

 The G7 warned on 11 November that a wider war could endanger regional security, humanitarian operations and Red Sea trade. You have drawn two routes on a map. You have yet to explain why the region would follow either script.

The same rule applies in both directions. Any proven Eritrean incursion deserves condemnation. Asmara denied the reported October incursion, which Reuters could not verify independently. Even if an armed attack is established, self-defence under Article 51 must be necessary and proportionate.

 A border attack gives Ethiopia no licence to seize Assab for leverage or impose a government in Asmara. If Ethiopian forces exercise effective control over Eritrean territory without consent, the law of occupation applies, however brief the deployment.

You call Isaias an Egyptian proxy. Cairo and Asmara acknowledge cooperation, but you offer no evidence that Cairo directs Eritrean policy. In contrast Abiy is a known UAE proxy and responsible for the suffering of the Sudanese people, but it looks like accountability is on sight.

You say Ethiopia’s latest Tigray campaigns were viewed more favourably. By whom?The ENDF has committed unspeakable crimes across Tigray, Amhara and other parts of Ethiopia. Human Rights Watch also documented arbitrary detention and deportation of Eritrean refugees by Ethiopian security forces. That record belongs in any serious assessment of civilian protection.

Your refugee figures broadly check out. UNHCR recorded 181,264 Eritrean refugees in Ethiopia at the end of 2020 and 117,472 Eritrean refugees and asylum seekers on 31 October 2026.  Eritreans have every right to criticise their  government if any, but  they also have the right to decide who governs them.

You tell the story of Harnet, who understood what Eritrean independence meant without ever setting foot in the country. Take her seriously. Eritrea joined the UN in 1993. In 2018, both governments agreed to resume transport and trade links. Ethiopia could negotiate port access before your call for military action, and it can do so today. If your respect for Eritrean sovereignty begins after Ethiopian troops have crossed the border and reshaped the government, you have already decided how much sovereignty Eritreans get to exercise.

text:
mesh networks will become a hot crypto narrative in the coming days/weeks.

mesh networks is what?

move information over bluetooth.

send messages, and money without depending on the internet.

imagine a world where people could communicate, coordinate, and transfer value even when internet infrastructure fails, gets censored, or becomes too expensive to access.

of course, bluetooth has range limitations, and offline payments need mechanisms to prevent double spending before settlement.. but these are problems worth solving.

i think the speculative premium should be on the higher side for projects which manage to get real adoption.

building tech is not tough anymore.. getting people to use that tech is tough.

and this is where i think most crypto founders are missing a huge opportunity.

projects which run offline campaigns, creating an army of volunteers to increase downloads, connectivity, and actual usage of mesh network apps, will survive longer.

but these volunteers shouldn't be random mercenaries farming tokens.

they should be picked from early believers of the project.. people who understand why decentralized communication matters, and who are willing to spend time building local communities around it.

imagine volunteers setting up neighborhood mesh networks, onboarding merchants, teaching people how to send messages and payments, and helping others become volunteers themselves.

every contribution should be measurable.. but downloading an app shouldn't carry the same reward as bringing 100 people who actively use it.

rewards should unlock after reaching milestones.. and those milestones should measure retention, successful message relays, verified network coverage, and actual economic activity.

there should also be ways to prevent fake downloads, sybil farming, and artificial usage.

the interesting part is token economics.

redemption of rewards could follow a dynamic curve based on token supply, demand, and actual network utilization.

when demand for network services grows, the system could reward productive contributions more efficiently.. when speculative demand exceeds real usage, emission and redemption rules should become more conservative.

but the token shouldn't exist only to reward volunteers.

it should provide access to premium services, relay capacity, merchant tools, and other utilities within the network.

people should earn tokens by contributing something useful, and spend tokens because the network offers something valuable.

that's how you build a sharing economy around connectivity.

we spent years building crypto products which depend on the internet.

maybe the next wave is about making crypto useful when the internet isn't available.

and the biggest winners might not be those with the best technology.. but those who manage to organize the largest productive communities around it.

Did you know that the world-famous Dunkin’ Donuts empire was founded by an American entrepreneur of Jewish descent, William Rosenberg (1916–2002)

Born in Boston to a family of Jewish immigrants, Rosenberg grew up facing financial difficulties. He left school at a young age and started working to support his family.

In 1948, he opened a small coffee and donut shop called Open Kettle in Quincy, Massachusetts.

Just two years later, in 1950, he renamed it Dunkin’ Donuts — and the rest is history!

While most competitors offered only four varieties of donuts, Rosenberg offered an incredible 52!

In 1955, he began franchising his business, transforming a small local shop into a global brand with thousands of locations worldwide.

Today, Dunkin’ is one of the most recognizable coffee and donut chains on the planet.

A company built by a man whose family carried Jewish traditions and heritage across the ocean is embracing a Muslim holiday.

There is nothing wrong with respecting different religions and cultures. But it does raise an interesting question: what about the heritage of the man who created this empire?

One can only imagine William Rosenberg turning in his grave.

Oh, how times have changed

text:
OttoGeoGraphica
June, 2024
Potter Marsh Bird Sanctuary
Seward Highway
Anchorage, Alaska

When I reach Palmer, I need supplies from the nearest Walmart and I need a shower. I find no Pilot or Love Travel Centers in Alaska. Driving up the highway many communities in Canada have a  community recreation complex that offers showers, but I found no such thing in Palmer. There is a gym facility. I call them and they graciously offer their shower facilities free of charge. I am soon refreshed.

My first concern in Anchorage is to secure facilities for the night. I plan to be here for two days. I bypass the city and stop at a place called Potter Marsh, just to the south of town. I sign is posted with hours meaning the lot is gated and thus no overnight parking. No problem. The marsh is a bird sanctuary and there is a lengthy boardwalk high above the water that extends both westward and southward from the parking lot. Waterfowl aside, this is prime moose sighting turf. I see white birds in the distance, too small for albatross and egrets, possibly seagulls, but no moose. 

When I reach the end of the walk, two friendly old timers are sitting on a bench wearing matching jackets and guarding a high tech telescope resting on a tripod. Before I can fix my eye through the viewer, a bald eagle flies overhead and continues to nest near the boundary of the marsh. The nest is built on a tree that appears dead and on a branch much lower than the evergreens around it. 

When I return to the telescope, the parent is maneuvering around the three sizeable chicks waiting for some attention. I see no feeding and though the squawking is apparent, yet unheard, the parent brings nothing. It soon flies away again. I didn’t hear the men say when the birds had hatched, but it seems recently and they assured me that the chicks are growing fast. This is the fifth year the parents have sought this marshland for their brood. The parent soon returns but before it does I notice the bland color of the chicks: brown, gray, gray-brown. Their down is unkempt and in need of a comb. All three appear to be extremely well fed. 

I leave the tripod and travel back along boardwalk toward the south of the marsh. This portion borders Seward Highway and the Turnagain Arm of the Cook Inlet. And in the pools of the marsh two families of geese are living. Each family has five hatchlings and each brood appears to be the same age. Their down is more camouflaged to their surroundings. Each with a yellow-green streak fluff that matches the color of the marsh grass. They are well disguised and with each family, I had to search out the baby chicks, each well huddled close to their closest parent. Understandably so since they are potentially eaglet food.

On a single bench, another old timer sits, wearing the same jacket as those earlier two. I read the patch. It states: “Ducks Unlimited”. He informs me of the second goose family located over between the boardwalk and the highway, which I had already seen but do not want to admit to. I go back and visit the gooselings one last time. I return to thank him and discover that he is inviting conversation. Over the next half hour I discover that he panned for gold in Nome for years, that he loved and lived in Santiago, Chili and Ushuaia, Argentina, hunted in Tierra del Fuego and fished in the Straits of Magellan, and that he was caught in both the Chilean Revolution and the Falkland Island war between Argentina and England. He stated that because the Americans supported England in that war, he was untrusted in Ushuaia and feared leaving his residence after dark. He told me of a beautiful Chilean girl that was the love of his life. Regretfully, I never got his name.

text:
MIT Technology Review’s What’s Next series looks across industries, trends, and technologies to give you a first look at the future. You can read the rest of them here.

In an industry in constant flux, sticking your neck out to predict what’s coming next may seem reckless. (AI bubble? What AI bubble?) But for the last few years we’ve done just that—and we’re doing it again. 

How did we do last time? We picked five hot AI trends to look out for in 2025, including what we called generative virtual playgrounds, a.k.a world models (check: From Google DeepMind’s Genie 3 to World Labs’s Marble, tech that can generate realistic virtual environments on the fly keeps getting better and better); so-called reasoning models (check: Need we say more? Reasoning models have fast become the new paradigm for best-in-class problem solving); a boom in AI for science (check: OpenAI is now following Google DeepMind by setting up a dedicated team to focus on just that); AI companies that are cozier with national security (check: OpenAI reversed position on the use of its technology for warfare to sign a deal with the defense-tech startup Anduril to help it take down battlefield drones); and legitimate competition for Nvidia (check, kind of: China is going all in on developing advanced AI chips, but Nvidia’s dominance still looks unassailable—for now at least). 

So what’s coming in 2026? Here are our big bets for the next 12 months. 

More Silicon Valley products will be built on Chinese LLMs

The last year shaped up as a big one for Chinese open-source models. In January, DeepSeek released R1, its open-source reasoning model, and shocked the world with what a relatively small firm in China could do with limited resources. By the end of the year, “DeepSeek moment” had become a phrase frequently tossed around by AI entrepreneurs, observers, and builders—an aspirational benchmark of sorts. 

It was the first time many people realized they could get a taste of top-tier AI performance without going through OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google.

Open-weight models like R1 allow anyone to download a model and run it on their own hardware. They are also more customizable, letting teams tweak models through techniques like distillation and pruning. This stands in stark contrast to the “closed” models released by major American firms, where core capabilities remain proprietary and access is often expensive.

As a result, Chinese models have become an easy choice. Reports by CNBC and Bloomberg suggest that startups in the US have increasingly recognized and embraced what they can offer.

One popular group of models is Qwen, created by Alibaba, the company behind China’s largest e-commerce platform, Taobao. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct alone has 8.85 million downloads, making it one of the most widely used pretrained LLMs. The Qwen family spans a wide range of model sizes alongside specialized versions tuned for math, coding, vision, and instruction-following, a breadth that has helped it become an open-source powerhouse.

Other Chinese AI firms that were previously unsure about committing to open source are following DeepSeek’s playbook. Standouts include Zhipu’s GLM and Moonshot’s Kimi. The competition has also pushed American firms to open up, at least in part. In August, OpenAI released its first open-source model. In November, the Allen Institute for AI, a Seattle-based nonprofit, released its latest open-source model, Olmo 3. 

Even amid growing US-China antagonism, Chinese AI firms’ near-unanimous embrace of open source has earned them goodwill in the global AI community and a long-term trust advantage. In 2026, expect more Silicon Valley apps to quietly ship on top of Chinese open models, and look for the lag between Chinese releases and the Western frontier to keep shrinking—from months to weeks, and sometimes less.

—Caiwei Chen

The US will face another year of regulatory tug-of-war

T​​he battle over regulating artificial intelligence is heading for a showdown. On December 11, President Donald Trump signed an executive order aiming to neuter state AI laws, a move meant to handcuff states from keeping the growing industry in check. In 2026, expect more political warfare. The White House and states will spar over who gets to govern the booming technology, while AI companies wage a fierce lobbying campaign to crush regulations, armed with the narrative that a patchwork of state laws will smother innovation and hobble the US in the AI arms race against China.

Under Trump’s executive order, states may fear being sued or starved federal funding if they clash with his vision for light-touch regulation. Big Democratic states like California—which just enacted the nation’s first frontier AI law requiring companies to publish safety testing for their AI models—will take the fight to court, arguing that only Congress can override state laws. But states that can’t afford to lose federal funding, or fear getting in Trump’s crosshairs, might fold. Still, expect to see more state lawmaking on hot-button issues, especially where Trump’s order gives states a green light to legislate. With chatbots accused of triggering teen suicides and data centers sucking up more and more energy, states will face mounting public pressure to push for guardrails. 

In place of state laws, Trump promises to work with Congress to establish a federal AI law. Don’t count on it. Congress failed to pass a moratorium on state legislation twice in 2025, and we aren’t holding out hope that it will deliver its own bill this year. 

AI companies like OpenAI and Meta will continue to deploy powerful super-PACs to support political candidates who back their agenda and target those who stand in their way. On the other side, super-PACs supporting AI regulation will build their own war chests to counter. Watch them duke it out at next year’s midterm elections.

The further AI advances, the more people will fight to steer its course, and 2026 will be another year of regulatory tug-of-war—with no end in sight.

—Michelle Kim

Chatbots will change the way we shop

Imagine a world in which you have a personal shopper at your disposal 24-7—an expert who can instantly recommend a gift for even the trickiest-to-buy-for friend or relative, or trawl the web to draw up a list of the best bookcases available within your tight budget. Better yet, they can analyze a kitchen appliance’s strengths and weaknesses, compare it with its seemingly identical competition, and find you the best deal. Then once you’re happy with their suggestion, they’ll take care of the purchasing and delivery details too.

But this ultra-knowledgeable shopper isn’t a clued-up human at all—it’s a chatbot. This is no distant prediction, either. Salesforce recently said it anticipates that AI will drive $263 billion in online purchases this holiday season. That’s some 21% of all orders. And experts are betting on AI-enhanced shopping becoming even bigger business within the next few years. By 2030, between $3 trillion and $5 trillion annually will be made from agentic commerce, according to research from the consulting firm McKinsey. 

Unsurprisingly, AI companies are already heavily invested in making purchasing through their platforms as frictionless as possible. Google’s Gemini app can now tap into the company’s powerful Shopping Graph data set of products and sellers, and can even use its agentic technology to call stores on your behalf. Meanwhile, back in November, OpenAI announced a ChatGPT shopping feature capable of rapidly compiling buyer’s guides, and the company has struck deals with Walmart, Target, and Etsy to allow shoppers to buy products directly within chatbot interactions. 

Expect plenty more of these kinds of deals to be struck within the next year as consumer time spent chatting with AI keeps on rising, and web traffic from search engines and social media continues to plummet. 

—Rhiannon Williams

An LLM will make an important new discovery

I’m going to hedge here, right out of the gate. It’s no secret that large language models spit out a lot of nonsense. Unless it’s with monkeys-and-typewriters luck, LLMs won’t discover anything by themselves. But LLMs do still have the potential to extend the bounds of human knowledge.

We got a glimpse of how this could work in May, when Google DeepMind revealed AlphaEvolve, a system that used the firm’s Gemini LLM to come up with new algorithms for solving unsolved problems. The breakthrough was to combine Gemini with an evolutionary algorithm that checked its suggestions, picked the best ones, and fed them back into the LLM to make them even better.

Google DeepMind used AlphaEvolve to come up with more efficient ways to manage power consumption by data centers and Google’s TPU chips. Those discoveries are significant but not game-changing. Yet. Researchers at Google DeepMind are now pushing their approach to see how far it will go.

And others have been quick to follow their lead. A week after AlphaEvolve came out, Asankhaya Sharma, an AI engineer in Singapore, shared OpenEvolve, an open-source version of Google DeepMind’s tool. In September, the Japanese firm Sakana AI released a version of the software called SinkaEvolve. And in November, a team of US and Chinese researchers revealed AlphaResearch, which they claim improves on one of AlphaEvolve’s already better-than-human math solutions.

There are alternative approaches too. For example, researchers at the University of Colorado Denver are trying to make LLMs more inventive by tweaking the way so-called reasoning models work. They have drawn on what cognitive scientists know about creative thinking in humans to push reasoning models toward solutions that are more outside the box than their typical safe-bet suggestions.

Hundreds of companies are spending billions of dollars looking for ways to get AI to crack unsolved math problems, speed up computers, and come up with new drugs and materials. Now that AlphaEvolve has shown what’s possible with LLMs, expect activity on this front to ramp up fast.    

—Will Douglas Heaven

Legal fights heat up

For a while, lawsuits against AI companies were pretty predictable: Rights holders like authors or musicians would sue companies that trained AI models on their work, and the courts generally found in favor of the tech giants. AI’s upcoming legal battles will be far messier.

The fights center on thorny, unresolved questions: Can AI companies be held liable for what their chatbots encourage people to do, as when they help teens plan suicides? If a chatbot spreads patently false information about you, can its creator be sued for defamation? If companies lose these cases, will insurers shun AI companies as clients?

In 2026, we’ll start to see the answers to these questions, in part because some notable cases will go to trial (the family of a teen who died by suicide will bring OpenAI to court in November).

At the same time, the legal landscape will be further complicated by President Trump’s executive order from December—see Michelle’s item above for more details on the brewing regulatory storm.

No matter what, we’ll see a dizzying array of lawsuits in all directions (not to mention some judges even turning to AI amid the deluge).

—James O’Donnell

text:
Sunny Leone was studying to become a nurse. She was working at a Jiffy Lube in California.

Ten years later she was the most Googled person in India.

Born Karenjit Kaur Vohra in Ontario, Canada. Sikh parents. Catholic school. She played street hockey with boys and dreamed of a medical career.

At 19, Penthouse made her Pet of the Month. By 2003, she was Pet of the Year. She signed with Vivid Entertainment and became one of the biggest names in the adult industry.

Then India happened.

In 2011, she walked into the Bigg Boss house India’s version of Big Brother on day 49. Her Twitter gained 8,000 followers in two days. Google searches for her name exploded. Politicians filed complaints. BJP leaders demanded action. The Ministry of Information was contacted.

She didn’t apologize. She didn’t hide.

Director Mahesh Bhatt entered the Bigg Boss house personally to offer her the lead in Jism 2. She accepted on camera.

The film was a commercial hit. Then came Ragini MMS 2 another hit. Then a cameo with Akshay Kumar. Then a dance number with Shah Rukh Khan in Raees. A critic wrote: “She carries off her character with supreme confidence.”

In 2016, a journalist named Bhupendra Chaubey sat her down for a live interview. He asked her if she regretted her past. He asked if people would ever accept her. He asked if she was ashamed. The questions kept coming.

She didn’t break. She smiled and said: “I don’t care what people think.”

The interview went viral. Aamir Khan one of the biggest actors on the planet publicly defended her. The entire country debated whether a woman’s past should define her future.

That same year BBC named her one of their 100 Women. PETA named her Person of the Year.

She adopted a daughter from Maharashtra. Had twin sons through surrogacy. Built a production company. Published a book. Got inducted into the AVN Hall of Fame.

“I am lucky that the audience is accepting me. I don’t have any plans to go back there.”

A woman who worked at a lube shop and studied nursing built an entertainment empire across two continents. Politicians tried to ban her. Journalists tried to shame her. The audience chose her anyway.

Is she the most unlikely crossover in entertainment history?

text:
Title: A Timeline of the Controversies Surrounding Jensen Huang

A series of controversies has recently emerged surrounding NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. I have put together a timeline of the major developments.

10/29 NYT reports allegations of Alice Huang's ties to   
            Chinese intelligence agencies.
11/03 U.S. midterm elections: Democrats gain control 
            of both the Senate and the House.
11/05–08 Democrats intensify scrutiny of the Trump 
            family's business dealings.
11/11 NYT publishes further allegations of Jensen 
          Huang's extramarital workplace affair, while WSJ  
          reports preparations to remove him as NVIDIA 
          CEO.

The relationship between The New York Times (NYT) and President Donald Trump has long been deeply adversarial. The NYT has consistently investigated Trump's wealth, business activities, family affairs, and political controversies. Trump, in turn, has repeatedly fought back by filing lawsuits against the newspaper.

Looking at the timeline above, the NYT first published allegations involving Alice Huang on October 29, just days before the November 3 midterm elections, and subsequently released further allegations concerning Jensen Huang's extramarital affair within NVIDIA.

This sequence suggests that the NYT may view Jensen Huang as a central figure supporting the Trump administration. Huang has not only provided substantial political funding to Trump and the Republican Party but has also played a major role in driving U.S. economic growth, effectively serving as a critical pillar sustaining Trump's second administration.

It is therefore conceivable that the NYT may continue releasing information in stages until Jensen Huang is forced to step down from NVIDIA altogether.

At this critical moment, the United States must not forget the painful lesson of the 1950s, when the country drove Chinese-born scientist Qian Xuesen back to China amid the hysteria of McCarthyism.

Qian Xuesen earned his doctorate at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) and was a key figure in establishing the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). The organization later became part of NASA, developing rocket propulsion systems, while subsequent generations of researchers following in his footsteps launched the Voyager spacecraft into deep space.

Qian also traveled to Germany, where he personally interviewed and helped recruit Wernher von Braun and other German rocket scientists. These scientists subsequently joined forces with American rocket researchers, including those at JPL, to lay the foundations of what would become NASA.

Yet Qian, subjected to suspicion and persecution in the United States, eventually returned to China, where he spearheaded the country's rocket development programs. Under his leadership, China's ballistic missile, satellite, and broader space programs gained significant momentum, eventually paving the way for human spaceflight.

Without Qian Xuesen, China's space program might still be at a far less advanced stage than it is today.

If American society continues to relentlessly pressure Jensen Huang, potentially leaving him isolated even from his own family, who can say that he would never decide to move to China and lead the development of an independent GPU industry there?

China has demonstrated a remarkable ability to recognize and capitalize on such opportunities.

In the 1950s, when Qian Xuesen wanted to return to China after being mistreated by the United States, Mao Zedong proposed exchanging 11 American military pilots captured during the Korean War for Qian.

The proposal received widespread media attention, prompting intense demands from the prisoners' families for their return. Ultimately, the U.S. government found itself under such pressure that it had little choice but to allow Qian to leave for China, however reluctantly.

If the United States continues to alienate one of its own most influential technology leaders, China may attempt to repeat history by offering Jensen Huang an extraordinarily prestigious research leadership position, along with virtually unlimited financial resources to develop an independent GPU ecosystem.

From China's perspective, Jensen Huang is unquestionably a figure whose expertise, experience, and strategic importance could justify such an extraordinary offer.

AAIP Accelerated Tech Pathway cut-offs have often sat lower than many general streams in recent draws.

This Alberta Advantage Immigration Program route targets people with a job offer or current full-time work in eligible tech occupations (such as software developers, data scientists, IT specialists, and related roles). Because demand and scoring can favor targeted pathways, minimum Worker EOI scores for tech have frequently been more reachable than broad Alberta Opportunity Stream rounds.

If you have any IT, data, or software experience, even freelance, personal, academic, or short-term work, build a simple portfolio of past projects before you apply. Use clear screenshots of dashboards, code, apps, analyses, or systems you worked on, paired with short descriptions (2–4 sentences) that name the tools, your role, and the result. Visual evidence plus concise notes is far more effective than long paragraphs. 

Officers reviewing applications can quickly confirm your skills match the occupation and job offer, which strengthens your case under the tech pathway rules. Keep it honest, organized, and limited to relevant work.

text:
I'm a college student in China running a WeChat public account. Today was messy.

Woke up at 7:15 to my roommate’s alarm that sounds like a fire truck. Opened Moments for ideas and just saw perfect breakfast photos and people posting “studying” from cafés.

Checked my numbers: 19 views, 4 likes. One from mom, one from dad (he still thinks this is the school paper), the rest are probably bots. Algorithm’s treating me like it’s still 2016.

Tried writing “A Day in the Life of a Chinese College Student.” Typed the title, then got distracted by a cat failing to jump on a fridge.

Class was economics. My notes turned into “why do the good noodles always sell out by 11:45?”

Lunch was dry pot. I sweated like I ran a 5K. Most people outside China would tap out after two bites and still call it medium. Dumplings and rice were solid and cost less than a latte.

Tried filming after. Set my phone on textbooks and started explaining how WeChat does everything. Roommate walked in at 2pm in pajamas and offered instant noodles. Video stopped.

Spent the afternoon scrolling Douyin and calling it research. Ended up with half-finished drafts and a clip of me tripping over my backpack.

Posted something simple tonight about late-night snacks and night markets. Food’s good and people actually help each other.

Exhausted, but the process is funny. Numbers are still tiny. Student life here is the same mess as everywhere else—just with better dumplings.

What a wonderful day!

text:
When I told my friends I was getting married to a woman from a poor family, they congratulated me and wished me well.

I loved Patricia, and I didn’t care that her family lived in a small village, struggled financially or had very little to offer. I believed marriage was about love, not wealth.

Unfortunately, I never imagined that my biggest problem would be her father.

When I first visited her family to introduce myself, her father welcomed me warmly.

After exchanging pleasantries, he asked about my job, income and family background.

I answered honestly.

He nodded and said, “My daughter has suffered enough. I don’t want her to marry a man who will make her suffer again.”

I respected his concerns.

However, things became uncomfortable when we started discussing the traditional marriage requirements.

He brought out a long list.

Two cows, several bags of rice, cartons of drinks, expensive fabrics, money for different family members and other items…

A report on the visit of the German “peace delegation” to Moscow https://t.co/CZ8TlTPLfv, focusing on the symposium at the Europe Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, was posted on the World News Monitor (WNM) https://t.co/Md5ssC1luy. Interventions by participants on both sides centered on the new framework for world peace and cooperation offered by the BRICS.

“Victoria Panova, head of the BRICS Expert Council for Russia, emphasized the value of the BRICS philosophy: a culture of dialogue based on respect for sovereignty and recognition of the diversity of national interests,” the WNM report says. “In her view, the multipolar model embodied by the BRICS is better suited to the needs of today’s world than the approaches prevailing in the United States and the European Union.”

This is followed by a long comment by Rainer Braun, member of the board of the Berlin-based International Peace Bureau (IPB). “Among other things,” he wrote, “the following were considered essential for a new peace process: Talks and dialogue without preconditions; Overcoming the current refusals that fuel escalation; A ceasefire; The resumption of economic and scientific relations; ‘Sustainable deterrence,’ such as arms control and military restraint, particularly in critical regions like Kaliningrad.”

Braun added: “The German participants emphasized that reviving the dialogue requires rejecting the ‘image of Russia as the enemy’ and the unsubstantiated claim of a Russian attack against NATO. The general consensus was simply: Merz must call Putin!”

His comment ends with a list of recent and forthcoming steps in the right direction, which seem to have been taken from the editorial of the last issue of the EIR Strategic Alert:

Aurora fire investigators are appealing to people acquainted with the arsonist who set a $22 million inferno to "please contact us, even anonymously."

A $60,000 reward is being offered for information leading to a conviction in the blaze that destroyed five buildings at a residential construction site in the 7300-block of South Addison Court on Dec. 14, 2023.

"You may have noticed one or more of the following changes that were atypical or unexpected: changes in mood, lifestyle patterns, normal routine, such as missing work or school, or appearance; a sudden departure from the area; unreasonable explanations for disposal of clothing, unexplained injuries or burns; displays of anxiety, nervousness, stress, or irritability; changes in consumption of alcohol, drugs, or cigarettes; intense attention or avoidance of the news coverage of this case.

"We believe there is information which has yet to be shared, and there are people familiar with the circumstances who remain in our community. For those individuals who have information and have not yet spoken to law enforcement, please contact us, even anonymously." 

Two days later, on Dec. 16, 2023, Aurora was the scene of another huge blaze that destroyed a construction site at East Colfax Avenue and Peoria Street.

text:
Panagia Hozoviotissa Monastery in Amorgos

Some buildings are impressive because of their size. Others leave you wondering how they were ever constructed in the first place. Panagia Hozoviotissa Monastery in Amorgos manages to do both, standing dramatically against a sheer cliff face high above the Aegean Sea.

Founded in the 11th century, the monastery is dedicated to the Virgin Mary and is one of the most important religious landmarks in the Cyclades. Its striking white structure appears almost impossibly narrow, built into the rock with the sea stretching out far below.

Reaching the monastery involves climbing a series of steps from the coastal road, but the effort is rewarded with extraordinary views and the chance to experience a place that feels far removed from the everyday world.

Inside, visitors can discover a peaceful religious setting, historic icons and an atmosphere shaped by centuries of devotion. The monks who live here continue the monastery's traditions, and visitors are welcomed with respect for its spiritual significance.

A visit offers several memorable experiences:
•  Admire the architecture: See how the monastery has been built into the steep cliff, making remarkable use of the available space.
•  Enjoy the panoramic views: Look out across the Aegean from one of the most dramatic settings in the Cyclades.
•  Discover its history: Learn about the monastery's origins and its importance to the island's religious heritage.
•  Experience the peaceful atmosphere: Take a moment to appreciate the quiet surroundings and the sense of calm within the monastery.
•  Explore the surrounding coastline: Combine the visit with a trip to nearby Agia Anna, famous for its beautiful rocky shore and clear water.

There are a few things to keep in mind before visiting. Modest clothing is required, and the monastery may provide appropriate garments if needed. Comfortable footwear is essential for the uphill walk, particularly during the warmer months.

Try to avoid the hottest part of the day, and allow enough time to explore without rushing. Opening arrangements can vary, so checking locally before your visit is sensible.

Panagia Hozoviotissa is more than an extraordinary photographic location. It is a place where history, faith, architecture and nature come together in a truly remarkable way. If you visit Amorgos, make sure it is part of your journey.

The Grok Bot What's New walkthrough put the phone calls and the shared team bots in one place, and honestly I would read the call limits twice before I handed it a real number.

I would give it one boring job for a business, like cancelling a plan. It can work through the phone menu and sit on hold with a live transcript, and I can take over or hang up from the same card.

And I would only do that in the US states where it is offered. I would look at the who-it-will-dial card every time, because the terms say it calls US businesses and people who have agreed to hear from them, and it is not available in Washington or Illinois.

But for a team I would share one bot and leave each person's chats private, which is how Team Bots are set up. People start as Collaborators, and some of them get made Managers.

And I really want the hidden-instruction warning left on. When a page hides instructions for AI agents the bot is supposed to tell me and skip them, so I am not following a buried line I never saw.

So the rest of what I would turn on is on the card. Drafts for email and Slack show the attached files before anything goes out. The gift list asks for the recipient and the deliver-by date, and there is an analytics tab that charts messages over 7, 30 or 90 days.

I put the limits on the card, so you can check them before you hand it a real call, which is maybe the only way I would start.

text:
🇮🇳🇺🇸 Democrat-led US Congress: Will India-US ties get more predictable?

With Democrats set to take control of Congress in January, India may see greater stability in its engagement with Washington. However, expectations of a major reset in bilateral ties need to be tempered.

1️⃣ Trade deal: Still dependent on Trump
• The India-US trade deal, under discussion since February 2025, remains unfinished despite an interim framework agreed in February.
• Tensions over India's Russian oil purchases and fresh US tariff threats have complicated negotiations.
• Congressional oversight could scrutinise trade decisions, even where formal approval is not mandatory.
• Trump's priorities will remain decisive, particularly given competing trade issues involving China and Canada.
2️⃣ Tariffs: Greater scrutiny, but no guarantee
• The US Supreme Court's February ruling struck down Trump's use of emergency powers to impose tariffs.
• A Democrat-controlled Congress could provide a check on tariff unpredictability.
• However, new tariff measures under different legal provisions remain a potential source of friction.
3️⃣ H-1B visas: Some relief, limited expectations
• Democrats have opposed the proposed $100,000 enhanced H-1B visa fee, which has been temporarily blocked by courts.
• Congress controls statutory caps and limits under the programme.
• Indians account for over 70% of H-1B applicants and approvals, making the issue particularly important for India.
• A softer Democratic approach to immigration is possible, but bipartisan concerns over immigration remain.
4️⃣ Political differences could complicate ties
• The Democrats' increasingly influential left caucus could bring greater scrutiny of India's domestic policies.
• India's close relationship with Israel may also attract attention given the caucus's pro-Palestinian position.
• The Democrats have not traditionally been India's natural allies.

Takeaway: A Democrat-led Congress could offer India greater predictability on tariffs and immigration, but it cannot guarantee a faster trade deal or easier H-1B access. Trump's executive powers and domestic political priorities will continue to shape the relationship.

text:
Iran targeted maritime navigation and monitoring facilities on Oman’s Didmar Island in the Strait of Hormuz on November 8. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed responsibility on November 10.

I. Additional Information

1. Didmar Island hosts an Omani Royal Navy maritime traffic monitoring center, marine radar, communication systems, and a navigational lighthouse, making it an important part of the infrastructure supporting maritime traffic through the Strait.

2. Iran’s apparent objective is to establish practical control over maritime transit by directing vessels toward routes it can monitor and regulate, while determining which ships may pass. This puts pressure on Oman and challenges its independent role, particularly in supporting the southern route, which does not require Iranian authorization.

3. Iran claimed that the attack targeted equipment assisting vessels using the southern route without Tehran’s approval, including vessels operating alongside US forces. It also claimed that traffic through this route had stopped. However, available information indicates that vessels continued to transit.

4. The immediate impact on maritime traffic may be limited because alternative navigation systems and facilities remain available. The operation’s strategic significance may therefore exceed its direct operational impact, particularly if Iran intends to raise the risks and costs of using the southern route.

5. The extent of the damage remains unclear. Although Reuters quoted three sources confirming the attack, Omani information and other reports indicated that the main equipment was not hit. A newly identified burn mark near the lighthouse does not establish that radar or communication systems were destroyed.

II. Assessment

Iran is seeking to impose its own rules on maritime transit through the Strait, including acceptable routes and the authority to grant passage. This exposes Oman to growing pressure despite its neutrality, as its geographical position and maritime infrastructure support the southern route and offer an alternative to Iranian control.

The attack also reflects broader competition over surveillance and control systems in the Strait, following US strikes against Iranian military facilities and radar installations on Qeshm Island. Iran may now be extending pressure beyond vessels to the infrastructure supporting and monitoring their movement.

III. Conclusions and Expectations

1. Iran is likely to continue targeting or pressuring infrastructure supporting maritime traffic along the southern side of the Strait.

2. Pressure on Oman may increase, potentially undermining its independent role in maritime traffic management and its mediation between Tehran and Washington.

3. US-Omani coordination will likely become more important in protecting southern transit routes and securing surveillance, communications, and navigation-aid systems.

4. Iran may expand its targeting to these facilities if it considers their continued operation a means of enabling passage without its approval.

5. The central challenge will be preventing Iranian threats and the resulting increase in transit risks and costs from becoming de facto control over maritime passage, while avoiding the expansion of the confrontation to Omani territory and facilities.

text:
🚨Sudanese Echo Sources: UAE Seeks Halt to Sudanese Media Campaign as Turkish Intelligence Chief Warns Against Continued Arms Supplies to Militia

Sudanese Echo | November 12, 2026 

The news platform Saber @SABERfi4 reported that the United Arab Emirates had asked Turkey to mediate the opening of negotiations with Sudan, amid growing political and diplomatic pressure on Abu Dhabi over its role in the war and its support for the Rapid Support Militia. The platform noted that Sudan's position on the proposed mediation remained unclear and that the request had not been officially confirmed.

Following Saber's report, Sudanese Echo conducted its own independent inquiries through sources familiar with the discussions, corroborating the existence of the Emirati request and obtaining additional details about consultations between Turkish National Intelligence Organization (MIT) Director Ibrahim Kalın and senior UAE officials in Abu Dhabi.

On November 3, the UAE officially announced that Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan had received the Turkish intelligence chief, in the presence of National Security Adviser Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Supreme Council for National Security Secretary-General Ali bin Hammad Al Shamsi. The official statement described the discussions as covering bilateral relations and regional and international developments, without disclosing details of the consultations concerning Sudan.

According to information obtained by Sudanese Echo, the Sudanese conflict featured prominently in Kalın's discussions during his visit to Abu Dhabi. He met with senior Emirati officials, including Vice President Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Minister of State Sheikh Shakhboot bin Nahyan Al Nahyan, who oversees the Sudan portfolio on behalf of the UAE. Sources also reported the participation of Ali Saeed Al Neyadi, chairman of the UAE's National Emergency Crisis and Disaster Management Authority, whose name has previously appeared in international investigative reporting concerning activities linked to Emirati intelligence services. These include the "Abu Dhabi Secrets" investigations published by Mediapart and its partners, which examined his reported role in overseeing intelligence operations and influence campaigns targeting individuals and institutions in Europe.

Sources told Sudanese Echo that Emirati officials asked Kalın to convey a message to Sudan's Transitional Sovereignty Council Chairman, General Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan, requesting an end to Sudanese media campaigns targeting the UAE. During the same consultations, the sources said, Kalın warned Emirati officials against continuing arms shipments to the UAE-backed Rapid Support Militia (Janjaweed), informing them that US intelligence agencies had detected and monitored these activities.

The Associated Press reported in November 2025, citing a US official familiar with two intelligence assessments produced by the State Department's Bureau of Intelligence and Research and the Defense Intelligence Agency, that both assessments had identified an increase in Emirati weapons supplies to the militia between late summer and early autumn 2025. According to those assessments, the shipments included armed and unarmed Chinese drones, heavy weapons, machine guns, ammunition, mortars, and artillery.

Evidence concerning Emirati support for the militia extends well beyond US intelligence assessments, forming part of an extensive and growing body of international investigative reporting. Major news organizations, including The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, Reuters, and the Financial Times, have published investigations examining various aspects of the UAE's alleged involvement in the Sudanese conflict. Their reporting has been complemented by investigations from Bellingcat and Lighthouse Reports, as well as satellite imagery analysis and research conducted by Yale University's Humanitarian Research Lab. This body of work is further reinforced by findings from Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan, and the UN Panel of Experts on Sudan, including confidential and leaked reports examining military and logistical supply networks, weapons transfers, drones, and foreign fighters entering Sudan through neighboring countries. Sudanese Echo previously obtained a leaked UN Panel of Experts report examining routes and networks associated with Emirati support for the militia. The breadth of these investigations provides important context for the warning that Sudanese Echo's sources say Kalın delivered to Emirati officials regarding continued arms shipments and their detection by US intelligence agencies. The UAE continues to deny providing military support to the militia.

The reported Emirati request to halt Sudanese media campaigns may also be connected to the international criticism surrounding the candidacy of UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh for the position of United Nations Secretary-General. Her candidacy has faced opposition from human rights organizations over her record of defending the UAE's position on the war in Sudan. Human Rights Watch criticized Nusseibeh's record of denying Emirati support for the Rapid Support Militia, while the Arab Organisation for Human Rights in the UK sent letters to 47 countries and five international and regional bodies urging them to reject her candidacy. The timing raises the possibility that Abu Dhabi is seeking to contain the diplomatic and reputational consequences of this campaign, although there is no confirmed information indicating that Nusseibeh's candidacy was specifically discussed during the Turkish-Emirati consultations.

Turkish mediation between Sudan and the UAE is not an entirely new proposal. In December 2024, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan offered Al-Burhan Turkey's assistance in mediating the dispute between Khartoum and Abu Dhabi. Al-Burhan welcomed any Turkish initiative that could help end the war, while the UAE also expressed its willingness to cooperate with Ankara on efforts to resolve the conflict. The latest consultations, however, come against a markedly different backdrop, following the growing number of international investigations into Emirati military support for the militia and the escalation of political and media tensions between Khartoum and Abu Dhabi.

It remains unclear how Sudanese authorities have responded to the Emirati request, or whether Ankara has formally conveyed the proposal to Al-Burhan. No official statement from the parties involved has confirmed the details of the Sudan-related consultations, while the question of Emirati military support for the militia remains one of the central points of contention between Khartoum and Abu Dhabi.
