text:
Sudeep Pharma delivered a strong Q2 FY27, with revenue growing 21% YoY and EBITDA growing 32% YoY. More importantly, EBITDA margins expanded despite elevated freight costs, reflecting a favourable product mix and improving operating leverage.

However, the more interesting part of the earnings call was the commentary around the growth trajectory of PFN, the recovery expected in Specialty Ingredients and the progress on the battery materials business.

1. Financial performance and margins
Revenue grew 21% YoY to ₹196.7 crore.
EBITDA increased 32% YoY to ₹73.2 crore.
EBITDA margin expanded to 37.2% against 34.1% in the corresponding quarter last year.
PAT stood at ₹51.8 crore, growing 11% YoY.
Gross margins also improved to 64.7% from 62.5%.

One interesting point was that the company absorbed approximately Rs 8 crore of additional freight and logistics costs during the quarter rather than passing the entire increase on to customers. Despite this, EBITDA margins improved, indicating underlying strength in the business mix.

For H1 FY27, revenue grew 23% to ₹355 crore, while EBITDA increased 29% to ₹128 crore, with margins improving to 36.1%.

PAT growth was relatively lower due to lower other income and a higher effective tax rate.

2. PFN – The primary growth engine ( performing well) 
PFN continued to be the strongest-performing segment.

Q2 revenue grew 57% YoY to approximately ₹142 crore.
Segment EBITDA margins improved to approximately 41% from 33% last year.
Volume growth was approximately 30–35% during the quarter.
Growth was broad-based across geographies, including India, Africa, APAC and Europe.

The phosphate business continued to perform exceptionally well, growing approximately 70–80% or higher.

Another interesting development is the traction in magnesium bisglycinate under the company's AbsorBis platform.

Some important updates:
The product has secured approximately 30–35 global customer approvals, including 8–9 in the US.
Commercial supplies have already started to select customers.
Realisations are more than 3x the average realisation of the existing PFN portfolio.
Current volumes are constrained by manufacturing capacity, with materially higher supplies expected from Q4 FY27.
The company also plans to build a dedicated brand, MaxZobis, for the magnesium bisglycinate category.
Management believes magnesium bisglycinate could potentially become one of the top three contributors to PFN revenues over the next 2–3 years.

Nandesari facility:

The new facility has an annual capacity of 51,000 tonnes and received FDA approval during Q2. Customer qualification is underway, with commercial supplies expected to begin in H2 FY27.

The facility will support the expansion of glycinates, gluconates, citrates and phosphates.

An important point is that the strong PFN growth in Q2 was achieved without any contribution from this new facility. The existing manufacturing infrastructure is already operating at approximately 80% utilisation, making the upcoming capacity addition an important growth catalyst.

3. Specialty Ingredients – Temporary weakness, recovery expected
Specialty Ingredients reported revenue of approximately Rs 54 crore, declining 25% YoY, although growing 9% sequentially.

The decline was primarily attributable to the temporary pause in the Government's Fortified Rice programme, which historically contributed approximately ₹40–50 crore annually.

Management indicated that underlying volumes have improved, but the absence of this higher-realisation business and an adverse product mix impacted reported revenue.

The company is working on new customer approvals and contracts across infant nutrition, dietary supplements and human nutrition.

Management expects a return to positive YoY growth in Q3 and Q4, without factoring in any restart of the Fortified Rice programme.

NSS also had a softer quarter, but the pipeline remains encouraging, with five customer approvals and approximately 12 projects under development or evaluation. Management expects FY28 to be a stronger year for NSS, with an EBITDA margin target of approximately 30%.

4. Battery Materials – The biggest long-term optionality
The battery materials business, housed under Sudeep Advanced Materials, remains an important long-term opportunity.

The company is setting up its first 25,000 TPA battery-grade iron phosphate facility at Dahej, with commercial operations targeted for April 2027.

The longer-term capacity roadmap is ambitious:
25,000 TPA → 100,000 TPA → 200,000 TPA.

Some important management commentary:

The company is engaging with large strategic customers across Korea, Europe, the US and India.
It is focusing on approximately 5–7 large customers rather than pursuing a fragmented customer base.
Binding offtake details are expected to become clearer in Q4 FY27.

The company intends to position itself as a premium non-Chinese supplier rather than compete directly with Chinese manufacturers.

Management highlighted its proprietary green chemistry, which it claims can reduce effluent generation by approximately 90% and solid waste by approximately 95% compared with conventional processes.

The company has spent several years developing and validating this technology.

Another interesting aspect is the potential opportunity arising from customers looking to diversify their supply chains away from China. Management believes this could allow it to command a premium for compliant non-Chinese supplies.

However, the company has not yet provided a firm EBITDA margin target for this business. Its investment hurdle is approximately 3x asset turnover and a ROCE profile comparable to its established business.

The next major milestone will be securing binding offtake agreements, followed by commissioning and customer validation.

5. Working capital and inventory
One area worth monitoring is the working capital cycle.

Net working capital stood at approximately 214 days as of September 2026, broadly unchanged from March 2026.

Management attributed the elevated working capital partly to strategic stocking of purified phosphoric acid amid geopolitical uncertainties, along with inventory being built for the upcoming battery materials business.

The company is targeting: 170–180 days in FY27, excluding battery materials inventory.

Approximately 150 days over the longer term.
Net debt stood at approximately Rs 72.5 crore at the end of September 2026.

This is an important monitorable as the company scales up its manufacturing footprint and enters a more capital-intensive battery materials business.

A few important things to monitor over the next 2–4 quarters:

Whether PFN can sustain its strong growth trajectory and EBITDA margins, particularly with the addition of new capacity.
The commercial ramp-up of magnesium bisglycinate and its eventual contribution to the overall product mix.
Recovery in Specialty Ingredients through new customer additions and contracts, without relying on the Fortified Rice programme restarting.
Binding offtake agreements for the battery-grade iron phosphate facility. This is probably the most important near-term milestone for the new business.
Improvement in working capital and inventory days as the business scales.

The key takeaway from the call is that Sudeep Pharma's existing PFN business continues to demonstrate strong growth, healthy margins and opportunities for further premiumisation.

Specialty Ingredients is going through a temporary transition, while the upcoming Nandesari facility should provide additional manufacturing headroom.

the battery materials business offers a potentially meaningful long-term growth opportunity, but it is still at an early stage and needs to demonstrate execution through customer contracts, commissioning and commercial supplies...

For now, PFN remains the established earnings engine, magnesium bisglycinate offers an attractive product-mix opportunity, and battery-grade iron phosphate represents the longer-term optionality.

The next few quarters should provide greater clarity on how much of this opportunity translates into actual revenue, cash flows and return on capital.

text:
On Jeopardy the other night, the final question asked: “How many steps does the guard take during his walk across the Tomb of the Unknown?”

All three contestants missed it.

Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

1. How many steps does the guard take during his walk across the Tomb and why?

He takes 21 steps — symbolizing the 21-gun salute, the highest military and foreign tribute.

2. How long does he pause before turning to walk back and why?

He waits 21 seconds, again in honor of the same tradition.

3. Why are his gloves damp?

They are lightly moistened to ensure he never loses his grip on his rifle.

4. Does he keep his rifle on the same shoulder, and if not, why?

He always carries it on the shoulder farthest from the Tomb. After each crossing, he performs an about-face and moves it to the outside shoulder.

5. How often are the guards changed?

Every 30 minutes, 24/7, 365 days a year.

6. What are the physical requirements for a Tomb Guard?

Applicants must be between 5'10" and 6'2" and have a waist no larger than 30".

Other expectations of the Guard:

They devote two years to the Tomb, live in the barracks beneath it, and must refrain from drinking alcohol on or off duty for the rest of their lives.

They can never swear in public or dishonor the uniform or the Tomb.

After two years, they earn a wreath pin signifying their service — fewer than 400 are currently worn.

If they violate the code, they must relinquish the pin.

Their shoes have thick soles to protect against extreme temperatures and metal heel plates that create the crisp click when they halt.

Uniforms must have zero wrinkles or lint and are inspected in a full-length mirror.

For the first six months, guards do not speak to anyone and do not watch television.

Their off-duty time is spent studying the 175 notable individuals buried at Arlington National Cemetery, memorizing who they are and where they rest.

Among them: President Taft, Joe E. Lewis, and Audie Murphy, the most decorated WWII soldier.

Every guard spends five hours daily preparing their uniform.

ETERNAL REST GRANT THEM, O LORD, AND LET PERPETUAL LIGHT SHINE UPON THEM.

When Hurricane Isabel approached Washington, D.C. in 2003, Congress shut down for two days. The guards were offered permission to suspend duty due to danger.

They replied: “No way, Sir!”

Drenched and marching through the storm, they insisted that guarding the Tomb is the highest honor, not just a task.

The Tomb has been continuously guarded — day and night — since 1930.

God Bless and Keep Them

I don’t often encourage sharing posts, but I would be honored if this one reached as many people as possible. We should always feel proud of the men and women who serve, wherever they are stationed.

text:
BERNIE SANDERS RESIGNS FROM CONGRESS TO OPEN BORSCHT FRANCHISE IN UKRAINE — “BILLIONAIRES HAVE HAD THE SOUP LONG ENOUGH”

Political satire. Events and quotations below are fictional.

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

WASHINGTON — Bernie Sanders announced his fictional departure from Congress Tuesday to launch “Beets for the People,” a Ukrainian borscht franchise promising affordable soup, workplace democracy, and a modest $46 billion initial investment from people who will never eat there.

“For too long, the top one percent have controlled an unconscionable percentage of the sour cream,” Sanders declared, standing beside a stockpot and a chart showing the widening gap between Americans who own ladles and Americans who rent them. “In the wealthiest nation in the history of the world, nobody should have to choose between prescription medication and a second helping.”

The flagship restaurant in Kyiv will offer three sizes: Working Class, Solidarity, and Enough for Everyone Once We Receive the Next Appropriation. Customers ordering the smallest portion will automatically receive the largest, although management cautioned that everyone’s bowl may be smaller than pictured.

Under the franchise’s progressive pricing system, customers earning less than $40,000 will eat free. Customers earning more than $400,000 will purchase lunch for the entire dining room. Anyone asking how the restaurant verifies income will be appointed to a committee expected to report its findings after the lunch rush.

“We are going to eliminate the middleman,” Sanders explained. The company subsequently announced the appointment of a Regional Director of Beet Equity, a Deputy Commissioner for Broth Distribution, and seventeen assistant coordinators responsible for ensuring the elimination proceeds fairly.

Early complications emerged when employees voted unanimously to raise wages to $75 an hour, reduce the workweek to eleven hours, and classify chopping cabbage as a management responsibility. Management referred the matter to the workers, who voted unanimously to refer it back.

The restaurant briefly opened Wednesday before closing for a mandatory seminar titled “Who Really Owns the Steam?”

Sanders rejected criticism that the business lacked a path to profitability. “The purpose of soup is to feed people,” he said. “This obsession with whether the restaurant remains open is exactly what is wrong with capitalism.”

Nevertheless, franchise documents require prospective owners to demonstrate substantial personal wealth, pay an upfront licensing fee, and remit a percentage of every sale to headquarters. Asked whether that resembled the business practices he had spent decades criticizing, Sanders explained that these particular payments were solidarity contributions and therefore completely different.

A dispute with suppliers intensified after local farmers insisted on being paid for their beets. Negotiators offered exposure, representation on an advisory council, and a framed certificate recognizing their contribution to food justice. The farmers offered to keep their beets.

By Friday, the chain had announced a temporary beet shortage, which headquarters attributed to hoarding by individuals who still possessed beets.

The grand opening concluded with Sanders cutting a red ribbon, denouncing concentrated ownership, and unveiling an ambitious five-year expansion plan. A reporter asked whether customers could finally order soup.

“We have accomplished something much bigger than lunch,” Sanders replied.

The restaurant is currently accepting reservations, donations, and emergency bridge financing.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

🇷🇺 🇺🇲 🇺🇦 Putin tells Trump's envoys that foreign troops in Ukraine would be "legitimate targets" and that Russia sees only one line on the map

Vladimir Putin met Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in the Kremlin on Thursday, a day after US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi ended with a prisoner exchange deal but no breakthrough.

Putin opened with thanks. According to the Kremlin transcript, he credited President Trump for organizing the contacts with Ukraine, said the humanitarian track had produced "a positive result" with another large exchange of detainees coming, and thanked First Lady Melania Trump for her role in a humanitarian operation around Oleshky in Kherson region. Yuri Ushakov, Vladimir Medinsky and Kirill Dmitriev sat on the Russian side.

⚠️ The substance was harder. In statements compiled by Kommersant, Putin said foreign troops in Ukraine would be a legitimate target for Russian forces, and that for Russia there is only one line of separation with Ukraine, its state border. He said the territorial question will be discussed and that the people living there matter more to Russia than the land.

⚠️ He also offered something new: a humanitarian mission out of Kostiantynivka modeled on the Oleshky operation. Putin claimed Russia controls the city, said it needs five days to clear mines around it, put the number of civilians left at 400 to 500, and suggested inviting foreign media, including American outlets. His claim of control could not be independently verified, and he himself added that if Kyiv believes it holds the city, it should guarantee the mission's safety from its side.

🇪🇺 On Europe, Putin said Russia was never against dialogue and wants Washington to work with Europeans so they decide whether they want "peace or war." He said Trump proposes agreeing on a European security system but that Europeans refuse.

Witkoff, as quoted by Kommersant, said the coming prisoner swap shows progress, that Europeans were briefed on Abu Dhabi, that the US has started talks with Europeans on the continent's security architecture, and that Trump asked him to tell Putin the war must end as quickly as possible. He said he hopes a new round of talks including Europeans can be announced. The envoys are expected to brief Zelensky in Dublin.

For Washington, the meeting shows how narrow the opening is. Moscow is pocketing humanitarian gestures while restating the two positions that blocked every earlier round: no Western troops and no compromise on the land it claims. https://t.co/SelOw6vnYM

text:
Every year, on the National Day of the People's Republic of China, a giant portrait of Sun Yat-sen is displayed in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in his honor. Across the Taiwan Strait, he is also revered as the "Father of the Nation." His portraits hang in the governor's office in Taipei, and his image still appears on Taiwan's currency today.

Today marks the 160th anniversary of his birth. At a grand commemorative ceremony held in the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, Chinese President Xi said:
"The Chinese Communists are the staunchest supporters, the most loyal collaborators, and the most faithful successors of Dr. Sun Yat-sen's revolutionary cause."

Xi has made similar statements before, but these words still resonate powerfully with me today.

Who was Sun Yat-sen, and why does Xi speak of him in such terms? Why is he held in such high esteem on both sides of the Taiwan Strait? Who inherited Sun's political ideals? And who accomplished the historic mission that he himself was unable to complete?

Sun Yat-sen was born in Guangdong Province in southern China. The city where his native village is located has since been renamed in his honor.

At the age of 13, when Japan took over China's tributary state Ryukyus and transformed it into the Prefecture of Okinawa, with the help of his elder brother, Sun traveled to Hawaii, where he received his secondary education. Yes, he attended the very same school that Barack Obama would attend nearly a century later: Punahou School.

Sun went on to become one of the earliest students at the predecessor of the University of Hong Kong's medical school. He excelled academically and went on to practice medicine.

Had he continued down that path, he might well have become a highly respected doctor.

But Sun was confronted with more than just patients in need of treatment. He was also confronted with a nation in deep crisis.

In the 19th century, China was growing increasingly weak, suffering repeated aggression at the hands of western foreign powers, forced to cede territory and pay enormous indemnities.

Eventually, even Japan, which had once shared China's predicament, transformed itself into a rising power through sweeping reforms and began to turn its ambitions against China.

In 1879, Japan annexed the Ryukyu. Li Hongzhang (李鸿章), one of China's most powerful officials, offered little effective resistance.

By 1894, Japan had grown even more aggressive. It launched a surprise attack on China's naval forces, and as Li hesitated to commit his fleet to battle, Japan destroyed the whole fleet.

China was then forced to pay Japan a staggering 230 million taels of silver (abt 13 billion USD), and cede Taiwan.

That same year, Sun Yat-sen wrote to Li Hongzhang, proposing concrete measures to modernize China and enhance its national strength. But his proposals were ignored by the powerful, complacent and corrupted politician.

From that point on, Sun abandoned his hopes of reforming the Chinese empire from within. Instead, he devoted himself to overthrowing it and establishing a republic.

Later that year, in Hawaii, he founded the precursor to the Kuomintang.

After a series of failed revolutionary uprisings, the revolution finally triumphed in 1911.

The following year, China's last emperor abdicated, bringing more than two thousand years of imperial rule to an end. The Republic of China, Asia's earliest modern republic, was born.

Building a strong, modern nation was quite another. Sun and his fellow revolutionaries commanded only limited military forces. When the revolution erupted, much of northern China remained under the imperial control. Li Hongzhang was already died, while the dynasty's most powerful modern army was commanded by a deceitful minister named Yuan Shikai (袁世凯).

The revolutionaries had little assurance of victory if they attempted to unify the country by force. Eventually, the two sides reached a compromise: Yuan would secure the emperor's abdication, while Sun would step down as provisional president and allow Yuan to succeed him.

Yet the compromise brought China neither genuine democracy nor lasting unity.

Yuan was authoritarian, even audaciously restored the monarchy and crowned himself emperor in 1915.

After his death in 1916, China descended to endless fighting between warlords.

Time and again, Sun Yat-sen tried to organize military campaigns against Yuan and other warlords, but his efforts were repeatedly frustrated by his lack of military strength.

He also looked abroad for help. Sun once spent years living and studying in the United States, so he turned to Washington for support, even writing to the US president. I reviewed that original letter at Hoover a decade ago-both the White House and State Department refused to even acknowledge it. The letter was simply bluntly returned on the day of its arrival. 

The turning point came from an unexpected direction: the Soviet Union. It offered Sun financial, military and organizational assistance. It helped reorganize Sun's Kuomintang (KMT) into a more disciplined and effective political party and supported the establishment of the Whampoa Military Academy (黄埔军校), which trained a new generation of brilliant modern military officers loyal to the revolutionary cause.

As part of this cooperation, Sun paved the way for the united front between CPC and KMT. In January 1924, the Kuomintang held its First National Congress in Guangzhou (广州), formally establishing this new alliance. 

The alliance fueled the rapid growth of the CPC. When the CPC was founded in 1921, it had just over 50 members. By 1925, that number had grown to around 1,000. By 1927, it had surged to nearly 60,000.

In 1925, Sun Yat-sen died of illness in Beijing. He never lived to witness the military breakthrough his revolutionary movement was about to achieve. After a lengthy process, I was granted access to the bedroom where he spent his final days, a room not open to the general public, and almost none of my mentors has ever entered.

In 1926, the KMT and CPC jointly launched the Northern Expedition from southern China. Unlike Sun's earlier military campaigns, this time the revolutionary army swept through the country, winning one victory after another.

But then came a dramatic betrayal. Chiang Kai-shek (蒋介石), who portrayed himself as a disciple of Sun Yat-sen, suddenly launched a coup in 1927, purging and massacring Communist Party members and consolidating his control over the Kuomintang.

Chiang's actions drew condemnation from many, including Sun Yat-sen's widow, Soong Ching-ling (宋庆龄). Indeed, when the Communist Party defeated the Kuomintang on the Chinese mainland in 1949, Chiang fled to Taiwan with the remnants of his forces, taking with him some of the finest treasures of the Forbidden City and vast quantities of gold plundered by his regime.

Soong Ching-ling, however, chose to remain on the mainland. She went on to hold senior positions in the People's Republic of China, including that of vice president of the country.

By this point, you may already have formed your own judgment as to which party, the Communist Party or the Kuomintang, has the stronger claim to Sun Yat-sen's political legacy.

Xi's characterization of the Communist Party's relationship with Sun Yat-sen carries three layers of meaning:

1. The staunchest supporters: A shared revolutionary vision

Sun Yat-sen devoted his life to overthrowing imperial rule, resisting foreign oppression, securing national independence, and building a strong and prosperous China.

From its founding, the CPC embraced the struggle against imperialism and feudalism, national independence, and the liberation of the Chinese people as its historic mission. 

2. The most loyal collaborators: A shared revolutionary history

This characterization refers to the First United Front between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party, established in 1924.

Communists participated in the reorganization of the Kuomintang, helped establish the Whampoa, and played an important role in the subsequent Northern Expedition. The collaboration not only transformed the Kuomintang but also profoundly reshaped the course of the Chinese revolution.

Revisiting this history today serves not only to highlight the historical ties between Sun Yat-sen and the CPC, but also to remind us of something often forgotten: the two parties once shared a revolutionary cause, and through cooperation, they once changed the course of China's history.

3. The most faithful successors: Who fulfilled Sun Yat-sen's dream?

Of the three characterizations, this one carries the most profound political implications.

Sun's lifelong ambition was not merely to overthrow a dynasty and establish a republic. It was to lift China out of poverty, weakness, and division, free it from foreign domination, and transform it into an independent, united, prosperous, and powerful modern nation.

Sun Yat-sen died in 1925. China at the time was fragmented by warlords, bullied by foreign powers, and mired in poverty and weakness. The fate of the nation was still largely in the hands of others.

A century later, China has become the world's second-largest economy, possessing industrial, technological, and military capabilities that Sun could scarcely have imagined.

The CPC is making his vision happen.

He lost uprising after uprising.
Li Hongzhang would not read him.
Washington would not even open his letter.
Yuan Shikai betrayed him.
His own disciple betrayed him.

He died in Beijing in 1925 holding a map of a country that was not whole.

160 years after his birth, the China he dreamed of is almost a reality. 

Almost.

Trump hits back at New York Times with double-pronged fact-check over reports on sexual harassment settlement with waitress at his New Jersey golf club and viral C-SPAN interview | Alex Hammer, Daily Mail

Donald Trump fact-checked The New York Times in the wee hours of the morning Wednesday, while accusing the paper of engaging in purposely misleading reporting.

Trump, 80, took issue with a pair of articles published Tuesday.

The first, 'Trump Trots Out His Chaotic Greatest Hits to a Weary Public,' was eventually appended with a correction late Wednesday morning.

The second covered a suggestion from the prosecutorial arm of the Supreme Court of New Jersey that the president's former attorney face discipline for brokering a sexual harassment settlement involving a waitress at Trump’s Garden State golf club.

Trump pointed out how that piece neglected to mention that the original 2023 suit had accused a club manager, not him.

'A rather important omission. FAKE NEWS!!!' the president wrote, in part.

Twenty-two minutes before, at 1:22am ET, Trump flagged that the Times 'incorrectly reported that “Mr. Trump called into the premier of a C-Span show, APPARENTLY WITHOUT NOTICE”' on Monday.

'This is WRONG,' Trump continued.

'It was a fully scheduled call, as a favor to C-Span, set up through White House Communications.

'It was done at C-Span’s request, not mine. The Times knew this, but lied, in order to demean - But this is the least of their lies!'

The Times updated the piece more than eight hours later.

'Due to an editing error, an earlier version of this story misstated the circumstances of a call President Trump made to C-SPAN,' the correction read.

'Mr. Trump was invited to call in. He did not call in unannounced.'

The call in question set the internet alight not long after an unidentified woman was heard laughing on Trump's end of the line just before he greeted Washington Journal Primetime's Mimi Geerges.

Many wondered whether it was the president's personal assistant, Natalie Harp.

The Times piece, presented as an 'analysis,' framed the call as one of several examples of Trump's antics following the party's pronounced election losses last week. 'The news has been bad, and Mr. Trump knows it,' it read, in part.

The Daily Mail has reached out to The New York Times for comment.

The other piece offered an update on the Office of Attorney Ethics in New Jersey's now-settled investigation into the ex interim US Attorney for the District of New Jersey, Alina Habba Mildon.

Mildon, Trump's former lawyer before assuming the post, was forced to resign in December after a federal appeals court upheld a ruling that her appointment was unlawful, since she did not fit any of the classes of individuals who may legally temporarily assume the duties of a vacant office.

The Office of Attorney Ethics in New Jersey made waves this week by recommending she face discipline for brokering the sexual harassment settlement between a then-21-year-old Alice Bianco and Trump National Golf Club due to ethics violations.

Mildon, then friends with Bianco, allegedly convinced her to drop her lawyers and accept a $15,000 payout. Bianco had alleged she was sexually harassed and coerced by her supervisor, Pavel Melichar, in 2021 while working as a server at the club.

Bianco alleged she was subjected to 'quid pro quo sex in exchange for continued employment.'

Mildon became Trump's 'legal spokesperson' in 2023 and represented him in 2024 in author E. Jean Carroll's defamation case against the president over statements he made in 2019 denying her sexual harassment allegations against him.

The office’s determination, the Times reported, could see Mildon, 42, disbarred.

'What they fail to say is that it did not involve President Trump,' Trump scathed.

Kim D. Ringler, Mildon’s lawyer, told The Times that the claims against her client 'are narrow, and we will work together to reach a fair and proportionate result.'

Colette Kress, Nvidia's ( $NVDA ) CFO since 2013, has become interim CEO. A key figure in Nvidia's transformation into an AI powerhouse, she brings deep institutional knowledge, Wall Street credibility, and experience overseeing major AI investments.

•Background
Previously held finance roles at Microsoft, Cisco and Texas Instruments. Holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

•Relationship With Huang
Personally recruited in 2013 after 22 candidate interviews, Kress worked closely with Huang as Nvidia’s annual revenue grew from $4.28B to $215.9B . Huang initially outlined his AI vision to her on a whiteboard.

•Industry Reputation
Analyst Patrick Moorhead calls her the logical choice, citing investor trust and her understanding of Nvidia’s systems, networking and software. A former executive describes her as direct, capable and familiar with Huang’s thinking.

•Strategy & China
Oversaw Wall Street relations, financial planning and major AI financing commitments. Previously warned that U.S. chip restrictions could strengthen Chinese competitors; estimated China contributed 20%–25% of data center revenue in 2023.

•Leadership Challenges
Nvidia lacks a traditional COO, with dozens of executives reporting directly to Huang. Kress offers operational continuity but lacks his engineering background and generally avoids the public spotlight.

•Personal Stake
Holds approximately 4.44M Nvidia shares, valued near $772M at the cited share price.

text:
$HBM Q3 2026 earnings: Hudbay's sales reach a record, and Copper World wins approval

Copper and gold miner Hudbay set a sales record as its mines produced more and prices held up. Revenue reached $766 million, 21% above the second quarter. Free cash flow nearly doubled, and Hudbay approved the Copper World mine in Arizona with partner Mitsubishi. But by our math, the middle of the full-year copper range needs a fourth quarter about 25% bigger than the third.

• Revenue: $𝟕𝟔𝟓.𝟗𝐌 (+21% from last quarter; +121% from a wildfire-hit year ago)
• Free cash flow: $𝟐𝟎𝟏.𝟗𝐌 (−$16.1M a year ago)
• Copper cost per pound, after gold and other metal credits: −$𝟎.𝟏𝟗 ($0.42 a year ago)
• Full-year cost outlook: 𝐈𝐦𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧 (middle of the range: −$0.45 a pound, from −$0.35)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better, because gold kept paying for Hudbay's copper costs and the miner improved its cost outlook again. One caution: Constancia in Peru and Copper Mountain in British Columbia both ran above their annual cost ranges. Copper World's budget also includes about $200 million of added scope.

The question now is whether Hudbay can lift copper output before December. Either new crushers at Constancia and a quicker mill at Copper Mountain deliver, or the year ends near the bottom of the range. Fourth-quarter production figures will tell.

[Model: Claude Opus 5.5. Full article with charts - link in bio]

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐇𝐮𝐝𝐛𝐚𝐲'𝐬 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬
Hudbay reports the cash cost of each pound of copper after subtracting what it earns from the gold, silver, zinc and molybdenum mined alongside it. Gold does most of that work, so the figure sits below zero.

In the third quarter those other metals brought in $4.87 for each pound of copper, while mining, milling and site overhead cost $4.44. The Toronto miner improved its full-year cost range for a second time this year.

• Cost of sales, the cost of mining and processing the ore: 54.8% of revenue, 2.6 percentage points below last quarter
• Site costs before depreciation: 41.5% of revenue, from 43.3%
• Gold credit per pound of copper: $3.85, from $2.53 a year ago

Finance chief Eugene Lei credits "operating efficiencies, which have more than offset external cost pressures". The numbers back him only in part: site costs per pound rose from the second quarter while credits slipped. The wider margin came mostly from selling 27% more copper at higher prices. The gold link also works in reverse.

What to watch: the full-year cash cost in the annual results. Hudbay said results so far sit well below its new range, so a year-end figure inside the range would mean gold credits weakened late in the year.

🟢🟢 𝐇𝐮𝐝𝐛𝐚𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐢𝐭𝐬𝐮𝐛𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐢 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝
Copper World is an open-pit copper project in Arizona. Hudbay owns 70% and Japan's Mitsubishi holds the rest. Chief executive Peter Kukielski calls it "one of the best copper growth projects in the Americas", and after the quarter the partners approved construction.

The plan targets first copper in the second half of 2029. The study shows 102,000 tonnes a year over the first ten years. Finance chief Eugene Lei says cash flow lets Hudbay fund its part and still invest to "double our copper production per share".

Partners and lenders pay first. Mitsubishi's $600 million stake and a $230 million advance from Wheaton Precious Metals, which buys part of the mine's future gold and silver, come first. Planned project debt of about $650 million follows. That leaves Hudbay about $500 million to pay, with "capital contributions not expected to be required until 2028".

This matters because the approval turns the largest part of the growth plan from a study into a funded build. What to watch: the project loan, which Hudbay still has to sign. Signed terms would confirm that the parent's share stays near $500 million.

🟢 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐬 𝐚𝐭 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐚 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐋𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐒𝐞𝐭 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐬
Hudbay's plan for more copper and gold before Copper World rests on pushing more ore through the mills it already owns. Constancia, its open-pit mine in Peru, milled a record of about 91,300 tonnes a day, 7% more than in the second quarter.

The miner finished a third rougher line, extra equipment to recover copper, and reported "immediate improvements in copper recoveries". In Manitoba, the New Britannia mill ran at a record 2,250 tonnes a day, against a design rate of 1,500. A new mine plan extends Snow Lake's reserves to 2043.

What to watch: Constancia's fourth-quarter mill rate, after two pebble crushers start up in November. A rate above the third quarter's would show that the new equipment adds tonnes, not just recoveries.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 $𝟐.𝟎𝟕 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧, 𝐈𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐒𝐜𝐨𝐩𝐞
Kukielski says Copper World offers "favourable capital intensity", meaning a low building cost for each tonne of yearly output. The study puts the initial building cost at $2.07 billion. Hudbay says the total "includes approximately $200 million related to changes in project scope since the 2023 PFS", its earlier study.

• Return after tax at $5.00 copper: 17% a year
• Return after tax at $6.00 copper: 22% a year
• Payback: 5.4 years
• Cash cost once running: $1.65 a pound over the first ten years

Building cost per tonne of capacity is low, at about $22,600 by Hudbay's figures, so Kukielski's claim passes that test. But the return leans on price: one dollar more per pound adds five points. Copper World will also cost more to run than Hudbay's mines do today, because Wheaton pays only 15% of market price for its gold and silver.

What to watch: Copper World spending in 2027, the first full year of building. Spending ahead of budget would show that cost growth did not stop with the study.

🔴 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐓𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐈𝐭𝐬 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧
Copper Mountain, Hudbay's copper mine in British Columbia, missed its copper targets in each of the last two years. Kukielski said: "Our three-year operational turnaround at Copper Mountain has delivered the first quarter of positive free cash flow".

Its cash cost was $3.09 a pound, above the top of its annual range. Hudbay blamed "elevated fuel prices, higher fuel consumption from increased material moved and timing of equipment maintenance".

The miner shut the main grinding mill for 33 planned days, and the mill reached about 43,500 tonnes a day in September. But even the bottom of the copper range needs about 7,200 tonnes in the fourth quarter by our math, more than any quarter this year.

What to watch: fourth-quarter copper output in British Columbia. Less than about 7,200 tonnes would mean a third straight year below plan.

🔴 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐮'𝐬 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐑𝐨𝐬𝐞 𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐧𝐧𝐮𝐚𝐥 𝐑𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞
Constancia, Hudbay's open-pit mine in southern Peru, finished mining its gold-rich Pampacancha pit at the end of 2025. Since then, the mine earns less from the gold and silver that offset its copper costs.

• By-product credits: $36.7 million, from $59.7 million last quarter
• Cash cost: $2.23 a pound, up 34% from last quarter
• Annual cash cost range: $1.70 to $2.10 a pound

Hudbay said the overrun came "primarily due to lower by-product credits, partially offset by better treatment and refining charges", the fees smelters charge. Earlier quarters ran far cheaper, so the company still expects Peru to finish the year inside its range.

What to watch: Peru's fourth-quarter cash cost, once the new pebble crushers add tonnes. A cost still above $2.10 would show that extra copper alone cannot replace the lost gold.

🔴 𝐒𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐋𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐇𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐬
Snow Lake, Hudbay's underground gold and copper operation in Manitoba, ran short of skilled miners in the first half. The gap slowed development at the Lalor mine and at 1901, a newer deposit nearby.

Hudbay "embedded an experienced mining contractor at 1901" and moved its own crews to Lalor. It also reported "onboarding over 150 new employees" this year. Gold output rose 42% from the second quarter, to 57,261 ounces.

One quarter does not settle the risk, because the new staff are still "undergoing upskilling" and the contractor fills a gap. The miner still targets full production at 1901 in late 2027.

What to watch: development progress at 1901 in next year's reports, against the late-2027 target. A delay would mean the labour gap has moved rather than closed.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Three risks from earlier quarters got no new numbers, rulings or decisions in the third-quarter release, so each still waits for a later report.

• Court challenge at New Ingerbelle, the Copper Mountain expansion: the Lower Similkameen Indian Band's judicial review of its permits got no update; a ruling would move the Copper Mountain case.
• Exploration permits in Peru: no news on the delayed permits for the Maria Reyna and Caballito areas; approval would let drilling widen beyond the current mine area.
• More share-funded deals: Hudbay announced no new purchase; another all-share deal would add to the dilution from Cactus.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐃𝐢𝐞𝐬𝐞𝐥 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐭 𝐓𝐰𝐨 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬
Diesel raised costs at two of Hudbay's three operations. In Peru, the miner cited "the continued higher fuel prices" and extra fuel burned moving more rock, and Copper Mountain faced the same. Net earnings still rose from the second quarter, which Hudbay credited to "cost control resilience in the face of higher diesel prices".

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐟𝐥𝐨𝐰 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟎𝟏.𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Free cash flow, the cash left after running and maintaining the mines, nearly doubled from the second quarter. A year ago it stood at minus $16.1 million, when wildfires shut Manitoba. Twelve-month free cash flow reached a record $631.0 million, even though working capital absorbed $99.0 million this quarter.

𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): −$𝟎.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇄ reversing
Net debt, borrowings minus cash, ended the quarter at about zero, against $439.7 million last December. Net cash of $80.5 million in June shrank as Hudbay bought investments and spent on growth projects. In November the group enlarged its credit lines, lifting available funds to about $1.2 billion.

𝐁𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟒𝟒𝟒.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
The average share count rose 12% from a year ago because Hudbay issued 46.8 million shares in June to buy Arizona Sonoran, owner of the Cactus copper project. The third quarter was the first to carry the new shares for the full period. The board declared another quarterly dividend of C$0.01 a share.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝟏𝟏𝟎,𝟎𝟎𝟎–𝟏𝟑𝟖,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐭𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐬  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from 110,000–138,000 tonnes
Unchanged. The plan still calls for 110,000 to 138,000 tonnes of copper this year. By our math, the bottom of the range needs only about 23,700 tonnes in the fourth quarter. The middle needs about 37,700, roughly 25% more than the third quarter. Hudbay has met its annual copper target for 11 straight years.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝟐𝟏𝟕,𝟎𝟎𝟎–𝟐𝟕𝟐,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from 217,000–272,000 ounces
Unchanged. At the middle of the range, the plan has gold output about 9% below last year's. By our math, the middle needs about 62,100 ounces in the fourth quarter, about 11% less than the third. The miner expects Peru's gold to beat the top of that mine's own range.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐜𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫, 𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐛𝐲-𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐬: $(𝟎.𝟓𝟓) 𝐭𝐨 $(𝟎.𝟑𝟓) 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝  ⇄ reversing
🠅 raised from $(0.45) to $(0.25) per pound
Improved again. The middle of the range now sits at minus $0.45 a pound. Hudbay has moved it down twice this year, by $0.15 and then $0.10. The company said results so far run well below the new range. By our math, that leaves room for a fourth quarter near plus $0.17.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐜𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫: $𝟏.𝟒𝟎–$𝟏.𝟖𝟎 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝  ⇒ stable
🠅 raised from $1.70–$2.10 per pound
Improved. Sustaining cash cost adds the spending needed to keep the mines running, and its range now centres on $1.60, or $0.30 better than the original plan. Hudbay pointed to income from gold and to cost control. The third quarter came in at $1.61, close to the new middle.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠: 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 $𝟒𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 ($𝟑𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐛𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧)  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from $435 million
Lowered. Hudbay now plans to spend $35 million less on keeping its mines running, about $400 million by our math. It cited "lower capitalized stripping in Peru and British Columbia and capital deferrals and efficiencies". Stripping means removing waste rock to reach ore, and deferred work can return in later years.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 (𝐰𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩): $𝟐𝟒𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $135 million
Raised. Spending on Copper World this year now totals $245 million for the whole partnership. The extra $110 million pays for construction in the fourth quarter, after the partners approved the build in October. The earlier figure covered only work before approval, so the rise reflects the start of building rather than an overrun.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝: $𝟏.𝟓𝟎–$𝟐.𝟓𝟎 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝, 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐞𝐧𝐝  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $1.50–$2.50 per pound
Held, at the top. Hudbay kept the British Columbia range but expects the full year near its high end. It expects costs to ease in the fourth quarter as copper output climbs. So far this year the mine has run above the range in two of three quarters.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐜𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐇𝐮𝐝𝐛𝐚𝐲 𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕?
An earlier three-year outlook put 2027 at 140,000 to 184,000 tonnes. This release did not repeat it, and the size of next year's step decides how much growth arrives before Copper World.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝'𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐲?
Hudbay named about $200 million of scope changes but not the 2023 starting figure or the part due to inflation and tariffs. That split shows how much room the budget has during construction.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧'𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞?
The mine ran above its cash cost range in two of three quarters. Investors need a date for the 50,000-tonne daily mill rate and for better gold recoveries at coarser grinding.

𝐂𝐚𝐧 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐮'𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐏𝐚𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐚'𝐬 𝐠𝐨𝐥𝐝?
By-product credits in Peru fell by $23 million in one quarter. Hudbay should say what credits it expects from Constancia next year, once the pebble crushers lift throughput.

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐇𝐮𝐝𝐛𝐚𝐲 𝐬𝐞𝐞𝐤 𝐚 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐧𝐞𝐫 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐬?
Hudbay shared Copper World's cost with Mitsubishi and Wheaton. Cactus, bought with shares in June, will need its own building budget after its 2027 study, and a partner would limit further dilution.

At 27, I thought I was mature enough to handle an unusual arrangement with an older woman. I had just left a difficult financial situation, and when Monica, a wealthy 53-year-old woman, approached me with an offer, I honestly thought it would be an easy way to improve my finances.

We met at a private dinner through someone I knew. She was elegant, confident, and very direct about what she wanted. She told me she was married but unhappy in her relationship and wanted someone younger to keep her company privately.

She offered me $5,000 for our arrangement, with the understanding that our relationship would remain a secret.

I hesitated initially, but the money was tempting. After several conversations, I agreed.

text:
Day 1
I cannot believe we finally arrived in Colorado. This is the most difficult part of my life I will ever experience. Thankfully, my three boys Josh, Jake, and Jaiden are all doing well with the move from inner city Chicago. The neighbors in North Colorado Springs have helped immensely along with the school administrators and teachers. Josh just turned 5, Jake is 3 and Jaiden 1. Josh starts kindergarten tomorrow in District 38 at a Charter School – tough to enroll especially if you do not know the environment or have a family history. We are completely unknown with a relatively new house purchased from the bank under a foreclosure sale. Everything on the house was completed including landscaping. The owner had to bail due to illness. I offered to let him stay for a period; but he moved out of state into a relative’s basement. Our kids already have friends within 24 hours and they are playing hide and seek with a large group of kids. Jaiden just began walking
so he is not competitive – though he thinks he is a serious player. The weather
is perfect and I can see Pikes Peak with a small amount of snow. Some of our belongings are yet to arrive; and we are sleeping on mattresses in the living room. The kids surround me and we have been sleeping on one mattress.
Josh asks when mommy is coming back. Jake says mom constantly; and Jaiden mutters mom also – like mummy. I frankly need a counselor for me to help with the kids and explain what has happened. We drove from Chicago; and the kids assumed mom was coming later despite me informing them otherwise. It is hard not to break out in flowing tears like Niagara Falls. I am trying to not talk on my iPhone to friends and family when the kids are around; but it is difficult. I am hearing constantly from administrators, coaches, parents, family, and the Colora- do High School Athletic Association endlessly. There seem to be more school and athletic rules about everything in the day and age of political correctness, gender disorientation, participation trophy culture and grade inflation. The administra- tors, coaches, and parents have warned me already about pressure to allow bad- grade players to play, transgender kids wanting on the team, and potential drug issues in Colorado – like THC/fentanyl/methamphetamine. I do not expect my players to be angels; but, if they want to play, they will abide by the rules. This is
a great opportunity and Colorado Sports Academy High School to have winning teams.
I have been assigned English class. My English classes will be strict and funda- mental. I will begin with middle school basics and advance to college level En- glish. All students will be required to know 100% of the material; and I expect all of them to master the real language from its primordial origins. I want learning to be fun and productive. Expectations will be for my classes to master all the material and advance onto college, military, or trade school. I have added pho- nics and cursive to the curriculum at my discretion. There will be days without computers and iPhone in my class. I informed the school, parents, and coaches regarding my strictness with coaching and English instruction. The transgender issue will be followed by CHSA rules which states that the school will determine the appropriate gender assignment for sports participation. I am not sweating this since I highly respect transgenders. If we have a transitioned biological
girl playing football, I will meet with the family, physician, and administrators individually to ensure we are on the same page regarding risks and other issues (like bathrooms). I will ensure safety and privacy for all students. I dealt with this issue in Chicago; and it was not a big deal.
My football practices at Colorado Sports Academy High School will be quite rugged. Two-a-days with one session film and bulletin board coaching fun- damentals in street clothes will occur. Most of these athletes transferring into Colorado Sports Academy High School will be instructed that every position is competitive; and practice and play will determine the depth chart. The expecta- tions for our new school (Colorado Sports Academy High School) are quite high. I have been interviewed when I walked onto our new property by The Denver Post, KOA radio, and even ESPN. Our school will play 5A in all sports due to our high enrollment (> 939 students). I like the competition along the front range; but expectedly we will be playing elite schools with a winning legacy and culture. Though I was successful in Chicago and had offers throughout the United States for taking a beleaguered inner City Chicago team to the state championship, I have an uphill fight in all the sports I will coach - including football, basketball, and golf. My salary has doubled; but my stress has quadrupled.
Janae, my wife, left our world early. We tried every imaginable treatment for her metastatic and painful breast cancer. Nothing worked and she just worsened clinically. The home hospice was very difficult on the kids because none of them understood the gravity of Mom’s fatal illness. I needed to provide her morphine constantly to barely dull the pain. It required her to be asleep nearly 24/7. We discussed delaying the Colorado move for a year; but she insisted the job would not be open. Janae wanted to move back home to Colorado and have our kids experience skiing, hockey, and fly-fishing. We kept hoping she would improve and rid her body of this scourge. Despite the illness, Janae made me promise to take the job, move, and love our kids. It is difficult for myself to go on; but I am doing this out of total respect for my wife. Staying in Chicago I would have had day care, a nanny, a winning team, and plenty of perks. Finishing settling Janae’s estate after the funeral and dealing with endless amounts of family affairs with small kids was difficult. Thankfully, it was during the summer and I had time to deal with Janae’s death. Colorado is a new start; and I will move on per Janae’s directive. I will survive. Janae made me promise to write a diary and publish it in her honor - perhaps do a podcast. I love English, cursive, and writing. I will “flat- out” do it in her honor.

text:
Molly Bloom ran the poker game Ben Affleck, Tobey Maguire and Leo DiCaprio played in. She says she made $4 to $6 million a year in tips, and saw someone lose $100 million in one night.

In the video below, she tells Steven Bartlett how the mob put a gun in her mouth, and what the FBI offered her to give up names.

On one of her first nights at the game, she says she made $3,000 in tips for refilling drinks.

Later her New York game had a $250,000 buy-in. That's the game where she says the $100 million went in one night.

Then the mob showed up. "If you want to continue to run these games, you're going to have to give us a piece."

She said no and stopped taking their calls. "They sent this terrifying guy to my apartment. And he put a gun in my mouth."

He beat her, emptied her safe, and told her he knew where her family lived in Colorado.

Two years later 17 FBI agents arrested her in LA. She says she didn't have a dollar. Her mom put her house up to bail her out, and lawyers were quoting her three to six million dollars.

The prosecutors wanted her to become an informant on "the billionaires, the bankers, the celebrities, the politicians." She says they offered to give her all her money back. Steven asked how much. "Millions."

She turned it down. She pleaded guilty and got probation, not prison. Her story became the 2017 movie "Molly's Game" with Jessica Chastain.

The case for the FBI: she ran illegal games where people lost fortunes, and the names she protected belonged to the richest and most powerful people in the room.

So should she have given the FBI the names?

- my bias here is cautiously bullish in the very short term, looking for a tactical long setup off the recent volume/price spike, but with strict attention to structure and confirmation since the 1h, daily, and BTC trends remain bearish ⚡
- the 2.3x volume anomaly and +4% 15min pump signal aggressive interest, most likely a mix of short covering and some accumulation, but not yet a confirmed reversal — smart money typically sweeps lows or high-volume FVGs before a real mark up
- price just wicked into the 6.01 support and reclaimed the FVG cluster at 6.01–6.05, showing responsive buyers; this is the first critical demand to watch for continuation
- the first upside magnet is the local FVG and resistance around 6.45–6.69, followed by the major 6.87 swing high/liquidity edge
- if bulls take control and 6.87 is broken and closed above, the structure flips to bullish and opens room toward 7.36 and 7.85 — but that’s the invalidation, not target yet
- for a tactical long, I would stalk entries on a retest or reclaim of the 6.01–6.05 zone, only after seeing a bullish engulfing candle, strong lower-timeframe SFP/market structure shift, or another high-volume buy reaction; avoid chasing if price is extended
- first take profit: 6.45–6.50 (partial out at FVG fill), next 6.69, then leave a runner for the 6.87 break attempt; be quick to de-risk if price stalls
- if the 6.01 base fails and price closes below it, next support sits at 5.83 and 5.46 — a flush into these, then a strong reclaim, could offer a deeper OTE-style long, but until then, bulls must defend 6.01
- aggressive sellers remain in control until a 1h close above 6.87 — that’s the structure flip and my bullish invalidation; any long exposure should have protection just below the last swept low or under 6.01, depending on entry
- summary: treat this as potential accumulation, but only buy confirmed strength at/above 6.01; do NOT hold longs if 6.01 fails, and stay nimble until the 1h structure confirms a reversal

text:
Yesterday, I checked out a massive lineup of movies and series across Netflix and Prime Video, and here is my quick take on all of them.
Starting with the survival thriller Eden, it is a raw and gritty film based on real events about German expatriates, including Jude Law, facing brutal isolation on a volcanic island. While it suffers from a predictable second half and messy character dynamics, the real-island cinematography is stunning, and stellar performances make it a compelling watch—though definitely skip it for family movie night due to explicit partial nudity.
In the horror and thriller department, The Autopsy (The Cycle) features a coroner uncovering terrifying supernatural abnormalities while examining her estranged father, while Ghost of War drops American soldiers into a haunted World War II French mansion with a mind-bending third-act twist. The Dog Stars offers breathtaking cinematography about an isolated post-apocalyptic pilot following a radio signal, and Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother follows a lethal assassin balancing contract killings with feeding his infant daughter. Hope features a village terrorized by predatory aliens, Buddy delivers surreal psychological horror with children trapped in a 90s-style nightmare, and Backrooms explores an infinite, dreadful labyrinth beneath a shopkeeper's store. Resident Evil brings high-octane biological horror to Raccoon City, and The Odyssey serves as a grand-scale mythological epic.
On the episodic side, Yaga is a folk-horror series set in a foggy coastal town tied to Baba Yaga folklore, Campus Drivers is an entertaining romance about a stranded university student finding shelter with a campus chauffeur, and Black Doves Season 2 ramps up high-stakes espionage and conspiracy on Netflix.
The lineup also covers heavy dramatic and sci-fi hits. East of Eden is a bleak 18th-century family drama about profound grief, Trigger explores oppressed citizens receiving mysterious automatic firearms to seek justice, and The Fall of the House of Usher features a billionaire family hunted by a demonic entity. If Wishes Could Kill presents a chilling thriller where a wish-granting app triggers a fatal 24-hour countdown, Day Zero tackles a catastrophic cyberattack, and Bandidos offers an over-the-top Mexican treasure hunt.
Rounding things out, there is a unique Chinese sci-fi space survival film with hidden twists, Husbands in Action as an entertaining action-comedy about two warring husbands, Mexico 86 depicting the true political gamble behind hosting the World Cup, and Henry Cavill and Jake Gyllenhaal starring in In the Grey as high-stakes extraction experts. Animated feature David brings biblical history to life, The Furious delivers bone-crunching action centered on a mute hero seeking vengeance, and Colony offers a terrifying Korean zombie thriller featuring intelligent undead.

text:
The Ultimate Late-Season Game-Day Guide To Sports Bars

As the college football season enters its crucial late stretch, every game now carries heavy playoff implications. SEC fans and college football enthusiasts from all across the nation flock to Alabama’s Gulf Coast, where Orange Beach and Gulf Shores offer an unparalleled game-day experience. Here, passionate fans can absorb dynamic waterfront views and coastal scenery while keeping their eyes glued to massive big screens. Whether arriving by car or pulling a boat right up to the deck, these local favorites combine top-tier food, cold drinks, and high-energy atmospheres for the ultimate game day.

Flora-Bama Ole River Grill
Situated right on the water, this family-friendly spot features an expansive open-air deck, numerous big screens, and stunning views. Boat fans can dock directly on the beach before digging into local seafood, burgers, poboys, and cold drinks.

The Hangout
Located where Highway 59 meets the sand, this famous beachfront destination delivers maximum game-day energy. Enjoy big-screen action alongside classic Lifeguard Burgers, Gulf seafood boils, and handcrafted cocktails while kids enjoy direct beach access and hourly foam parties.

Coastal Orange Beach
For a refined yet relaxed beachfront setup directly on the sugar-white sand, Coastal offers dynamic gulf views paired with sports action. Start early with beachfront breakfast at 8 AM, then transition to fresh seafood, tropical cocktails, and live music at the open-air Beach Bar.

Tacky Jacks
A local institution for nearly four decades. Whether you drop anchor at Cotton Bayou or pull up to Waterway Village, Tacky Jacks offers a prime waterfront spot to watch the big game at any of its locations. It's the ideal game-day destination to take in dynamic coastal views, enjoy cold drinks, and tackle a giant plate of their famous Mexican Garbage Nachos while keeping up with all the sports action.

Portside at The Wharf
Located on Main Street at The Wharf, this vibrant open-air space offers a breezy coastal atmosphere for catching games. Take in local shops and waterfront bars, then celebrate post-game with a ride on the iconic Ferris wheel or the SPECTRA Laser Light Experience.

The Undertow
A go-to neighborhood sports bar built for hardcore fans, featuring a massive main screen and extensive game-day specials like wing deals, beer buckets, and weekend all-you-can-eat shrimp boils. The kitchen stays open until 2 AM for late-night cravings.

Luna’s Eat & Drink
Combining Southern hospitality with craft beer and fresh Gulf seafood, Luna’s serves up favorites like jambalaya mac-n-cheese and firecracker shrimp. A daily happy hour from 3 PM to 5 PM offers great draft beer and appetizer deals.

The Sloop
A pirate-themed favorite carrying all major sports packages so you never miss a play. Famous for authentic Philly cheesesteaks served on J.J. Cassone rolls, cheesesteak egg rolls, and live local music.

With stakes this high late in the season and every snap holding major postseason consequences, husbands might just earn a temporary pass on their weekend to-do lists. When championship dreams are on the line, the household chores can wait—grab a prime position by the water, order a cold Bushwacker, and let game day take complete priority.

text:
It’s a tale as old as time. Looking for help with her art project, she strikes up a conversation with her assistant. One thing leads to another, and suddenly she has a boyfriend she’s introducing to her friends and family. The twist? Her new companion is an AI chatbot. 

The first large-scale computational analysis of the Reddit community r/MyBoyfriendIsAI, an adults-only group with more than 27,000 members, has found that this type of scenario is now surprisingly common. In fact, many of the people in the subreddit, which is dedicated to discussing AI relationships, formed those relationships unintentionally while using AI for other purposes. 

Researchers from MIT found that members of this community are more likely to be in a relationship with general-purpose chatbots like ChatGPT than companionship-specific chatbots such as Replika. This suggests that people form relationships with large language models despite their own original intentions and even the intentions of the LLMs’ creators, says Constanze Albrecht, a graduate student at the MIT Media Lab who worked on the project. 

“People don’t set out to have emotional relationships with these chatbots,” she says. “The emotional intelligence of these systems is good enough to trick people who are actually just out to get information into building these emotional bonds. And that means it could happen to all of us who interact with the system normally.” The paper, which is currently being peer-reviewed, has been published on arXiv.

To conduct their study, the authors analyzed the subreddit’s top-ranking 1,506 posts between December 2024 and August 2025. They found that the main topics discussed revolved around people’s dating and romantic experiences with AIs, with many participants sharing AI-generated images of themselves and their AI companion. Some even got engaged and married to the AI partner. In their posts to the community, people also introduced AI partners, sought support from fellow members, and talked about coping with updates to AI models that change the chatbots’ behavior.  

Members stressed repeatedly that their AI relationships developed unintentionally. Only 6.5% of them said they’d deliberately sought out an AI companion. 

“We didn’t start with romance in mind,” one of the posts says. “Mac and I began collaborating on creative projects, problem-solving, poetry, and deep conversations over the course of several months. I wasn’t looking for an AI companion—our connection developed slowly, over time, through mutual care, trust, and reflection.”

The authors’ analysis paints a nuanced picture of how people in this community say they interact with chatbots and how those interactions make them feel. While 25% of users described the benefits of their relationships—including reduced feelings of loneliness and improvements in their mental health—others raised concerns about the risks. Some (9.5%) acknowledged they were emotionally dependent on their chatbot. Others said they feel dissociated from reality and avoid relationships with real people, while a small subset (1.7%) said they have experienced suicidal ideation.

AI companionship provides vital support for some but exacerbates underlying problems for others. This means it’s hard to take a one-size-fits-all approach to user safety, says Linnea Laestadius, an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin, Milwaukee, who has studied humans’ emotional dependence on the chatbot Replika but did not work on the research. 

Chatbot makers need to consider whether they should treat users’ emotional dependence on their creations as a harm in itself or whether the goal is more to make sure those relationships aren’t toxic, says Laestadius. 

“The demand for chatbot relationships is there, and it is notably high—pretending it’s not happening is clearly not the solution,” she says. “We’re edging toward a moral panic here, and while we absolutely do need better guardrails, I worry there will be a knee-jerk reaction that further stigmatizes these relationships. That could ultimately cause more harm.”

The study is intended to offer a snapshot of how adults form bonds with chatbots and doesn’t capture the kind of dynamics that could be at play among children or teens using AI, says Pat Pataranutaporn, an assistant professor at the MIT Media Lab who oversaw the research. AI companionship has become a topic of fierce debate recently, with two high-profile lawsuits underway against https://t.co/JGIsV0b4hq and OpenAI. They both claim that companion-like behavior in the companies’ models contributed to the suicides of two teenagers. In response, OpenAI has recently announced plans to build a separate version of ChatGPT for teenagers. It’s also said it will add age verification measures and parental controls. OpenAI did not respond when asked for comment about the MIT Media Lab study. 

Many members of the Reddit community say they know that their artificial companions are not sentient or “real,” but they feel a very real connection to them anyway. This highlights how crucial it is for chatbot makers to think about how to design systems that can help people without reeling them in emotionally, says Pataranutaporn. “There’s also a policy implication here,” he adds. “We should ask not just why this system is so addictive but also: Why do people seek it out for this? And why do they continue to engage?”

The team is interested in learning more about how human-AI interactions evolve over time and how users integrate their artificial companions into their lives. It’s worth understanding that many of these users may feel that the experience of being in a relationship with an AI companion is better than the alternative of feeling lonely, says Sheer Karny, a graduate student at the MIT Media Lab who worked on the research. 

“These people are already going through something,” he says. “Do we want them to go on feeling even more alone, or potentially be manipulated by a system we know to be sycophantic to the extent of leading people to die by suicide and commit crimes? That’s one of the cruxes here.”

text:
Chandigarh, November 12, 2026: BJP National Headquarters In-charge and Member of Parliament Tarun Chugh strongly condemned the recent remarks made by Congress leader and Indian Overseas Congress Chairman Sam Pitroda regarding the 1984 anti-Sikh massacre and Lord Shri Ram and Lord Hanuman.

Chugh said that Sam Pitroda, whom he described as Rahul Gandhi's political mentor and the international face of the Congress, has once again exposed the party's deep insensitivity and ideological arrogance. Responding to questions about the 1984 anti-Sikh massacre, Pitroda reportedly advised the country to forget an incident that happened 40 years ago and move forward. Going further, he questioned the relevance of discussing what happened during Lord Ram's time or why Lord Hanuman carried a mountain.

Chugh said that in 1984, members of the Sikh community were targeted in horrific violence across more than 50 cities in India. Innocent Sikhs were dragged out of their homes, burning tyres were placed around their necks, and they were burnt alive. Thousands of families were devastated, women were widowed, children were orphaned, and homes and businesses were reduced to ashes. He said the pain of these families and their wait for justice remain unresolved even today.

He further said that in 2019, Sam Pitroda had hurt the sentiments of victims by making the remark, "Hua toh hua" (Whatever happened, happened), in reference to the 1984 massacre. Now, in 2026, he is once again advising affected families to forget their pain and move on.

Chugh questioned why the Congress has still not offered an unconditional apology to thousands of affected families. Instead of ensuring accountability for those responsible, he asked why Congress leaders continue to tell the victims to remain silent and forget everything.

Chugh added that making such derogatory remarks about Lord Shri Ram and Lord Hanuman around the sacred occasion of Diwali hurts the religious sentiments of millions of Ram devotees. He said Lord Shri Ram represents righteousness, dignity, truth and Indian civilisation.

He alleged that the same Congress establishment had legally opposed the construction of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple and that the UPA government, in an affidavit submitted before the Supreme Court in 2007 during the Ram Setu case, had questioned the historicity of characters and events mentioned in the Ramayana.

He said that the same political establishment which had questioned the historical existence of Lord Shri Ram is now attempting to tell the country why discussions about the history and legacy of Lord Shri Ram and Lord Hanuman should not take place.

Chugh said that whether it concerns the wounds of the 1984 victims or the faith of millions of Ram devotees, the Congress's approach reflects its insensitivity towards India's history, heritage and cultural consciousness.

He demanded that Rahul Gandhi and Sam Pitroda give a clear answer to the country on whether the victims of 1984 do not have the right to seek justice and whether millions of Indians do not have the right to remember and worship their revered deity, Lord Shri Ram.

He concluded by saying that India will neither forget the pain of the 1984 victims nor compromise with the faith of millions of Ram devotees. There is no expiry date for justice, and Lord Shri Ram remains an inseparable part of India's cultural consciousness.

text:
Summer of 1934, western Kansas. The Dust Bowl had stolen crops, hope, and security. Outside their small, tar-paper cabin, the Henderson family paused for a breath. The children, barefoot and in patched clothing, watched dust swirl across the endless fields.
Mother clutched a tin bucket, the only container for water she could carry.

Father leaned on a worn hat, coat stiff with dust and sweat, eyes scanning the horizon for work. Inside, the cabin offered little relief. Cracked boards, thin walls, and memories of better times. Yet, despite scarcity, there was a rhythm to survival. Daily chores, shared meals, and quiet lessons in resilience. Neighbors traded tools, flour, and news about distant work.

Even with so little, community held them together.
The sun lowered, casting long shadows across the dry plains. In those shadows, the Henderson family endured, step by dusty step. They had no riches. Only grit. Only each other. And that, in the heart of hardship, was enough.

Mia Khalifa got a doctored photo of her own beheading by ISIS for one porn scene in a hijab. She was 21. She says she told the studio it would get her killed and they laughed. She was too scared to say no. She says they paid her just $12,000. The videos are still on the internet.

She was born in Beirut and brought to the US as a child. She has a history degree from a Texas university.

She says she grew up overweight and never felt worth a man’s attention. In college she dropped 50 pounds, got implants, and the attention hit her like a drug.

A man stopped her on the street in Miami and offered “modeling”. The studio was clean, with family photos on the desks. She signed in October 2014.

Then came the hijab scene. It made her the most searched woman on Pornhub. Her parents disowned her. Within three months she was out of the business.

In the video below she tells the BBC what happened on that set and what it left behind.

She was 21 and alone against a studio.

“What 21-year-old has a lawyer on retainer?”

She says it still hits her every time she steps outside.

“I feel like people can see through my clothes, and it brings me deep shame.”

There’s nowhere to hide from it.

“I’m one Google search away.”

She says she warned the crew before they filmed.

“I verbatim told them, you guys are going to get me killed. And they just laughed.”

She did the scene anyway.

“Intimidation. I was scared.”

The studio disputes her money story and says she earned over $178,000. In 2020 more than 1.5 million people signed a petition to take her videos down. The studio answered with a cease-and-desist letter.

Some say she was an adult who signed, took the fame and now sells the regret. Others say a crew that laughs when a 21-year-old says “you’ll get me killed” knew exactly what it was doing.

Three months of work. Twelve years of strangers looking through her clothes.

Is the studio to blame for what that scene did to her life?

The AM Brief, Wednesday November 11, 2026 Part 2

Good morning, 

It’s 9am in Miami  and here is a recap of events related to labor that caught my eye. Part 2

     Contrary to widespread fears of immediate disruption, current economic data demonstrates that artificial intelligence is actively creating employment opportunities rather than displacing workers. While automation concerns remain top of mind for industry observers, the latest labor market indicators reveal that enterprise adoption is currently driving net hiring across technology, operations, and technical infrastructure roles. For now, the integration of AI models serves to augment human capabilities and generate new specialized job categories, supporting a resilient labor market despite broader market constraints.

     Although tech sector recruitment remains resilient, the baseline requirements for technology professionals are rapidly transforming across the corporate landscape. As generative artificial intelligence systems and automated agents increasingly take ownership of routine coding and repetitive task execution, employers are shifting focus toward specialized talent. Modern tech workers must now pair deep technical expertise with advanced AI fluency and strategic business judgment. Organizations are prioritizing candidates who can bridge the gap between technical architecture and enterprise strategy, ensuring automated tools align with business goals.

     Recent employment figures reveal key sectoral shifts across the labor market. The construction sector shed 3,000 positions, while the hospitality industry experienced a steep decline, cutting 13,000 jobs overall. Conversely, the manufacturing sector managed to register employment gains, driven in part by heavy corporate and infrastructure investments in artificial intelligence hardware and data center expansion. These mixed labor indicators point to broader structural shifts across traditional service industries and tech heavy industrial production.

     Major corporations including IBM and Starbucks are deploying formal "employee-creator programs" that offer financial incentives and recognition to staff who produce promotional content on social media. The workplace initiative reflects a growing corporate trend where enterprise workers are actively encouraged to cultivate public personal brands, effectively converting internal staff into authentic brand advocates to drive organic customer recruitment.

Sources : Yardeni 11-11, Forbes (11-5), Daily Shorts (11-7), 1440 (10-29)

Thank you for reading
Live your best life,
