The AM Brief, Wednesday November 11, 2026 Part 1

Good morning, 

It’s 9am in Miami  and here is a recap of market related events that caught my eye. Part 1

     The October Consumer Price Index increased by 0.4%, surpassing the forecasted 0.3% rise, while core CPI advanced by 0.3%. Primary drivers included shelter cost pressure and a sharp 0.5% surge in food prices, highlighted by a record 5.1% single month spike in baby formula costs. Following this higher than expected inflation reading, financial markets now view a quarter-point rate hike by the Federal Reserve at its upcoming December meeting as a near certainty to rein in sticky consumer price growth.

     Infrastructure updates highlight the soaring valuation of regional digital facilities. Texas Governor elect Gina Hinojosa reportedly confirmed that data centers holding active permits will be allowed to complete construction without interference. The colossal fiscal footprint of these facilities is already visible in places like Loudoun County, Virginia, which collected an astonishing $1.2 billion in property taxes from data centers during fiscal year 2026 alone. That massive influx accounts for roughly 39% of the county's total annual budget, underlining the reliance of local economies on tech growth.

     Financial columnist Matt Levine estimates that global spending on artificial intelligence could realistically scale to approximately $4 trillion annually within the next five years. Aggregated over time, this massive capital allocation equates to an extraordinary net present value of roughly $40 trillion. Because market valuations are anchored to such monumental expectations, overall equity pricing has become exquisitely sensitive to subtle shifts in timing, execution risks, and the ultimate magnitude of these anticipated AI-driven cash flows across public enterprises.

     Semiconductor stocks have compressed to remarkably historic valuation discounts despite strong long term structural demand. Following recent market drawdowns and sector volatility, chipmakers across the index are currently trading at their lowest earnings multiples in nearly seven years. Analysts emphasize that this dramatic valuation drop offers a compelling entry point for value investors, though ongoing geopolitical trade tensions, supply chain realignments, and fluctuating hardware demand continue to cast temporary clouds over short term revenue forecasts.

text:
Miami-Dade County property owners can now pay their tax bills with Bitcoin ($BTC), following a payment-system change announced November 9. The new option works online and in person, while the county continues receiving the money in U.S. dollars.

Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez (@darielfernandez) said the change is intended to give residents more ways to pay and modernize public services. Existing payment methods remain available, and using cryptocurrency is entirely optional.

Online users select the cryptocurrency option during checkout. People paying in person can request it, then connect a supported exchange account or digital wallet and authorize the transaction through the payment system.

The cryptocurrency is converted into dollars before the funds reach the Tax Collector’s Office. The office says it does not hold, invest in or manage digital assets, and it receives the full dollar amount of taxes owed.

That structure also keeps transactions within the office’s existing accounting and reconciliation process. The county does not need to maintain cryptocurrency wallets or add a speculative asset to its treasury simply to offer another way of settling a bill.

The distinction matters for the broader debate over crypto adoption. Miami-Dade is adding a payment channel for residents who already use digital assets while keeping public collections denominated in dollars. 

It shows how a government can accommodate cryptocurrency users without making Bitcoin ownership part of its fiscal strategy.

text:
I had just received another call from my son’s hospital.

They were asking about the payment arrangements, and I still had no answer for them.

After the call ended, I couldn’t hold it together anymore.

I stood there quietly crying, trying to wipe my face before anyone noticed.

But the elderly millionaire had seen me.

He approached and asked:

Him: What’s wrong?

I tried to smile.

Me: Nothing. I’m fine.

He looked at me for a moment.

Him: You don’t look fine.

I didn’t want to tell him my problems. I didn’t want anyone feeling sorry for me.

But he kept asking, and eventually, I told him everything.

I explained that my son needed a complicated heart operation, that the hospital had given me an amount I couldn’t afford, and that I had been working two jobs just to keep us going.

I also told him that his father had disappeared before my son was born and that I had been raising the boy alone.

I expected him to offer some kind words and move on.

Instead, he listened without interrupting.

The next morning, he called me into his office.

I walked in, expecting him to discuss his sister’s care or perhaps give me instructions about my work.

But he said something that left me completely confused.

Him: Marry me.

I honestly thought I had heard him incorrectly.

Me: I’m sorry?

Him: Marry me. I’ll pay for your son’s surgery.

I stood there staring at him.

I didn’t know whether he was serious or whether he was confused.

Then he explained the arrangement.

Him: In return, I need someone I can trust beside me when my children discover what I’ve been doing.

I didn’t understand what he meant by that last part.

Me: Your children? What are you talking about?

He didn’t give me the full explanation.

He simply repeated that he would take care of my son’s medical expenses if I agreed to marry him.

I was thirty-four.

He was eighty-two.

And I knew exactly how ridiculous the arrangement would look to everyone who heard about it.

But then I thought about my son.

His condition was getting worse, and the doctors had already warned me that waiting too long could cost him his life.

I couldn’t afford to spend another week wondering where the money would come from.

So I agreed.

Our wedding took place at his enormous estate.

It wasn’t a small private ceremony.

There were reporters waiting outside the gates, white roses covering the staircase, and enough attention surrounding the wedding to make it feel like the entire world had been invited to watch.

I could already imagine what people would say.

A thirty-four-year-old woman marrying an eighty-two-year-old millionaire?

Nobody was going to believe it was about anything other than money.

And his children made sure I understood exactly what they thought of me.

They barely tried to hide their disgust.

At one point, his eldest son leaned toward his sister and whispered something.

I couldn’t hear every word, but I saw them both laugh while looking in my direction.

I knew what they were thinking.

They believed I had married their father for his fortune.

I wanted to turn around and tell them that I had spent years working two jobs, that I had been struggling to raise a child alone, and that I would never have considered marrying a man old enough to be my grandfather if my son’s life wasn’t at stake.

But I didn’t say anything.

What would have been the point?

They had already decided who I was.

So I kept quiet.

My little boy stood beside me in his navy-blue suit, holding my hand.

Scripture warns that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil — not money itself, but the grip it takes on the soul. (2 Timothy 6:20) 

Musk’s story runs the other direction. He poured his PayPal fortune into rockets that exploded and a car company that nearly died. He slept on a couch in a library to save a platform. He signed away shares to every child in America. 

The money moves through his hands like water through soil — it doesn’t pool, it grows things. 

Musk has shown again that he sees his wealth as a responsibility as well as a reward. In the 2026 midterms he put at least $445 million of his own money into the democratic process, and Axios and WIRED estimate the figure at closer to $475 million. He did it out of love for his country and a citizen's sense of duty. 

Musk has long argued that success, his own and everyone else's, depends on freedoms protected by the Rule of Law and the Constitution. In his view, sound governance makes room for lawful, peaceful wealth creation that lifts whole communities, not just a few. 

The results were hard: according to Reuters, only 3 of the 37 House Republicans he backed won, 6 of his 7 Senate picks lost, and Alaska was still too close to call. Yet the intent was plainly the common good rather than personal gain. 

Knowing the man’s record, if the need is there again and he has the means, he may well do it again, if it is good for America and humanity.

Can technology make wealth creation possible for everyone, not just the few? 

Musk often says AI could lead to "universal high income", a future of abundance where goods and services become cheap and plentiful for all.

The interesting part isn't the promise, it is the tools. Grok, Grok Imagine and AI bots are now open to everyday people, not just big companies. A mother, a teacher or a small builder can now create, write, design and serve at a scale that used to need a whole team.

That's real wealth creation: wealth that you own and multiply it through sane leadership. The multiplicative factor is employed because it is what changes lives: value you build with your own hands and mind, multiplied by good tools. The money comes from what you make and offer to others.

The man talking about abundance for all sold his houses. The same man works in the midst of factories according to need, so that he can be close to his employees. He has no trouble living in an Airstream if that would get the foundations being built, done. 

His wealth is also mostly reinvested not spent on luxury. He sees wealth as a tool for building, not for hoarding. That's a principle worth copying and passing on, to the full extent or however possible.

What remains when you strip away the trillion-dollar number is not a man guarding a vault, rather a man who counted the cost, paid it, and kept building. He isn’t  greedy. That’s love with a mission attached. He must have learned this from  someone else.

"But remember the Lord your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.” (Deuteronomy 8:18)

"May those who delight in my vindication shout for joy and gladness; may they always say, ‘Great is the Lord, who delights in the prosperity of his servant.’”(Psalm 35:27)

Meta has announced long-term purchase agreements covering lower-carbon cement, near-zero-emission steel, electric freight and recycled plastics.

Its 12 November update connects AI infrastructure spending with the factories and transport networks needed to build data centres.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗿𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀

Meta says its Sublime Systems agreement supports at least 180,000 tons of lower-carbon cement production. Another agreement supports a Fortera plant in Missouri.

A Stegra agreement covers near-zero-emission primary steel. Expanded electric-trucking work includes the I-10 corridor in California and Arizona.

A MacroCycle agreement supports financing for a US plant targeting 5,000 tons of recycled PET a year.

Those figures describe supported production or planned capacity. They are not a statement that all that material has already reached Meta’s construction sites.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸

Meta says the agreements include Environmental Attribute Certificates: it pays for a verified environmental benefit while the underlying material or service can be used in its local market.

Where possible, it also seeks priority access for future data-centre projects.

That detail helps explain what the company is buying and how it expects the commitments to influence supply.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗯𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘀 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝘄𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵

Our analysis: AI investment reaches well beyond chips and software. Cement producers, steelmakers, recycling companies and freight operators can become part of the infrastructure story.

Long-term customers can make a proposed factory easier to finance. The next test is delivery: plants opening, commercial output increasing and lower-carbon products becoming available to buyers beyond the original sponsor.

For suppliers, the useful questions concern contracted volumes, commissioning dates, verification methods and the cost of meeting the specifications.

For communities, construction announcements need to be followed through into actual local employment and measurable environmental outcomes.

These agreements offer a procurement route towards cleaner industrial supply. Their impact will depend on the projects being built and the promised production arriving.

TaprConnect will track the infrastructure behind AI alongside the models it powers.

$DRTS brings the REGAIN trial's first-ever scientific conference appearance to SNO 2026, the world's preeminent neuro-oncology forum, announcing new interim data alongside an investor call set for Nov. 16, 2026, 8:30 a.m. ET.

🧠 Alpha Tau's REGAIN trial presents updated safety and feasibility data on intratumoral alpha radiation in recurrent glioblastoma at the 31st SNO Annual Meeting. An investor call with the trial's principal investigator follows Monday, Nov. 16, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

https://t.co/v3Jd28TtY3

Recurrent glioblastoma (rGBM) is neuro-oncology's most urgent unresolved challenge. After initial standard treatment including radiation, recurrence is nearly universal, and median overall survival following recurrence typically remains under 12 months. Approved second-line agents offer modest and inconsistent benefit. Approximately 160,000 new glioblastoma cases are diagnosed globally each year, making it the most common and most lethal primary brain tumor in adults.

Alpha DaRT's mechanism is designed to deliver treatment from within the tumor. Radium-224 sources are implanted directly into the tumor via intratumoral delivery. When the radium decays, its short-lived daughter atoms are released and disperse, emitting high-energy alpha particles with the goal of destroying the tumor from within. Since the alpha-emitting atoms diffuse only a short distance, Alpha DaRT aims to primarily affect the tumor and spare surrounding healthy brain tissue. For intracranial delivery, sources are placed through a minimally invasive stereotactic burr hole under real-time neuronavigation, without the need for open craniotomy.

The May 2026 interim analysis of the first three REGAIN patients (enrolled December 2025 through March 2026) showed 100% local disease control and a 67% complete response rate, with no unanticipated serious adverse events and only one associated grade 3 SAE (seizure with temporary paralysis, resolved with steroid administration). These early results prompted the FDA to approve an IDE supplement in October 2026 expanding enrollment from 10 to 20 patients, adding progression-free survival and quality-of-life endpoints, and opening the protocol to IDH-mutant grade 4 tumors. The fifth patient was treated in July 2026. The SNO abstract, titled "First-In-Human Study to Assess the Feasibility and Safety of Intratumoral Diffusing Alpha Emitters for the Treatment of Recurrent Glioblastoma: Safety Interim Analysis (REGAIN)," will be presented by REGAIN principal investigator Dr. Joshua Palmer of The Ohio State University on November 13, 2026.

From a regulatory pathway perspective, REGAIN operates under an FDA Investigational Device Exemption. The company has indicated that the expanded 20-patient cohort may generate data sufficient to support a future market submission for Alpha DaRT in recurrent glioblastoma. The protocol-specified additional interim analysis six months after the fifth patient's treatment in July 2026 is the next internal milestone in the development program, and the data presented at SNO will mark the first externally validated communication of updated clinical findings for this indication.

text:
My sister, Lenora, owned a small wedding venue outside Charlotte, North Carolina.

It wasn’t luxurious, but couples loved it. She had built the business from nothing, starting with a rented farmhouse and gradually expanding it into a beautiful event space.

Her husband, Curtis, handled some of the finances.

Last summer, she discovered he’d taken out several loans using business documents and had fallen behind on repayments.

The lenders began contacting her.

She was devastated, especially when she discovered that some of the money had gone toward Curtis’s failed investment projects.

To prevent the business from being dragged into the financial mess, she decided to sell the property.

The buyer, a retired event planner named Maribel, agreed to purchase the venue, its equipment, and most of its furniture.

But when the inventory was completed, Lenora refused to include the furniture in the bridal preparation room.

Maribel offered extra money.

Lenora still refused.

I thought she was being sentimental until I walked into that room and noticed a small wooden cabinet beside the mirror.

It had dozens of handwritten names inside the drawers.

Each name had a date beside it.

I asked my sister what they were.

She sat down and told me something I’d never known about her business.

text:
Iris Chang, The Chinese in America — 重要語句・英文法40項目

アイリス・チャン（Iris Chang）の The Chinese in America: A Narrative History（2003年）から提示された英文を教材として、重要語句・熟語・構文・文法事項を40項目に整理します。

各項目は、①英文、②日本語訳、③語句・文法分析、④歴史的・社会的意味、という順序で説明します。引用文は、すべてご提示の原文から選びました。

第Ⅰ部　冷戦の終結とアメリカの覇権（1〜8）

1. unanticipated success / pave the way for

英文

Unanticipated success in the international sphere during the 1980s paved the way for unbridled prosperity at home in the 1990s.

和訳

1980年代に国際舞台で収めた予想外の成功は、1990年代に国内で制約のない繁栄を実現する道を切り開いた。

文法・語句

unanticipated：予期されなかった。anticipate（予期する）の過去分詞に否定接頭辞 un- が付いた形容詞。
in the international sphere：国際的な領域において。sphere は活動範囲・分野。
pave the way for A：Aへの道を開く。比喩的な動詞句。
unbridled：抑制されない、際限のない。もとは馬の手綱を外した状態。
at home：ここでは「国内で」。家庭で、という意味ではない。

歴史的意味

冷戦終結という外交的・軍事的成功が、1990年代のアメリカ経済の繁栄につながった、という著者の基本的な歴史解釈を示す冒頭文です。

2. not with A but with B

英文

A forty-year nuclear standoff with the Soviet Union had ended in 1989 not with a bang but with a series of cheers across Eastern Europe.

和訳

ソ連との40年間にわたる核兵器をめぐる対峙は、1989年、爆発音によってではなく、東ヨーロッパ各地の歓声によって終わった。

文法・語句

standoff：対峙、膠着状態。
had ended：過去完了。過去のある時点から振り返った出来事。
not with A but with B：「Aによってではなく、Bによって」という対比構文。
a series of：一連の。
cheers：歓声、喝采。

歴史的意味

核戦争ではなく、民衆によるベルリンの壁の破壊によって冷戦が終結したという劇的な対比です。

3. nothing more than

英文

The Berlin Wall was demolished by people using nothing more than sledgehammers and bare hands.

和訳

ベルリンの壁は、大型ハンマーと素手だけを使う人々によって破壊された。

文法・語句

was demolished：受動態。「破壊された」。
by people：受動態の動作主。
using ...：現在分詞句で people を後置修飾する。
nothing more than：単に～だけ、～にすぎない。
bare hands：素手。
sledgehammer：大型ハンマー。

構文

people who were using ... と関係節に書き換えられます。

歴史的意味

巨大な軍事力を象徴する冷戦体制が、一般市民の手によって崩壊したことを強調しています。

4. one ... after another

英文

When one satellite state after another broke away from the Soviet bloc ...

和訳

ソ連の衛星国家が次々とソビエト陣営から離脱したとき……。

文法・語句

one A after another：Aが次々と。
satellite state：衛星国家。
break away from：～から離脱する。
bloc：政治的・軍事的な国家集団。
when：時を表す従属接続詞。

歴史的意味

東欧諸国がソ連の支配圏から離れていく連鎖的な政治変動を表しています。

5. find oneself + 補語

英文

The United States found itself the winner of the cold war by default.

和訳

アメリカは、成り行きの結果として、自らが冷戦の勝者になっていることに気づいた。

文法・語句

find oneself + 名詞句：自分がある立場に置かれていることに気づく。
itself：再帰代名詞。the United States を指す。
the winner：目的格補語。
by default：相手の不参加・脱落などによって、結果的に。

構文

SVOCの第5文型です。

\[ S+V+O+C \]

The United States = S、found = V、itself = O、the winner = C。

歴史的意味

アメリカが直接ソ連を征服したのではなく、ソ連体制の崩壊によって勝者となったことを示します。

6. seemingly inevitable / materialize

英文

The long-dreaded and seemingly inevitable nuclear apocalypse had never materialized.

和訳

長年恐れられ、避けられないと思われていた核による世界の終末は、結局現実にはならなかった。

文法・語句

long-dreaded：長年恐れられてきた。
seemingly：一見したところ、～と思われる。
inevitable：不可避の。
nuclear apocalypse：核戦争による破滅的終末。
materialize：現実化する。

文法上の要点

long-dreaded と seemingly inevitable は、いずれも名詞 apocalypse を修飾しています。

7. born of the fact that ...

英文

A new era of confidence born of the fact that the United States was now the world’s number one economic and military power.

和訳

アメリカが今や世界第一の経済・軍事大国になったという事実から生まれた、新しい自信の時代。

文法・語句

born of：～から生じた。
the fact that ...：～という事実。
that：同格の内容を導く接続詞。
economic and military power：経済・軍事大国。

構文

the fact と that 以下は同格関係です。

関係代名詞の that ではありません。

8. not by A but by B

英文

He ended the cold war not by backing off from the arms race but by accelerating it.

和訳

彼は軍拡競争から撤退することによってではなく、それを加速させることによって冷戦を終わらせた。

文法・語句

not by A but by B：AによってではなくBによって。
back off from：～から手を引く。
arms race：軍拡競争。
accelerate：加速させる。
前置詞 by の後に動名詞が置かれている。

歴史的意味

レーガンの軍拡政策がソ連の経済的疲弊を促したとする解釈です。これは著者がレーガン支持者の主張として紹介しているものであり、冷戦終結の原因については歴史学上さまざまな見解があります。

第Ⅱ部　軍事技術と新しい経済（9〜16）

9. high-stakes / no-rules / cry uncle

英文

He engaged the Soviet Union in a high-stakes, no-rules poker game.

和訳

彼はソ連を、巨額の賭け金がかかり、ルールもないポーカーゲームに引き込んだ。

文法・語句

engage A in B：AをBに参加させる。

high-stakes：大きな危険や利益がかかった。
no-rules：規則のない。
poker game：ポーカーゲーム。
cry uncle：降参する。アメリカ英語の口語表現。
歴史的意味

軍拡競争を、資金力の乏しい側が先に降参する危険な賭博にたとえています。

10. legacy / by far

英文

The first was an enormous national debt, by far the largest ever.

和訳

第一の遺産は、巨額の国家債務であり、それまでで群を抜いて最大のものだった。

文法・語句

legacy：遺産。肯定的なものにも否定的なものにも使う。

national debt：国家債務、国債残高。
by far：はるかに、断然。
the largest ever：それまでで最大のもの。
ever は最上級を強調する。
11. not solely ... but also ...

英文

The huge expenditures were not solely for weaponry, but also to develop and support new technologies.

和訳

巨額の支出は兵器だけのためではなく、新技術の開発と支援のためにも使われた。

文法・語句

expenditure：支出。

not solely ... but also ...：単に～だけではなく、～も。
weaponry：兵器類。
to develop and support：目的を表す不定詞。
technology：技術。ここでは複数形 technologies。
構文上の注意

for weaponry と to develop ... は形の異なる表現ですが、支出の用途・目的という意味で並列されています。

12. once + 過去分詞

英文

Once unleashed, these technologies placed enormous pressure on the American industrial economy.

和訳

いったん解き放たれると、これらの技術はアメリカの産業経済に巨大な圧力を加えた。

文法・語句

once：いったん～すると。

unleashed：解き放たれた。
place pressure on：～に圧力を加える。
industrial economy：産業経済。
構文

Once unleashed は、主語とbe動詞が省略された副詞節と考えられます。

Once these technologies were unleashed, ...

13. trigger / broad social consequences

英文

Triggering a business revolution that would have broad social consequences.

和訳

広範な社会的影響を及ぼすことになる企業経営上の革命を引き起こしながら。

文法・語句

trigger：引き起こす、誘発する。

business revolution：企業活動・経営の革命。
that would have ...：将来の結果を過去の視点から表す。
consequence：結果、影響。
構文

triggering は前文の技術が経済に圧力を加えたことに伴う結果を示す分詞句です。

14. those who / faster than

英文

Power flowed to those who could create or master new technology faster than their competitors.

和訳

競争相手よりも速く新技術を創造し、あるいは習得できる人々のもとに権力が流れ込んだ。

文法・語句

flow to：～へ流れる、集中する。

those who ...：～する人々。
master：習得する、使いこなす。
faster than：～より速く。
competitor：競争相手。
文法

those は先行詞、who は主格関係代名詞です。

15. It should be no surprise that ...

英文

It should be no surprise that the richest man in the world, Bill Gates, would make his fortune in computers.

和訳

世界一の富豪ビル・ゲイツがコンピューターによって財を成したことは、何ら驚くべきことではない。

文法・語句

It should be no surprise that ...：～は驚くに当たらない。

make one's fortune：財産を築く。
the richest man in the world：世界一の富豪。
would make：過去から見た将来、または歴史的叙述における結果。
構文

形式主語 It を用い、that 節が実質的な内容を表します。

16. greater than that of ...

英文

Greater than that of entire countries, as well as the one hundred million poorest Americans combined.

和訳

国家全体の資産規模をも上回り、さらにアメリカの最も貧しい1億人の資産合計をも上回るほどだった。

文法・語句

greater than：～より大きい。

that of ...：～のそれ。
as well as：～に加えて。
combined：合計した、合わせた。
文法

that は前出の net worth を受ける代名詞です。

比較構文で名詞の反復を避ける働きをしています。

第Ⅲ部　経済格差と中国系移民（17〜24）

17. emerge from ... with ...

英文

The wealthiest one percent of America emerged from the 1990s with 40 percent of the country’s assets.

和訳

アメリカの最富裕層1パーセントは、1990年代を終えた時点で、国の資産の40パーセントを保有していた。

文法・語句

wealthiest：最も裕福な。

emerge from：～を経て現れる、～から抜け出す。

with：所有・付帯状況を示す。
assets：資産。
歴史的意味
情報技術革命の利益が一部の富裕層に集中したことを示しています。

18. indeed / all those without ...

英文

Meanwhile, the poor—indeed, all those without the skills demanded by this new economy—grew poorer.

和訳

その一方で、貧しい人々、いや、それどころか新しい経済が求める技能を持たないすべての人々が、ますます貧しくなっていった。

文法・語句

meanwhile：一方では。

indeed：いや、それどころか。ここでは前の表現を補強・拡張する。

those without ...：～を持たない人々。
demanded by ...：過去分詞による後置修飾。
grow poorer：より貧しくなる。
文法
grow + 形容詞 は状態変化を表す第2文型です。

19. when adjusted for inflation

英文

When adjusted for inflation for 1995 dollars, their holdings shrank from $4,000 to $900.

和訳

1995年のドル価値に換算してインフレ調整を行うと、彼らの保有資産は4,000ドルから900ドルに減少した。

文法・語句

adjust for inflation：インフレを考慮して調整する。

holdings：保有資産。

shrink from A to B：AからBへ縮小する。
when adjusted：受動態の省略構文。
構文
When their holdings were adjusted ... と補って理解できます。

20. one reason ... was that ...

英文

One reason for the disappearance of their wealth was that highly paid manufacturing jobs gradually disappeared.

和訳

彼らの富が失われた一つの理由は、高賃金の製造業の仕事が徐々に消滅したことだった。

文法・語句

one reason for ...：～の一つの理由。

disappearance：消失。

highly paid：高給の。
manufacturing jobs：製造業の仕事。
gradually：徐々に。
構文
S + be + that節 の形で、that 節が理由の内容を説明します。

21. afford + 人 + 物

英文

Which had once afforded working- and middle-class Americans a certain measure of prosperity.

和訳

それらの仕事は、かつて労働者階級と中産階級のアメリカ人に、ある程度の豊かさをもたらしていた。

文法・語句

afford A B：AにBを与える。

working-class：労働者階級の。

middle-class：中産階級の。
a certain measure of：ある程度の。
prosperity：繁栄、豊かさ。
文法
afford は「購入する余裕がある」だけでなく、「機会や利益を与える」という意味でも使われます。

22. farm out / labor-intensive

英文

Corporations farmed labor-intensive work to Third World countries.

和訳

企業は労働集約的な仕事を第三世界の国々へ外注した。

文法・語句

farm out：外注する、下請けに出す。

labor-intensive：労働集約的な。

corporation：企業、法人。
Third World countries：第三世界の国々。当時の歴史的な用語。
歴史的意味
アメリカの製造業の海外移転と、国内の雇用機会の減少を表しています。

23. haves and have-nots

英文

The growing divide between American haves and have-nots was felt keenly.

和訳

アメリカの富める者と持たざる者との間で拡大する格差が、痛切に感じられるようになった。

文法・語句

the haves：富を持つ人々。

the have-nots：富を持たない人々。

divide：分断、格差。
keenly：鋭く、痛切に。
was felt：受動態。
歴史的意味
社会的階級の分断を、非常に簡潔な対照語で表現しています。

24. whether A or B / face crises

英文

Whether they were “high-tech” or “low-tech” immigrants, both groups would face a series of crises.

和訳

彼らが「ハイテク」移民であろうと「ローテク」移民であろうと、どちらの集団も一連の危機に直面することになるのだった。

文法・語句

whether A or B：AであろうとBであろうと。

both groups：両方の集団。

face a crisis：危機に直面する。
a series of：一連の。
would face：過去の視点から見た将来。
歴史的意味
経済的地位が異なっていても、中国系という民族的出自に関係する問題を共有していたことが示されています。

第Ⅳ部　シリコンバレーとインターネット（25〜32）

25. resemble / except that ...

英文

The 1990s resembled the gold rush days, except that the 1990 fortune seekers were mining for nuggets in a new form of sand—silicon.

和訳

1990年代はゴールドラッシュの時代に似ていた。ただし、当時の一攫千金を夢見る人々が金塊を探していたのは、シリコンという新しい種類の砂のなかだった。

文法・語句

resemble：～に似ている。他動詞なので resemble to とはしない。

except that ...：ただし～という点を除いて。

fortune seeker：一攫千金を狙う人。

mine for：～を採掘する。
nugget：天然の金塊。
silicon：ケイ素。
修辞
1849年のゴールドラッシュと1990年代のIT革命を重ねる、歴史的な比喩です。
26. dubbed / already witnessed

英文

In a region dubbed Silicon Valley.

和訳

シリコンバレーと名付けられた地域で。

文法・語句

dub A B：AをBと名付ける。

dubbed：過去分詞による後置修飾。

region：地域。

witness：目撃する、経験する。
構文
a region which was dubbed Silicon Valley と言い換えられます。
27. proximity to / help + 原形不定詞

英文

Proximity to Stanford University ... helped transform the area into a world center of the high-tech industry.

和訳

スタンフォード大学などに近接していたことが、その地域を世界的なハイテク産業の中心地へと変貌させる助けとなった。

文法・語句

proximity to：～への近さ、近接性。

help + 動詞の原形：～する助けとなる。

transform A into B：AをBへ変える。

high-tech industry：先端技術産業。
構文
helped to transform としても意味はほぼ同じです。
28. stretch back to / envision + -ing

英文

The roots of the Internet stretch back to the 1960s, when academic and government experts envisioned building a global computer network.

和訳

インターネットの起源は1960年代にさかのぼる。当時、大学や政府機関の専門家たちは、世界規模のコンピューターネットワークを構築することを構想していた。

文法・語句

roots：起源、根源。

stretch back to：～までさかのぼる。

when：関係副詞。

envision doing：～することを思い描く。
global computer network：世界規模のコンピューターネットワーク。
文法
when は the 1960s を先行詞とする関係副詞です。
29. even in the event of ...

英文

A global computer network that could function even in the event of nuclear war.

和訳

核戦争が起こった場合でさえ機能し続けることのできる、世界規模のコンピューターネットワーク。

文法・語句

that could function：関係代名詞節。

function：機能する。

even：～でさえ。

in the event of：～の場合には。
nuclear war：核戦争。
構文
that は network を先行詞とする主格関係代名詞です。
30. link together / through telephone lines

英文

Which linked together a few computers at major universities through telephone lines.

和訳

それは、主要大学の少数のコンピューターを電話回線を通じて相互に接続した。

文法・語句

link together：互いに結びつける。

a few：少数の。

major universities：主要大学。

through：～を通じて。
telephone lines：電話回線。
文法
which は先行する研究契約・計画を受ける関係代名詞です。
31. by posting / government-funded

英文

Academics would exchange information with colleagues by posting messages on this cyberspace bulletin board.

和訳

研究者たちは、このサイバー空間の掲示板にメッセージを投稿することで、同僚たちと情報を交換していた。

文法・語句

exchange A with B：BとAを交換する。

by doing：～することによって。

post messages：メッセージを投稿する。

bulletin board：掲示板。
government-funded：政府の資金で運営される。
文法
ここでの would exchange は、過去の習慣的行為を表しています。
32. crash into public awareness

英文

This network crashed into public awareness when companies ... began offering the general public unlimited access.

和訳

企業が一般大衆に無制限のアクセスを提供し始めると、このネットワークは突如として一般社会の注目を集めた。

文法・語句

crash into：激しく入り込む。

public awareness：一般社会の認知。

begin doing：～し始める。

offer A B：AにBを提供する。
unlimited access：無制限の利用。
修辞
crashed into は、インターネットの急激な普及を勢いのある動詞で表現しています。
第Ⅴ部　ドットコム企業とYahoo!（33〜40）

33. spawn / a rash of / startup

英文

The unprecedented growth ... spawned a rash of new Silicon Valley startups.

和訳

前例のない成長は、シリコンバレーで新興企業の設立ラッシュを引き起こした。

文法・語句

unprecedented：前例のない。

spawn：生み出す、引き起こす。

a rash of：相次ぐ発生、急増。

startup：新興企業。

語法
a rash of は、もともと発疹のように急に広がる現象を連想させる表現です。
34. fresh out of school
英文

These companies were typically run by young men and women fresh out of school.

和訳

これらの企業は、典型的には学校を卒業したばかりの若い男女によって経営されていた。

文法・語句

be run by：～によって経営される。

typically：典型的には。

fresh out of school：学校を出たばかりの。

fresh：ここでは「～したばかりの」という意味。

文法
fresh out of school は young men and women を後ろから説明する形容詞句です。
35. in lieu of / stock options
英文

Most of these cash-poor start-ups offered employees stock options in lieu of high pay.

和訳

資金の乏しい新興企業の大部分は、高額の給与の代わりに従業員へストックオプションを与えた。

文法・語句

cash-poor：現金資金に乏しい。

offer A B：AにBを与える。

stock option：株式購入選択権。

in lieu of：～の代わりに。

high pay：高額の給与。
構文
offer employees stock options は第4文型（SVOO）です。
36. get in on the ground floor / IPO
英文

A rush to get in on the ground floor of a brand-new industry ... led to oversubscribed initial public offerings (IPOs).

和訳

まったく新しい産業に初期段階から参加しようとする投資家の殺到が、申し込み超過の新規株式公開をもたらした。

文法・語句

get in on the ground floor：事業の初期段階から参加する。

brand-new：真新しい。

lead to：～をもたらす。

oversubscribed：募集数を超える申し込みがある。

initial public offering：新規株式公開。
歴史的意味
IT企業への投資熱が、株価の急騰をもたらした状況です。
37. bid up / despite the fact that ...
英文

The outstanding stock was then bid up to astronomical levels, despite the fact that most of these companies had not yet shown a profit.

和訳

これらの企業の大部分がまだ利益を上げていなかったにもかかわらず、発行済み株式の価格は天文学的な水準にまで競り上げられた。

文法・語句

outstanding stock：発行済み株式。

bid up：競り上げる。

astronomical levels：天文学的な水準。

despite the fact that：～という事実にもかかわらず。

show a profit：利益を計上する。
文法
despite は前置詞なので、直接 despite that S + V とはしません。despite the fact that S + V という形を用います。
38. join the ranks of / expect to
英文

Many young Americans of Chinese heritage ... joined the ranks of twenty-somethings with million-dollar portfolios.

和訳

中国系の若いアメリカ人の多くが、100万ドル規模の株式資産を保有する20代の人々の仲間入りを果たした。

文法・語句

of Chinese heritage：中国系の出自を持つ。

join the ranks of：～の仲間入りをする。

twenty-something：20代の人。

portfolio：投資資産の組み合わせ。

expect to do：～することを期待する。
歴史的意味
中国系アメリカ人の社会的イメージが、低賃金労働者からIT企業家へと変化したことを示しています。
39. grow out of / refer to as
英文

His company grew out of a simple idea: to create a directory of his favorite sites on the international network of information now referred to as the World Wide Web.

和訳

彼の会社は、単純な着想から生まれた。それは、現在ワールド・ワイド・ウェブと呼ばれる国際的な情報ネットワーク上で、お気に入りのサイトの案内目録を作成するというものだった。

文法・語句

grow out of：～から生まれる。

simple idea：単純な着想。

directory：案内目録、一覧。

refer to A as B：AをBと呼ぶ。

now referred to as ...：現在～と呼ばれている。
構文
コロン以下の to create ... は、前の a simple idea の内容を具体的に説明しています。
40. so ... that / force A to do / exponentially
英文

Their directory grew so popular that its level of traffic crashed the computer servers at Stanford, forcing the company to move off campus.

和訳

彼らの案内目録は非常に人気を集めたため、アクセスの集中によってスタンフォード大学のコンピューターサーバーが停止し、会社はキャンパスの外へ移転せざるを得なくなった。

文法・語句

so + 形容詞 + that ...：非常に～なので……。

traffic：通信量、アクセス数。

crash a server：サーバーを停止させる。

force A to do：Aに～することを強いる。

off campus：キャンパスの外へ。
exponentially：指数関数的に。後続のYahoo!の企業価値増大を表す重要語。
構文
forcing the company ... は、前の出来事の結果を表す分詞構文です。
Ⅵ．40項目の文法的総括
文法・語法の分野該当項目学習上の重要点過去完了・過去から見た未来2、6、13、15、24、31歴史叙述の時間関係受動態・過去分詞3、7、12、18、19、26、34動作主と修飾関係関係代名詞・関係副詞7、14、21、28、29、30名詞の後置修飾不定詞・動名詞8、11、27、28、31、38、39目的・手段・内容分詞構文12、13、19、40時・条件・結果比較・対照構文2、8、16、24、25歴史的対比の表現第4・第5文型5、21、32、35動詞と補語・目的語経済・経営の専門語彙10、17、19、22、35〜38経済史を読む基礎比喩・慣用表現1、9、23、25、32、36アメリカ英語の修辞

Ⅶ．アイリス・チャンの英文の特徴

この文章は、歴史叙述と経済分析を組み合わせた英語教材として興味深いものです。

第一に、チャンは not A but B、whether A or B、haves and have-nots など、対比を作る構文を繰り返し使用しています。これによって、冷戦の勝者と敗者、富裕層と貧困層、ハイテク移民とローテク移民という社会的な対立を浮き彫りにしています。

第二に、gold rush、mining for nuggets、ground floor、crashed into public awareness など、具体的なイメージを喚起する比喩が目立ちます。特に1849年のカリフォルニア・ゴールドラッシュと1990年代のシリコンバレーを重ねる手法は、中国系移民の歴史を長期的に捉えるうえで重要です。
第三に、had ended、would face、would make などの時制表現を用いて、過去の出来事と、その後に生じる歴史的帰結を結びつけています。
第四に、assets、net worth、stock options、IPOs、market capitalization など、経済学・経営学の専門語彙を、移民の社会史の説明に組み込んでいます。
この抜粋の核心は、アメリカの技術革命が中国系移民に新しい成功の機会を与える一方で、同じ中国系移民社会の内部に深刻な経済的・社会的分断を生み出した、という点にあります。
その意味で、アイリス・チャンの英文は、英文法の教材であると同時に、アメリカ経済史、移民史、情報技術史を横断して学ぶための優れた読解素材になっています。

text: This last-stage arms race left the United States two legacies. The first was an enormous national debt, by far the largest ever. But the huge expenditures were not solely for weaponry, but also to develop and support new technologies, especially in computers and information processing. Once unleashed, these technologies placed enormous pressure on the American industrial economy, triggering a business revolution that would have broad social consequences. In the new economy, power flowed to those who could create or master new technology faster than their competitors. It should be no surprise that the richest man in the world, Bill Gates, would make his fortune in computers, as the co-founder and leader of Microsoft. By the end of the decade, his net worth was estimated at $85 billion, greater than that of entire countries, as well as the one hundred million poorest Americans combined. The wealthiest one percent of America emerged from the 1990s with 40 percent of the country’s assets, twice as much as they had held only two decades earlier. Meanwhile, the poor—indeed, all those without the skills demanded by this new economy—grew poorer. According to economist Edward N. Wolff, between 1983 and 1995, poor, working-class, and lower-middle-class families—the bottom 40 percent of American society—lost 80 percent of their net worth; when adjusted for inflation for 1995 dollars, their holdings shrank from $4,000 to $900. One reason for the disappearance of their wealth was that highly paid manufacturing jobs, which had once afforded working- and middle-class Americans a certain measure of prosperity, gradually disappeared as corporations farmed labor-intensive work to Third World countries. The growing divide between American haves and have-nots was felt keenly not only among whites and blacks, but within the ethnic Chinese population as well. The decade of the 1990s would witness the development of a two-tiered society among new Chinese arrivals: the rise of an elite group of highly visible, educated people, and the disappearance of thousands of illegal aliens into servile positions in underground economy, where they were forced to endure dismal working conditions. But whether they were “high-tech” or “low-tech” immigrants, both groups would face a series of crises during the 1990s related to their Chinese ethnicity. For “high-tech” Chinese, the 1990s resembled the gold rush days, except that the 1990 fortune seekers were mining for nuggets in a new form of sand—silicon. The modern gold rush, like the 1849 gold rush, occurred in northern California, but this time south of San Francisco, in a region dubbed Silicon Valley. The area had already witnessed the birth of the personal computer revolution in the 1970s, when two young men, Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak, started the Apple corporation, selling desktop computers they had built in their garage. Proximity to Stanford University in Palo Alto, the University of California at Berkeley, and San Francisco as a major port for trade with Asia, helped transform the area into a world center of the high-tech industry.   But an even bigger revolution erupted in the 1990s—the Internet revolution. The roots of the Internet stretch back to the 1960s, when academic and government experts envisioned building a global computer network that could function even in the event of nuclear war. Preliminary research at MIT led to a government contract with the Advanced Research Projects Agency (ARPA), which linked together a few computers at major universities through telephone lines. For the next two decades, a small community of academics—mostly computer scientists, engineers, and librarians—would exchange information with colleagues by posting messages on this cyberspace bulletin board, a government-funded system of electronic mail (or “e-mail”). In the early 1990s, this network crashed into public awareness when companies such as America Online, CompuServe, and Prodigy began offering the general public unlimited access to this new form of communication for a monthly fee. The unprecedented growth of what came to be called the Internet spawned a rash of new Silicon Valley startups. Known as “dotcoms,” these companies were typically run by young men and women fresh out of school. To attract employees with the special computer talents needed, most of these cash-poor start-ups offered employees stock options in lieu of high pay. When the companies were able to offer their stock to the general public, a rush to get in on the ground floor of a brand-new industry that seemed to have an unbounded future led to oversubscribed initial public offerings (IPOs). The outstanding stock was then bid up to astronomical levels, despite the fact that most of these companies had not yet shown a profit (and many never would). Before the dotcom bubble burst, many young Americans of Chinese heritage, both founders and those who had received stock options, joined the ranks of twenty-somethings with million-dollar portfolios, with many expecting to accumulate their first billion before age thirty. This kind of wealth, noted Stanford historian Gordon Chang, transformed the image of the young Asian American male from “son of a laborer or laundryman” to “future Internet millionaire.” One icon of the dotcom world was Jerry Yang, the billionaire founder of Yahoo!, an Internet search engine and Web service. Born in Taiwan in 1967, Yang moved with his family to San Jose, California, while he was still a teenager. His company grew out of a simple idea: to create a directory of his favorite sites on the international network of information now referred to as the World Wide Web. By the early 1990s, any location on the Web could be accessed by typing the location’s Web address into an address box. Yang helped develop the first popular search tool for the Web, so that users could type names or relevant phrases into a search box, and have the search engine find all documents with a string of characters matching those in the search box. In a tiny office trailer at Stanford University, Yang, then a twenty-six-year-old doctoral student in electrical engineering, and his classmate, David Filo, sorted hyperlinks by subject and posted them on the Web. Their directory grew so popular that its level of traffic crashed the computer servers at Stanford, forcing the company to move off campus. Yang and Filo took Yahoo! public and watched its worth increase exponentially as the Internet market exploded. By March 2000, the market capitalization of Yahoo! had exceeded $100 billion.

Spencer Hatcher: From the Shenandoah Valley to Nashville

"Spencer Hatcher is a country music singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist whose roots run deep in Virginia’s Shenandoah Valley. Raised on a family farm near Timberville in Rockingham County, Hatcher grew up surrounded by the sounds of bluegrass, traditional country, and church music. Those influences helped shape a musical identity grounded in family, faith, and small-town life.

Music was part of Hatcher’s childhood. He began learning the mandolin around age eight and took up the five-string banjo by age twelve. Performing with his father and younger brother, Connor, in the family group The Hatcher Boys, he developed his skills at churches, festivals, and community events throughout the region. His mother, Holly, also contributed to the family’s musical foundation through her involvement in church music.

Hatcher later attended East Tennessee State University, studying business and bluegrass music. As his interests expanded beyond bluegrass, he began pursuing a sound inspired by artists such as George Strait, Johnny Cash, Keith Whitley, and George Jones. In 2020, he formed his own country band with Connor, and a widely shared Johnny Cash cover helped introduce his music to a larger online audience.

His momentum continued through regional performances and recordings. He released “Like a Friday Night” in 2022 and played more than 150 shows in 2023. In 2024, he signed with Nashville-based Stone Country Records. The following year brought his debut EP, Honky Tonk Hideaway, and representation by WME. His 2026 releases included the EP Hot Weather, Cold Beer and the single “Keep the Sad People Happy.”

Behind those achievements is a story of resilience. Hatcher recovered from serious injuries sustained in a 2024 fall and faced profound family loss in 2025 following the death of his mother. Through difficult seasons, music and community have remained important parts of his journey.

Although Nashville has opened new doors, Hatcher’s artistic identity remains unmistakably Virginian. His traditional country sound reflects the people, places, and values of the Shenandoah Valley, connecting his Rockingham County upbringing with audiences far beyond the mountains he calls home. For listeners, his music offers a meeting place between old-fashioned country traditions and contemporary storytelling."

FIRST-CLASS RELIC OF ST. CARLO ACUTIS TO VISIT TWO U.S. CHURCHES THIS NOVEMBER

A first-class relic of St. Carlo Acutis, consisting of a portion of his pericardium—the membrane surrounding the heart—will be brought to the United States this November for public veneration.

The relic is being transported from Assisi, Italy, by Msgr. Anthony Figueiredo and is scheduled to visit two confirmed Catholic locations.

November 11 – Basilica of Saint Mary, Alexandria, Virginia

On Veterans Day, the relic will be welcomed at the Basilica of Saint Mary. The program will begin with a special Mass at 9:00 a.m., followed by a talk and blessing led by Msgr. Figueiredo.

November 15–17 – Our Lady of Mt. Carmel Parish, Nutley, New Jersey

The relic will then visit Our Lady of Mt. Carmel Parish for a three-day spiritual gathering. Activities will include Holy Mass, public veneration, Eucharistic Adoration, the Sacrament of Reconciliation, and spiritual talks.

WHO IS ST. CARLO ACUTIS?

St. Carlo Acutis, often called the first millennial saint, died of leukemia in 2006 at just 15 years old. He was canonized in 2025 and is especially remembered for his deep devotion to the Holy Eucharist and his use of digital technology to share the Catholic faith.

His life continues to inspire young people and Catholics around the world to place Christ at the center of their lives.

The visit of his relic offers the faithful an opportunity to reflect on his example of holiness and seek his intercession through prayer.

🙏 St. Carlo Acutis, pray for us!

text:
I haven’t heard this much debate about the departure of a @Raiders quarterback since Derek Carr was eating his first bowl of gumbo.

It feels like most fans are ok with the trade part, it’s the compensation that has given some people agita.

“All we got was a third round pick?”

“Why didn’t Spytek hold out for a second?”

“I wouldn’t have traded Cousins unless I got a one.”

“The Raiders should’ve got a pick AND a player.”

“I miss Josh McDaniels!”

Ok, nobody has ever said that last part.

Thanks to the daily infusion of twitter General Managers and Armchair Quarterbacks, many of us expected the Godfather offer from the Vikings.

A first round pick, Alan Page, a guided tour of Paisley Park and unlimited rides on the Mall of America rollercoaster.

Well that didn’t happen.

Do I wish the third was a second or that the third was the better of Minnesota’s two thirds or that the third could turn into a second if ________?

Of course, but the reality is, the Raiders didn’t just trade for a draft pick.

Along with Kirk Cousins, we also sent a $10 million bill to the Vikings so they could pay his guaranteed money for 2027 AND, as a bonus, we now get the opportunity to start the number one overall pick from last year’s draft.

After watching the Minnesota offense set back the sport of football by 100 years on Monday night, we all knew the Raiders had the leverage.

Some might say, we had them by the purple balls, which I hear is worse than blue.

But that didn’t mean they would sell the farm for half a season of the third oldest starting quarterback in the league who has won exactly one playoff game in his 15 years.

I am not here to bury Caesar or Kirk Cousins, I appreciate EVERYTHING he did to help us look like a football team and prepare our rookie for the primetime.  Other than Rich Bisaccia, Cousins had the best nine-game career of anyone in Silver and Black and that includes DeAngelo Hall.

But the fact that he played better than Geno Smith + Kenny Pickett + Gardner Minshew + Desmond Ridder + Jimmy Garoppolo + Brian Hoyer (and Aidan O’Connell) doesn’t mean he was gonna be traded for a first or second round pick.

According to @AlbertBreer the Vikings were willing to part with a FIFTH round pick for Cousins before Spytek and Co. held out for what they got.

With the trade deadline clock ticking, the Raiders finally agreed to trade their 38-year-old quarterback, who can’t run and can’t throw the ball over 30 yards in the air, for a third round draft pick.

By any measure, that’s a good deal.

The Jets traded the Raiders a third round pick in 2024 for Davante Adams, when we thought he was bad.

We traded that same pick a year later to Seattle for Geno Smith, when we thought he was good.

28 Hall of Famers have been drafted in the third round, including Art Shell of the Raiders in 1968.

The Raiders also drafted the wrong Byron Young in the third round, so anything is possible.

I’m calling it now, even with the return of Kirko Chainz, the Minnesota Vikings will finish last in the NFC North.

You like that?

They are playing in the toughest division in football and of their nine remaining games, six are against current playoff teams.

As much as I sincerely appreciate Kirk Cousins’ time in Vegas, and truly wish him all the best, I am very excited about what lies ahead for us.

And whether we got a fifth round pick or a fifth of vodka, Monday’s trade was not about Kirk Cousins, it was about trading in our old car for the new one.

And I’ll drink to that.

text:
🙏❤️ A Special Morning Prayer — Lord, Let Today Be Different
Heavenly Father,
This morning, I come before You not asking for riches, fame, or anything this world can offer. I come asking for something far more valuable: a heart at peace, a mind free from worry, and a soul that never loses faith in You.
Lord, somewhere this morning, a mother is crying, a father is struggling, a child is hungry, a veteran feels forgotten, and someone is sitting alone wondering whether anybody in this world truly cares.
Father, let them feel Your presence today.
Walk into the hospital rooms where families are praying for miracles. Sit beside the elderly who haven't received a phone call. Comfort the homeless sleeping on cold streets. Lift the brokenhearted who are grieving someone they would give anything to hold just one more time.
Lord, remember those who have lost everything but still wake up and whisper, "Thank You, Jesus, for another day."
And Father, I have one special request this morning.
Please heal the things in us that nobody else can see.
Heal the friendships that ended without understanding. Heal the families divided by anger and pride. Heal the hearts carrying guilt, regret, and words they wish they could take back.
Teach us to forgive even when we never receive an apology. Teach us to love without allowing others to destroy our peace. And give us the wisdom to recognize the difference between someone who needs our help and someone who only wants to take advantage of our kindness.
Lord, if someone crosses my path today who is hurting, let me be a reason they smile. If someone is hungry, help me share what I have. If someone feels invisible, remind me to acknowledge them.
And if today is the last day someone gets to spend with a person they love, please don't let them waste it on anger.
Because tomorrow is never promised, Father.
We spend so much of our lives chasing things that cannot follow us into eternity, while the greatest treasures You ever gave us are the people we sometimes forget to appreciate.
Today, Lord, I ask You to protect every person reading this prayer, including those who don't believe in You, those who have turned away from You, and those who are desperately trying to find their way back.
Bless our families, our friends, our enemies, our military, our first responders, and every innocent soul suffering around this world.
And for those of us who have buried people we love, remind us that grief is the price of having loved someone deeply, but love itself never becomes meaningless.
Father, when this day ends, I don't need to say I conquered the world.
I just want to be able to say:
I treated somebody with kindness.
I forgave somebody who hurt me.
I helped somebody who had less than me.
And through every struggle, I never stopped trusting You.
Lord, don't just change what happens around us today.
Change what happens inside our hearts.
In the mighty, precious, and everlasting name of Jesus Christ, our Lord and Savior.
AMEN. 🙏❤️✝️
One more sunrise. One more chance to forgive. One more chance to love. One more chance to become the person God created us to be.
GOD FIRST. LOVE ALWAYS. TOMORROW IS NEVER PROMISED. ❤️🙏

#HarryPotter #OrderofthePhoenix #Book5 #malfoid #Malfoid #malfoygirl 

"And Sirius is dead!"

Harry's voice cracked on the last word, but he scarcely noticed. He was too angry, too sick with the memory of Sirius falling backwards through the Veil, of Bellatrix Lestrange laughing, of Lucius Malfoy standing among the Death Eaters who had lured him to the Ministry in the first place. And now here was Lucius's daughter, looking at him with those enormous grey eyes, expecting—what? That he would put his arms around her and pretend her father had had nothing to do with it?

Draconia had gone very pale. Her eyes glistened, and she opened her mouth, only to shut it again when Harry glared at her. He knew what was coming. She would tell him that her father had only been following orders, that he wasn't really a bad man, that Harry didn't understand. He had heard her defend Lucius often enough over the years.

But Draconia only looked down at her hands.

"I know," she said, so quietly that Harry almost missed it.

"Do you?" he demanded. "Do you have any idea what it's like to lose someone like that? He was the only family I had left!"

He knew, even as he said it, that it wasn't quite fair. There was Ron and Hermione, and there were the Weasleys. There was Draconia herself. None of them was Sirius, though. None of them had been his father's best friend or offered him a home where he might finally have belonged.

A tear slipped down Draconia's cheek. She wiped it away angrily, as though furious with herself for crying.

"I'm not going to defend my father, Harry. I know what he did. And I know I've said horrible things about your family. I was cruel, and stupid, and I can't take any of it back." She swallowed and tried to meet his eyes. "But I love you. I do. And I wish there was something I could say that would help, but there isn't, is there?"

Harry wanted to stay angry. It would have been so much easier if she had argued with him, if she had made some ridiculous excuse for Lucius that he could tear to pieces. Instead, she stood there looking utterly miserable, and he found that he couldn't bear to look at her either.

He turned away, pressing the heels of his hands against his eyes. It was no good. Sirius was still dead. Harry could shout himself hoarse, smash every window in the corridor, or spend the rest of his life hating the Malfoys, and Sirius would still be lying somewhere beyond that dreadful curtain, where Harry could never reach him.

"I just want him back," he said, hardly recognising his own voice.

"Oh, Harry."

Draconia moved towards him, hesitated, and then put her arms around him. He stiffened at first. He was still angry with her father, still angry with practically everybody, and some stubborn part of him resented being comforted when there was nothing in the world worth feeling better about.

Then she drew him against her, one hand resting on the back of his head, and he remembered Sirius laughing in the kitchen at Grimmauld Place.

That did it.

Harry clutched at the back of her robes and buried his face against her shoulder. He tried desperately to keep himself under control, but his breath caught, his shoulders shook, and suddenly he was crying harder than he had since he was a little boy.

Draconia held him more tightly. Harry could feel her trembling too, and once she pressed her cheek against his hair and whispered his name. Otherwise, she left him alone to cry, though she never loosened her arms.

He had no idea how long they stood there. His glasses had slipped crookedly down his nose, his face was wet, and he had made a dreadful mess of Draconia's robes. Under ordinary circumstances she would have complained about that, and the thought made him give a miserable little laugh against her shoulder.

"What's funny?" she murmured.

"Nothing." He sniffed. "You'd normally hex me for getting your robes wet."

Draconia drew back just enough to look at him. Her own cheeks were streaked with tears.

"Well, they're rather ugly robes anyway."

Harry gave another shaky laugh, and she managed a small smile before pulling him close again.

He still wanted Sirius back. He wanted it so badly that it hurt to breathe, and he knew he would wake tomorrow and remember all over again that Sirius was gone. But for now Draconia was there, holding him in the deserted corridor, and Harry was grateful that she hadn't listened when he'd told her to leave.

text:
⚡️ Decoding WhiteOak Capital Diversified Equity Small Cap Active FoF: How Different Are Its Five Funds?

Let'scompare their 31 October 2026 portfolios to understand what this combination actually brings together. 🧵👇

1. What does the FoF own?

• Abakkus Small Cap - 24.13%
• Bajaj Finserv Small Cap - 19.56%
• Motilal Oswal Small Cap - 19.38%
• DSP Small Cap - 19.27%
• Groww Small Cap - 14.46%

Together: 96.80% of the FoF.

2. Stock overlap is surprisingly low

Weighted overlap ranges from just 4.18% to 13.13%.

Lowest: DSP × Motilal - 4.18%
Highest: Bajaj × DSP - 13.13%

Across the five portfolios, there are 287 distinct ordinary stocks. 

3. The portfolios differ in size

October month-end AUM:

• DSP: ₹20,252 crore
• Motilal: ₹8,096 crore
• Abakkus: ₹3,351 crore
• Bajaj: ₹2,735 crore
• Groww: ₹1,020 crore

That is a wide range of operating scale. Smaller AUM may offer flexibility, but size alone does not establish investment skill or liquidity.

4. Deployment also differs

Cash/TREPS plus net receivables/payables:

• DSP: 12.07%
• Abakkus: 6.06%
• Groww: 5.84%
• Motilal: 2.59%
• Bajaj: 1.72%

These are october month end data. A high cash position currently does not establish a permanently defensive strategy.

5.  Shared sectors, different weights

• Abakkus: relatively balanced across industrial products (8.2%), banks (7.8%) and auto components (7.8%).

• Bajaj: higher exposure to pharmaceuticals (12.3%) and industrial products (11.8%).

• Motilal: tilts towards consumer durables (9.9%), industrial manufacturing (9.3%), retailing (8.6%) and healthcare services (8.0%).

• DSP: substantial exposure to auto components (14.7%) and industrial products (14.3%), followed by consumer durables (11.3%).

• Groww: emphasises auto components (15.7%), electrical equipment (12.1%) and industrial products (10.0%).

The basket diversifies stock selection more clearly than sector exposure. Several funds share auto and industrial bets, while Motilal provides a relatively different sector mix.

6. Are these five completely different styles?

The stated frameworks include:

• Abakkus - MEETS: Management, Earnings, Events/Trends, Timing and Structural opportunity. Growth investing with valuation discipline.

• Bajaj - INQUBE: INformation edge, QUantitative edge and BEhavioural edge. Combines growth, quality and value opportunities.

• Motilal - QGLP: Quality, Growth, Longevity and Price. Focuses on quality businesses with sustainable growth at an appropriate price.

• DSP: Bottom-up stock selection with a business-ownership mindset, focusing on management quality, scalable businesses, sustainable competitive advantages and valuation discipline.

• Groww - QGaRP: Quality and Growth at a Reasonable Price. Seeks quality businesses with growth potential and reasonable entry valuations.

Quality, growth and reasonable valuations recur across several managers.

7. Low overlap does not mean low correlation

Over the short common window of 20 March–30 October 2026, daily-return correlations ranged from 0.86 to 0.95.

So the basket diversifies company-specific and manager-specific bets, while retaining substantial shared small-cap market risk.

8. Market-cap mix adds some variation

Small-cap allocations ranged from 77.00% to 84.86%, while mid-cap exposure ranged from 1.86% to 12.00%.

Abakkus had the highest large-cap allocation at 6.20%; Motilal had the highest mid-cap allocation at 12.00%. All five remained predominantly small-cap portfolios.

9. Reported valuations differ too

Trailing 12-month portfolio P/E:

• Abakkus: 28.52×
• Bajaj Finserv: 43.60×
• Motilal Oswal: 32.30×
• DSP: 30.11×
• Groww: 23.20×

This shows different reported valuation levels within the basket. A higher P/E alone does not establish overvaluation-sector mix, earnings quality, growth expectations and calculation conventions also matter.

10. Track record deserves attention

Abakkus and Groww together account for 38.59% of FoF NAV. Both were under a year old at October-end.

Including Bajaj, 58.15% sits in schemes under 18 months old.

The selection case therefore needs qualitative manager research alongside scheme performance history.

11. How does WhiteOak say it selects funds?

WhiteOak’s SID lists manager process, valuations, liquidity, overlap and risk-return characteristics among its allocation considerations. Value Research’s CEO interview write-up describes quantitative screening followed by questionnaires and manager meetings. The sources reviewed do not explain the individual fund-selection scores or precise portfolio weights.

12.  Takeaway

The strength of this basket lies in combining different stock-picking decisions and manager processes. Low overlap provides meaningful company-level diversification. September disclosures also show variation in reported valuations and market-cap allocations.

However, recurring sector exposures and high return correlations over the short common history indicate substantial sensitivity to the same small-cap market cycle. Five fund names and different P/E ratios do not establish five independent investment styles.

WhiteOak’s potential value lies in manager due diligence, ongoing monitoring and rebalancing. Whether that produces better investor outcomes must be demonstrated over a full market cycle, after combined costs.

The portfolio has a reasonable diversification case. Its ability to deliver superior outcomes remains unproven.

text:
Another find.

At Sardis, archaeologists excavated an altar of the Mother Goddess decorated with lions, situated directly within an ancient gold-refining district.

Metallurgy + Mother Goddess + Lions.

And there's a second, independently documented connection between Thrace and Denmark.

Sardis — Lydia, sixth century BCE

The Sardis excavations document lion sculptures associated with the altar of Cybele in the Lydian gold-refining sector. This is a physical overlap between precious-metal processing and the lion-associated Mother Goddess, rather than an association inferred solely from mythology.

https://t.co/UcZZu2NW9Q

That matters because the literary Idaean Dactyl tradition connects metallurgy, Phrygian Mount Ida, and the Mother Goddess. Sardis offers an archaeological setting in which some of those ideas occupy the same physical landscape.

The National Museum of Denmark explicitly compares the treatment of the deer and lion on a Rogozen silver pitcher with animal imagery on the Gundestrup cauldron.

It also identifies the metalworking technique and style of Gundestrup as closely related to Thracian silverwork, while acknowledging Celtic elements in the imagery. Its proposed manufacturing region is the Thracian–Celtic contact zone around present-day northwestern Bulgaria and southwestern Romania.

https://t.co/tkpEb64Cy4

At Carvoran Roman Fort, near Hadrian's Wall, an inscription dating to approximately AD 197–217 describes a heavenly goddess associated with the Lion and explicitly identifies her with the Mother of the Gods, Ceres, and the Syrian Goddess.

RIB 1791 — ancient religious dedication

“The Virgin in her heavenly place rides upon the Lion”

The remaining text combines celestial symbolism with agriculture, law, civic foundation, and the worship of the Mother of the Gods.

𝗕𝗟𝗨𝗙: Putin wants a repeat of Oleshky, where a humanitarian pause gave Russian forces a drone-free window to rotate, fortify and resupply. He claims control of Kostiantynivka, which the Kremlin declared captured in July, yet says Russia needs five days to clear mines near the city. With the Sloviansk front stabilized and Russian losses mounting, the pause would buy movement in an area of intense Russian pressure in Donetsk, at a time when Ukraine has gained significant tactical advantages near Sloviansk and stabilized the front near Konstantynivka.

On 12 November, Putin told U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner he wants an Oleshky-style joint humanitarian mission in Kostiantynivka. The last pause gave the Russian Federation (RF) a drone-free window to rotate and resupply. This proposal could provide a similar window in an area of intense Russian pressure in Donetsk.

The Oleshky pause ran 27 October to 1 November. Ukraine's General Staff recorded Russian unit rotations, fortified positions, expanded anti-drone protection along roads and increased ammunition deliveries. The Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) held fire and stayed within the agreed terms. Asked about the report, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called regrouping during a ceasefire "standard practice," which tacitly confirms the practice.

Putin claims Russia controls Kostiantynivka, a city Moscow declared captured in July. In the same breath, he says Russian forces need five days to clear mines near the city. DeepState and Black Bird Group show heavy fighting, with Russian forces advancing from the eastern outskirts. A city held since July does not need five days of mine clearance on its approaches.

The Sloviansk front has stabilized. AFU drone teams and artillery have moved forward through the forests between Mykolaivka and Lyman, and Russian sources describe a growing need to replace losses. ISW assessed that Russia suffered a net territorial loss of 27.29 km² across Ukraine in October, its second consecutive month of net losses. Russian gains have been limited and have come at a high personnel cost, while Russian force generation has struggled to offset losses. The heaviest Russian activity has shifted to the Kostiantynivka-Druzhkivka axis.

Not surprisingly, the offer went to Washington, not Kyiv or the UN. Accepting it means treating Russia's claim to Kostiantynivka as the starting point and giving Russian units five days of movement free from Ukrainian drones. Oleshky already showed what Russian forces do with that time.

If the White House pressures Ukraine into the ceasefire, Russian forces will use the five-day drone-free window to rotate depleted units, push ammunition and equipment forward, strengthen anti-drone cover, and consolidate the eastern and northwestern footholds they already have, exactly as they did in Oleshky.

In short, Russia is currently losing ground near Sloviansk and spending men it struggles to replace. A humanitarian pause on the southern approach to Kramatorsk would buy back the one thing drones have taken away, which is safe movement.

text:
He shot his 18-year-old classmate twice in the head while the boy was driving and begging for his life. Then he dragged the body into a ditch, covered it with dirt and a stick, and walked away down a dark country road. He did it for one reason: he wanted to know what killing someone feels like.

His name is Jerrod Murray.

Asked why he chose Generro: "He would have had the least impact. He didn't have many friends."

Remorse? "No."

December 5, 2012. Jerrod Murray and Generro Sanchez were both 18, both freshmen at East Central University in Oklahoma.

Murray knocked on Generro's dorm room door and asked for a ride to Walmart. He offered $20 for gas. Generro, who friends say always saw the good in everybody, said yes.

In the Walmart parking lot, Murray pulled out a stolen .40-caliber handgun and ordered Generro to drive north, out of town.

On a dark country road, he fired. The first shot missed. The second hit Generro in the head. The truck drifted off the road and crashed into a tree.

Hours later, a deputy spotted a young man walking alone on the highway at 3 a.m. and pulled his gun. Murray didn't run. He said: "I am the guy you're trying to find."

In the video below, he sits in the interrogation room in a suit and tie and explains, without a trace of emotion, how he picked his victim. Not someone he hated. Someone he thought nobody would miss.

When the detective asks if he feels any remorse, he says one word: "No."

When asked what should happen to him, he answers: "Death sentence, sir."

He never got one.

In 2015, a judge found Jerrod Murray not guilty by reason of insanity. He was sent to a state mental health facility instead of prison.

The district attorney said it plainly: "Nobody has been accountable for this crime."

Generro's mother said her son had dreams, and Jerrod crushed them.

Should "insanity" ever be a defense for a killer who planned his murder for weeks?

text:
The fall waterfowl migration is bringing large numbers of ducks into the wetlands of the central United States.

At Loess Bluffs National Wildlife Refuge in northwest Missouri, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service counted 83,440 ducks during its November 10 survey.

That's more than five times the 15,237 ducks recorded on October 20.

Northern pintails showed particularly strong numbers, increasing from 9,050 to 25,135 over the same period.

Green-winged teal, mallards and other dabbling ducks also contributed to the growing concentration.

Loess Bluffs sits along the Missouri River corridor, an important migration route for birds traveling between northern breeding grounds and southern wintering areas.

As temperatures fall and northern wetlands begin freezing, ducks move south in search of open water and food.

Managed wetlands provide places for migrating birds to rest and replenish their energy reserves before continuing their journey.

The refuge's survey also recorded 19,406 geese and 15 bald eagles.

But a large count at one refuge doesn't necessarily mean the overall duck population has increased.

Migration surveys measure how many birds are present at a particular place and time. Weather, water availability and migration timing can produce substantial changes from week to week.

For hunters farther north and west, those movements can offer useful information about how birds are progressing through the flyway.

The refuge itself is an important stopover, but the broader migration depends on a network of wetlands across the Plains.

Maintaining shallow-water habitat, food sources and resting areas helps birds complete journeys that can span thousands of miles.

The latest count offers a clear picture of just how quickly waterfowl concentrations can change during the fall migration.

Hosted at the Diné Event Center, the gathering recognized the courage, dedication, and sacrifices of those who have worn the uniform while celebrating the Nation’s longstanding tradition of military service.

Sharen Sandoval, Chief of Staff for the Office of the President, delivered remarks on behalf of President Buu Nygren. John James, Chief Executive Officer of Navajo Gaming, also delivered special remarks acknowledging the contributions of service members and NNGE employees who have served in the United States Armed Forces.

One of the event’s special features was the “Honoring Our Veterans” Wall, located in the resort’s rotunda. Attendees were invited to write the names of loved ones, family members, and community heroes on stickers and place them on a commemorative banner, creating a visual tribute of gratitude and remembrance.

Navajo Gaming also offered special commemorative coins to eligible military personnel as a gesture of appreciation, with opportunities to receive discounts at participating venues throughout the year.

The Office of the President extends its sincere appreciation to NNGE leadership, staff, and event organizers for bringing families and the community together in recognition of those who have answered the call to serve.

The gathering reflected the Nation’s enduring respect for its warriors and the legacy of honor, courage, and commitment they continue to carry forward for future generations.

Few fighter jet displays offer a backdrop quite like the Swiss Alps. 🇨🇭

At the 2023 Axalp Airshow, Swiss Air Force F/A-18 Hornets tear through a landscape of steep mountain ridges, deep valleys and alpine lakes, demonstrating the manoeuvrability of a frontline fighter in spectacular surroundings.

Flying in mountainous terrain demands careful control of speed, altitude and flight path. The surrounding peaks and rapidly changing terrain leave little room for error, making situational awareness and precise handling essential.

What makes Axalp particularly special is the setting. Unlike a conventional airshow over a flat airfield, spectators watch from elevated mountain slopes as the Hornets pass through the alpine landscape, bringing the aircraft remarkably close to the surrounding terrain.

It is a remarkable combination of military aviation, pilot skill and one of Europe's most spectacular natural backdrops.

text:
U.S. National Politics Update 2: A Democratic blue wave in the midterm elections has temporarily offset a projected decline in Black representation within the U.S. House of Representatives. According to an NPR analysis, the incoming Congress is set to include 60 Black House members, including nonvoting delegates, down from 63 in the current body. This figure remains just one away from the record loss of four Black representatives that occurred after the 1876 election.

The decline stems from a combination of factors, including high-level redistricting battles and standard political churn such as retirements. However, elevated Black voter turnout, particularly in the South, fueled Democratic victories that mitigated these losses. This dynamic was evident in Alabama, where Rep. Shomari Figures won reelection despite his district being redrawn by Republican state leaders to be more GOP-leaning following a Supreme Court ruling that weakened Voting Rights Act protections.

Advocates and experts warn that redistricting after the 2030 census continues to pose a threat to Black representation. The Supreme Court's decision in Louisiana v. Callais, released weeks before the midterms, allowed Alabama's legislature to redraw districts in a way that previously offered zero chance for Black-preferred candidates to win. While Figures' victory was attributed to remarkable turnout, experts caution that relying on such waves is not sustainable if voting rights are further diluted over time.

Redistricting changes also impacted Texas and Florida, where new maps undid some Black-represented districts. Conversely, Democrats flipped districts in North Carolina represented by incoming Black House Democrats Cyril Jefferson and LaKesha Womack. Additionally, Democratic socialist Reps.-elect Melat Kiros in Colorado and Donavan McKinney in Michigan are adding to the tally.

Beyond the House, Black representation in the Senate has reached a historic high of seven members. This includes Scott Colom, who is set to become the first Black senator from Mississippi since Reconstruction, and Juliana Stratton as Illinois Lt. Gov. While some politicians declare a generational shift, redistricting experts advise caution, noting that the full impact of recent Supreme Court decisions on state legislative maps may not be felt until 2028 or 2030.

text:
Sherrill Said NJ Would Be the Best Place to Do Business. Then Came 14,000 Layoffs.
https://t.co/E6ZMTazpiz via @YouTube 
At the New Jersey Chamber of Commerce Business Summit this spring, Governor Sherrill stood up and promised to make New Jersey the best place to do business in the world.  While she was saying it, companies were quietly filing the paperwork to leave.  Assemblyman Chris DePhillips breaks down what they’re not telling you.  The layoffs: In 2026 alone, New Jersey employers have filed warn notices — the forms required before any mass layoff of 50 or more workers — accounting for more than 14,000 lost jobs. Samsung. Bristol Myers Squibb, three rounds. Novartis, four rounds. Verizon. AT&T. JP Morgan Chase. Johnson & Johnson. Round after round, notice after notice.  The departures: In 2018, New Jersey was home to 22 Fortune 500 companies. Today it’s 15. Samsung moved its entire U.S. headquarters to Texas. ExxonMobil — 140 years of New Jersey history — went to Texas too. JetBlue closed up in Newark and expanded in Florida. Burlington Coat Factory, born here in 1972, moved to Philadelphia after Pennsylvania put up $30 million and offered a corporate tax rate headed to 4.99%. Mars Wrigley. HelloFresh. Hertz. Mercedes-Benz. Honeywell. Gone.  The reason: New Jersey has the highest corporate tax rate in the country — 11.5%. The Tax Foundation ranks New Jersey dead last in its state business tax climate index. A recent NJBIA survey found 59% of New Jersey businesses have no plans to expand here, 26% said they’d expand in another state instead, and 77% said business affordability has gotten worse over the last five years.  The head of the New Jersey Business and Industry Association called it the result of decades of anti-business policies. Governor Sherrill’s office declined to comment on Samsung’s departure.  The plan Democrats don’t have: The Assembly Commerce Committee held a hearing. Business leaders came in and told lawmakers the truth. When Republicans asked Democrats for a plan, they had no answers.  DePhillips has introduced legislation to cut New Jersey’s corporate tax rate from 11.5% to 2.5% — incrementally and responsibly. Assembly Republicans have pushed for a special budget committee hearing with business leaders whose companies have downsized or left. The majority hasn’t moved on either.  The governor says she wants New Jersey to be the best place to do business in the world. So does the Assembly Republican Conference. It’s time to act like it.

text: (For those who are pondering a similar move, please be advised that if it is sacred in Massachusetts it is probably illegal in Florida. For example, in MA the sacred principle is that public school kids shouldn't be tracked into gifted programs. Everyone is kept on grade level until 8th grade or high school. In FL, if a county-run school system wanted to do this it would violate a state law. Every FL public school must test and identify above-average students and offer them ability-appropriate gifted education starting in 2nd grade. For example, a child who is loafing in 3rd grade in MA because he or she has already mastered 3rd grade math might be challenged with 4th or 5th grade math in a Palm Beach County public school's 3rd grade.)
